chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the letters and their corresponding sounds for effective communication, b) pronounce words with the target sounds accurately for effective communication, c) use words related to greetings in everyday conversations, d) realize the importance of greetings in diverse contexts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an oral text with words containing the sounds corresponding to the letters a-h,  take turns to pronounce sounds /a:/ /æ/ (cat), / ɜː/( bird) , / ɑː/ (car) /ə/ (about) b: /b/c: /k/, /s/ d: /d/e: /e/ (bed), /iː/ (peel) /f:/ /f/ g: /g/ h:/ /h/, as modelled by peers, the teacher or an audio recording,  match sounds to corresponding letters  talk about pictures/photos of people greeting one another,  watch videos of people greeting each other,  use non-verbal cues such as eye KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we greet people? 2. How do we greet people at different times of the day?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Pre- reading Letter - sound Knowledge
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Pre- reading Letter - sound Knowledge (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify an appropriate posture for reading preparedness, b) read words containing the target letters correctly, c) realize the importance of correct posture in preparation for reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  select the appropriate sitting position from pictures, videos and teacher’s demonstration,  position self and reading materials appropriately,  turn pages of a book from right to left for easy reading,  track print through finger reading  pick out words with letters (a-h) from flash cards or charts,  match target letters with the sounds they represent,  read 2-3 letter words containing the target sounds KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we sit while reading? 2. How do we position our books while reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’ (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ in sentences, b) use the present tense realisations of the verb ‘to be’ to greet and introduce oneself and others, c) acknowledge the various present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ in day- to-day communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  participate in language games and songs using the present tense form of the verb ‘to be’,  watch videos of children greeting one another and introducing themselves,  observe as peers introduce themselves using the verb ‘to be,’  introduce himself/herself politely using the verb ‘to be’  describe himself/herself, and other people using the verb ‘to be’  practise various types of greetings using appropriate language e.g., how are you? I am fine,  role play various types of greetings using the verb ‘to be’. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we introduce ourselves? 2. How do we greet people in the morning/afternoon/ evening?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.1 Pre- writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.1 Pre- writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise appropriate sitting posture in preparation for writing, b) exhibit appropriate eye- hand coordination in preparation for writing, c) realize the role of correct posture and positioning of materials in writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at pictures, watch videos on appropriate sitting posture,  practise sitting in the right posture in pairs or small group,  position the exercise book correctly,  hold pencils/ colouring materials correctly,  practise writing from the left to the right,  join dotted lines to make letters and patterns,  draw and colour different shapes and letters,  draw patterns and shapes, trace letters and shapes, mould letters using plasticine or clay. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to sit properly when writing? 2. How do we place our books when writing?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words featuring the target sounds for effective communication, b) articulate the target sounds correctly for effective communication, c) make sentences using words related to the theme, d) realise the role of listening in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify the target sounds from short passages: o i: /iː/ (feet), /ɪ / (fit) /aɪ/ (price) o j: /ʤ/ (just) o k: /k/ o l: /l/ o m: /m/ o n: /n/ o o: for example / ɒ/ (lot), /ɔː/ (cot) o p: /p/  take pictures of items during a nature walk around the school and name them,  use a Frayer model to discuss the meaning of words related to the theme,  construct sentences using words KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which words do we use to talk about school? 2. How can we listen attentively to others?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Pre- reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Pre- reading (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify small and capital letters of the alphabet for reading preparedness, b) demonstrate appropriate posture in preparation for reading, c) realize the importance of positioning materials appropriately for reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out small letters with their corresponding capital letters from flash cards or charts,  match small and capital letters of the alphabet,  identify reading materials that are correctly positioned,  focus eyes on a line or word,  track print through finger pointing as the teacher reads letters I to P,  observe each other’s sitting posture and give feedback,  demonstrate and practise positioning reading materials appropriately,  practise turning over the pages of a book from left to right. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do people sit when reading? 2. How do people place books and newspapers while reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Subject-verb agreement
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Subject-verb agreement (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the correct use of subject-verb agreement in statements and questions, b) construct simple sentences related to the theme with correct subject-verb agreement for effective communication, c) acknowledge the importance of subject- verb agreement for fluency. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a story and identify sentences with subject-verb agreement,  ask each other questions using the target language pattern,  engage in a dialogue using singular and plural items (I, she/he, they)  construct sentences about pictures showing singular and plural forms,  construct sentences about actions demonstrated by peers,  recite poems featuring singular and plural forms. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you talk about a person, an object or a place? 2. How do we talk about many people?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4.1 Pre-writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.1 Pre-writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify appropriate sitting posture in preparation for writing, b) demonstrate appropriate eye hand co-ordination in preparation for writing, c) realize the importance of positioning oneself and writing materials appropriately in preparation for writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at each other’s sitting posture and identify the correct posture for writing,  work collaboratively with peers to demonstrate and practise the correct body posture for writing,  identify writing materials that are correctly positioned,  demonstrate and practise positioning writing materials appropriately,  practise writing from the left to the right,  draw and colour different shapes,  role play how to use their exercise books well. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we sit when writing? 2. How do we write?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand the learner should be able to: a) link the target letters of the alphabet with their sound appropriately. b) use words related to the theme correctly in oral communication, c) respond to verbally and non-verbally to simple one directional instructions, d) realize the role of correct pronunciation in conversations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen and point out the sounds of the letters: q, r, s, t, u,v,w,x, y, z as modelled by the teacher,  say the sounds of the letters as the teacher points at them,  watch a video/ listen to a story related to the theme,  talk about family members,  role play responding to simple instructions using appropriate eye contact and facial expressions,  use dialogues/rhymes/tongue twisters/ language games/ songs to practise vocabulary related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce words correctly? 2. How can we listen attentively during conversation?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Pre-reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Pre-reading (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) name the target letters in preparation for reading , b) read the sounds corresponding to the target letters fluently, c) advocate for the importance of letter –sound correspondence in preparation for reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  name the letters q, r, s, t, u,v,w,x, y, z and practise saying their corresponding sounds,  articulate the target sounds and write the corresponding letter, in pairs.  model letter shapes for the target letters.  track print through finger pointing as the teacher reads,  match and pair sound with their corresponding letters, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we learn sounds?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Pronouns (‘I, you’) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct use of the pronouns “I”, and “you” in short sentences and other texts, b) use the pronouns “I, and “you” correctly in short sentences and other texts, c) value the role of pronoun “I”, and “you” correctly in day- to- day communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  watch a video of family members talking to each other using pronouns “I”, and “you”,,  listen to the teacher’s instructions or an audio recording of a dialogue, songs or stories using pronouns “I”, and “you”,  use pronouns “I”, and “you” in a conversation related to the theme,  talk to peers/oneself using the pronouns ‘you’/“1” ,  role play and record conversations between family members using the pronouns “I”, and “you”  answer questions related to the language structure. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Which words do you use to talk about yourself?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct formation of lower case letters of the alphabet, b) form lower case letters correctly, c) write from left to right correctly, d) adopt forming letter correctly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  practise correct letter formation from models on the board, chart, pattern books,  Copy lower case letter patterns,  draw and label objects related to the theme,  practise writing lower case letters from left to right. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we need to write in good handwriting?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise target sounds in the given words, b) pronounce the target sounds for clarity in communication, c) respond to simple specific one- directional instructions using the new words, d) adopt using the vocabulary learnt in oral communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to the teacher or an audio modelling of the sounds /æ/ /m/, /t/ /e/, and mimic pronunciation of the target sounds  form words featuring the target sounds,  use the vocabulary related to the theme to construct sentences,  respond to instructions given by the teacher,  role play giving each other one-directional instructions, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we listen attentively? 2. Why should we pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.1 Pre- reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Pre- reading (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) identify target letters in given words, b) form words using the target letters in preparation for reading, c) realise the importance of letters in word formation. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to audio recordings of the target letters (A a; M m; Tt; Ee),  point out and name letters on a chart or flashcards,  listen and sort the target letters in word games,  practise using target letters in forming words,  match and pair the target letters with their corresponding sounds with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we learn letters?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 Singular and plurals (add -s and -es)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Singular and plurals (add -s and -es) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify singular and plural nouns which require addition of -s and -es. b) use singular and plural nouns which require an addition of -s and -es, c) realise the importance of using singular and plural nouns for effective oral communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  talk about objects at home in their singular and plural forms,  learners group pictures of items found at home in columns of one and many with peers,  draw and colour pictures of objects found at home and indicate number  recite and record poems containing singular and plural nouns with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What objects are found at home?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 4.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct letter formation of target letters. b) form letters in terms of shape and size correctly, c) write from left to right to communicate effectively, d) realize the importance of correct letter formation for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  copy capital and small letter patterns for target letters: Aa, Mm, Tt, Ee,  practise correct letter formation of target letters from models on the board/chart/pattern books,  practise writing 3-4 letter words from left to right with peers,  watch videos on formation of target letters. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we need to write clearly and neatly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify new words featuring the target sounds in sentences, b) use new words related to the theme in sentences, c) use facial expressions appropriately during conversations d) appreciate the use of facial expression in communication SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to modelling of the target sounds (Ss, Ll, Ii, Pp) and mimick,  look at pictures and watch videos depicting different times of the day,  role play activities done at different times of the day using words related to the theme, with peers  sing songs about time,  watch videos of people taking part in a conversation about time,  interpret different facial expressions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to look at the person talking to us? 2. Which words do we use to talk about time?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Pre- reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Pre- reading (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify letter names and corresponding sounds for reading preparedness, b) read simple 3-4 letter words featuring the target letters for effective reading, c) realize the importance of letter- sound correspondence for reading preparedness. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  engage in letter matching activities using pocket charts/digital flash cards/ charts/flash cards,  recognise letters of the alphabet: (Ss, Ll, Ii, Pp),  match target letters to their corresponding sounds,  play a fishing game by identifying specific sounds with peers,  read simple 3-4 letter words made up of the target letters and letters learnt previously,  read sight words encountered in a story. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we learn sounds?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Present Simple Tense (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words in the present simple tense in given sentences, b) use present tense forms to talk about time, c) apply present tense forms to sequence routine or daily activities. a) adopt the use of present simple tense to talk about routine activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video on children participating in routine activities and talk about the activities using present simple tense,  respond to questions based on daily routines,  report what he or she does at home,  respond to simple questions demonstrating the use of present tense in talking about routine activities,  repeat sentences containing present tense from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do you do from morning to evening?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 5.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) form letters in terms of shape and size correctly, b) write words from left to right to communicate effectively, c) realise the need to form letters correctly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  copy letters (Ss, Ll, Ii, Pp) as modelled by the teacher or peers,  practise correct letter formation from models on the board/ charts/pattern books,  draw and label objects related to theme,  practise writing letters and words from left to right,  play language games involving the shaping of letters,  sort out small letters and capital letters and write them separately. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to write clearly and neatly? 2. How can we tell letters are correctly written?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words featuring the target sounds from an oral text, b) pronounce words with the target sounds for reading preparedness, c) responding to simple specific one- directional instructions using new words, d) realize the importance of correct pronunciation in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an audio text containing the target sounds: /f/, /n/ /h/ / ɒ/ and / ɔː/ and identify words with the target sounds  say the target sounds as modeled by peers/ teacher / audio recording,  use a Frayer model to discuss the meaning of words related to the theme,  recite rhymes/sing songs about weather  listen to a story related the theme and discuss the story using the new words,  role play responding to KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to pronounce words correctly? 2. What should we do when someone is talking to us?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.1 Word Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1 Word Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, b) pronounce words with the target sounds accurately, c) realise the importance of reading words accurately. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner be guided to:  point out words with the sounds: /f/, /n/ /h/ /ɒ/ and / / ɔː/,  select words with the target sounds from a chart,  read words including words with target letters sounds,  read words about weather and the environment with minimal hesitations,  practise reading sentences containing decodable words. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3. 1 Present continuous tense
chunks.text: STRAND: 6. 3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 6.3. 1 Present continuous tense. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify ongoing activities in and out of school b) use the present continuous tense to describe on-going activities related to weather and the environment, c) adopt communicating ideas using the present continuous tense. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  name the activities going on in the school compound,  recite poems/sing songs featuring the present continuous tense,  answer questions about ongoing activities related to the theme, in pairs or groups,  listen to a story with present continuous tense,  retell portions of a short story in the present continuous tense, for example, ‘the hare was going…,  role play events with peers using the present continuous tense. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is going on in the school compound?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.4.1 Spelling
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 6.4.1 Spelling (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words featuring the target letters in written texts, b) spell 3-5 letter words featuring the target letters for writing fluency, c) realise the need for correct spelling in written communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify words featuring the target capital and small letters: Ff, Hh, Nn, Oo,  sit appropriately when writing down words related to the theme from a dictation,  practise holding pencils/ colouring materials correctly,  listen to an audio recording and write down target words,  copy a list of sentences featuring the target words,  create a poster featuring the target words with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we spell words correctly? 2. What makes one’s handwriting readable?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in an oral text, b) pronounce words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, c) use new words related to the theme in a variety of contexts, d) realise the importance of listening attentively. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an audio recording/clip about hygiene  Pick out words which have the sounds /b/, /r/, /u/ and /g/  recite alliterative words that have the target sounds as modeled by the peers/ teacher or audio record/clip  look at pictures from a story, and say the meaning of words related to the theme,  practise matching vocabulary learnt to pictures and objects,  recite rhymes and sing songs, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to pronounce words correctly? 2. How do we learn to speak?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.2.1 Word Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1 Word Reading (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds and letters for reading competence , b) read non-decodable words featuring the target sounds for reading competence, c) realize the importance of word reading for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify the sounds corresponding to the letters, Bb, Rr, Uu, Gg,  identify and read non- decodable words with the sounds /b/, /r/ /u/ and /g/,  listen to an audio recording containing non decodable words,  practise reading non-decodable words on a word wall with peers and give feedback,  read words related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3.1 Simple past tense (adding -ed/- d)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Simple past tense (adding -ed/- d) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with - ed/ and -d from a written text, b) use simple past tense to discuss activities they carried out in the past, c) adopt communicating ideas using the simple past tense. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner guided to:  identify sentences with simple past tense from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to,  respond to simple questions related to the theme using the simple past,  engage in games, changing verbs from present simple to past simple tense, in small groups/ pairs,  construct oral sentences using simple past tense ending with -ed, -d, to talk about hygiene, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What did you do in the morning before coming to school? 2. What did your family do last Saturday to keep the home clean?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4.1 Spelling
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 7.4.1 Spelling (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words featuring the target letters in written texts, b) form the target letters correctly in terms of shape and size for effective communication, c) write 3-5 letter words featuring the target sounds correctly for effective communication , d) realise the importance of writing words correctly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out words related to the target letters,  practise correct letter formation from models drawn on the board, chart or pattern books,  differentiate neat handwriting from untidy ones, with peers,  practise writing letters Bb, Rr, Uu, Gg neatly from the left to the right,  draw and label objects. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should people write neatly? 2. How can we spell words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the target sounds from an audio text, b) pronounce words with the target sounds correctly for communication clarity, c) use new words related to the theme in relevant contexts, d) realise the importance of using words appropriately in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an audio recording of words featuring the target sounds(/k/, /d/ and /w/) or words modelled by the peers or teacher,  pronounce the sounds by taking turns ,  match vocabulary learnt to pictures and objects,  recite poems featuring the target sounds  construct sentences using vocabulary related to the theme,  recite rhymes and sing songs related to the theme with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you do when someone is talking to you? 2. What is likely to happen if you pronounce a word wrongly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 8.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, b) read a grade- appropriate text at the right speed and with minimal hesitations, c) display the right feelings or emotions when reading a text, d) realise the importance of reading fluency for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  point out words with the sounds /k/, /d/ and /w/,  read 3-4 letter words including words with letters ‘c, d, w’ in a text,  engage in timed reading (30 words per minute),  practice reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words, with peers,  participate in a readers theatre where he or she reads some lines or stanzas of a poem  display the right facial expressions and tone when reading,  read a text with minimal hesitations. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to read at the right speed? 2. Why should we display the right feelings and expressions when reading a text?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.3.1 Demonstratives
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Demonstratives (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify singular and plural nouns from a text, b) use demonstratives to talk about the theme, c) realise the importance of well-formed sentences in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  use demonstratives in singular and plural to talk about objects identified,  point at parts of the body and describe them using the words: (this/ that), (these/those) in pairs or small groups,  use demonstratives to talk about near or far objects,  recite a poem featuring the new words with peers,  sing songs or recite rhymes about parts of the body. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we tell others about near and far objects?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.4.1 Spelling
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 8.4.1 Spelling (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letters in a written text, b) spell words with the target letters correctly for writing fluency, c) write words related to the theme legibly and neatly, d) realise the importance of correct spelling in written communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  name the letters that make words with the target sounds,  select words with the letters c’, ‘d’ and ‘w’,  spell the words with the letters ‘c’, ‘d’ and ‘w’,  make words related to parts of the body from jumbled letters,  write the words read aloud to them,  copy words legibly and correctly,  form words with peers using the letters of their names. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we spell words correctly? 2. How can we write legibly and neatly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds from written texts, b) pronounce words with the target sounds correctly, , c) use the vocabulary related to the theme in oral sentences, d) realize the role of vocabulary in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  say the target sounds: /k/, /j/, /l/ and /s/ as modelled by peers, teacher or audio recording,  recite rhyming words featuring the target sounds,  use words with the target sounds to talk about their friends,  listen to an audio recording on friendship,  use vocabulary related to the theme in dialogues,  role play events related to the theme,  Sing songs related to friends. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. How can we improve our pronunciation?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 9.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, b) read a grade- appropriate text accurately, at the right speed and with minimal hesitations, c) display the appropriate feelings or emotions when reading a text, d) realize the importance of reading fluency in effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The leaner should be guided to:  identify words with the sounds /k/, /j/ and /l/,  select words with the target sounds from a chart,  engage in timed reading with peers (30 words per minute),  display the right facial expressions when reading,  pause appropriately and avoid hesitations while reading,  recite poems relevant to the theme,  participate in a readers’ theatre where he or she reads some lines or stanzas of a poem. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. How does correct pronunciation help us in reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.3.1 Common and proper nouns
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Common and proper nouns (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise common and proper nouns from texts, b) use common and proper nouns to talk about the theme, c) adopt using of common and proper nouns in everyday communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  single out common and proper nouns from a text,  name items in the classroom,  talk about their friends using common and proper nouns,  talk about what their friends like using common and proper nouns,  fill in blank spaces using common and proper nouns. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1) Why is it important to refer to people and places by their names? 2) What things can you see in the classroom?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and the full stop)
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 9.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and the full stop) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: - a) identify capital letters, small letters and the full stop in a text, b) use capital and small letters correctly for names and proper nouns in writing, c) realize the use of capital letters, small letters and the full stop in writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  observe a display of correctly written text containing capital and small letters,  point out capital letters, small letters and the full stop in a text,  use capital and small letters correctly when writing proper nouns,  practise writing their names/names of their friends starting with capital letters. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1) Why do we use the full stop? 2) When do we use capital letters?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 10.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds for oral fluency, b) pronounce the words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, c) use new words correctly in oral communication, d) realise the importance of varied vocabulary in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to the target sounds as modelled by peers, teacher or audio recording,  say words with the vowel sounds and diphthongs: o / æ/ as in heart o / ɔː /as in thought o /i:/ as in feet o /u:/ as in pool o / ɔɪ / as in boy o / eɪ / as in day  play word family games containing the target sounds,  use picture clues to explain the meaning of new words related KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What happens if we don’t listen to instructions carefully? 2. How can we ensure we are safe when doing activities at home or at school?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 10.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, b) read a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression for fluency, c) realize the importance of reading accurately, at the right speed and with expression in lifelong SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify and read words with the target sounds( a:/, /o:/, /i:/, /u:/, /oi/ and /ei/),  track print through finger pointing observing punctuation as the teacher reads,  engage in timed reading (30 words per minute) displaying the correct expressions and observing punctuations,  practice reading sentences containing decodable and non- decodable words with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you like reading? 2. How can you show that you are observing correct punctuations?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.3.1 Simple prepositions (in, on, under, between, behind, in front, inside, outside)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 10.3.1 Simple prepositions (in, on, under, between, behind, in front, inside, outside) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct placement of targeted prepositions to show positional relationship, b) use prepositions in relevant contexts, c) realise the use of prepositions for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss where different objects are found at home  describe positions of various items as displayed in the classroom,  engage in a hide and seek game in small groups to locate their peers,  play a digital games based on prepositions,  construct sentences featuring target prepositions in a story, poem or conversation,  role play situations related to the theme involving use of target prepositions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Where do we keep different items in the classroom? 2. Where do we keep different items at home?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and question marks)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 10.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and question marks) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: - a) identify capital letters and question marks in a text, b) use capital and question marks in sentences correctly, c) acknowledge the use of capital letters and question marks in writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  Show capital letters and question marks in a written text,  punctuate sentences using capital letters and question marks, in pairs/small groups,  use capital letters and question marks in sentences related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we use the question marks? 2. When do we use capital letters?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.1.1 Pronunciation And Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.1 Listening And Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 11.1.1 Pronunciation And Vocabulary. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target sounds in words from an oral text, b) articulate words correctly to discriminate the target sounds, c) use the vocabulary learnt in relevant contexts, d) advocate for appropriate pronunciation for clarity in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a print or digital text containing the target sounds: / ʃ/, /tʃ/, /θ/, /ð/,  practise sound discrimination using minimal pairs,  pick out the target vocabulary as used in short sentences/short paragraphs/teacher read-aloud stories  infer the meaning of new words from stories, dialogues, and role plays,  construct simple sentences using new words learnt, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we use sounds to make new words? 2. How do we learn to pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 11.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds correctly, b) read sentences in a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression for effective communication, c) realize the importance of fluency in reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to short paragraphs containing words with the target sounds: / ʃ/, /tʃ/, /θ/, /ð/  read words with the target sounds adhering to the correct pronunciation,  watch videos on reading fluently,  read simple sentences in the story aloud paying attention to the punctuation,  take part in timed-reading competitions.  recite poems/ rhymes related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Which words have the target sounds?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 11.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story related to the theme in preparation for reading, b) answer direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension, c) adopt reading pictures and texts for enjoyment and information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  discuss the pictures and the title, and make predictions,  read words with the target sounds in a text of about 60 words,  take turns to read simple sentences in the story aloud, paying attention to the punctuation,  answer comprehension questions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do the pictures and the title tell us about the story? 2. Which words have the target sounds?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.3.1 Adjectives
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 11.3.1 Adjectives (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify adjectives used to describe objects and people, b) use base forms of one and two- syllable adjectives in relevant contexts, c) appreciate the use of adjectives for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  name objects in the classroom and attach appropriate adjectives to them,  talk about objects in a picture/photograph/video clip by using correct adjectives,  engage in language games containing base forms of one and two- syllable adjectives,  sing songs/rhymes, recite poems that use adjectives. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we talk about people, things or places?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.4.1 Guided Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 11.4.1 Guided Writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify ideas depicted in different pictures related to the theme in preparation for writing, b) use 4-6 letter words to fill in gaps in sentences correctly, c) appreciate the importance of writing correctly in communication, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  talk about what they have seen in pictures with peers,  engage in spelling games with words related to the theme and picture prompts in preparation for writing,  create sentences from pictures, with peers,  match pictures and sentences,  fill in gaps in sentences, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do pictures help us to write?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target sounds in words for effective communication, b) articulate words correctly to discriminate the target sounds, c) use the vocabulary learnt in relevant contexts, d) realize the importance of proper pronunciation in oral communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to an audio recording/ read aloud passage and identify words with the sounds: /e /, / iː/, / eə /,  practise sound discrimination using minimal pairs,  recite poems/ rhymes/ tongue twisters using words with the target sounds observing turn taking rules,  pick out the new words as used in short sentences/short paragraphs/teacher read- aloud stories,  practise pronouncing words in response to picture cues,  construct simple sentences using new words, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How would you know if someone is listening to you? 2. How do we learn to pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 12.2.1 Fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in a text, b) read sentences in a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression for effective communication c) realize the importance of fluency in reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to short paragraphs and point out words with the target sounds: /e /, / iː/, /ea/,/iː/ ,  read words with the target sounds correctly,  read simple sentences in a story aloud paying attention to the punctuation,  take part in timed-reading of a text of about displaying the right expressions,  recite poems/ rhymes related to the theme with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we read fluently?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.2.1 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 12.2.1 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story related to the theme based on the title and picture, b) read words that have the target sounds in a text related to the theme, c) respond to direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension, d) adopt reading pictures and texts for enjoyment and information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  make predictions of what will happen after discussing the title and pictures in the text,  read a story and identify words that have the sounds: /e /, /iː/, / eə /,/ with their meaning,  talk about their own experiences in relation to the story, with peers,  respond to direct and indirect questions from a text in print or digital device, using contextual clues,  role play, with peers the events from a story. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you think will happen in this story? 2. How can you tell that someone has understood a story? 3. What makes a story interesting?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.3.1 Use of possessives (my, our, her, his, their, its)
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 12.3.1 Use of possessives (my, our, her, his, their, its) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise possessives from a written text, b) use possessives to talk about ownership in relation to the theme, c) adopt the use of possessives to show ownership in oral communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify objects in the classroom and attach appropriate possessives to each,  ask questions whose responses will include possessives such as: (my pen, his book) with peers,  engage in a role play to show ownership of various items.  pick out possessives from a text,  use possessives in phrases and sentences to illustrate ownership. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which words do we use to show ownership? 2. Why is it important to use possessives correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.4.1 Guided Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 12.4.1 Guided Writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct words to fill in gaps to complete sentences, b) fill in gaps in simple sentences for effective communication, c) realise the importance of writing complete sentences to express meaning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work with peers to match pictures with words,  pick out correct words that can be used to fill in gaps in sentences appropriately,  use the words provided to fill in gaps correctly and meaningfully in given sentences,  write short sentences using prompts. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to write clearly and legibly? 2. What should you consider when selecting words to fill in gaps?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify targets sounds in words from an oral text , b) articulate words with the target sounds accurately to discriminate the sounds, c) use the vocabulary leant in relevant context, d) adopt using the vocabulary learnt to communicate effectively in various contexts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a print or digital text containing the target sounds: /ʊ/ and / eɪ / (pay, wait)  practise sound discrimination using minimal with peers,  pick out the target vocabulary as used in short sentences/short paragraphs/teacher read-aloud stories  infer the meaning of new words from stories, dialogues, and role plays,  construct simple sentences using new words learnt,  practise pronouncing words in response to picture cues and record themselves, recite poems/ rhymes/ tongue twisters using words with the target sounds. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 13.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) use the title and the pictures to make predictions about a story, b) use context clues to infer the meanings of new words, c) answer direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension, d) recommend reading for enjoyment and information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  talk about the title and pictures of a story with peers,  make predictions of where the action could be happening,  read a text ( about 60 words) aloud with peers,  infer the meanings of words using contextual clues,  answer comprehension questions related to the theme, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you see in the pictures? 2. Where do you think the events in story are happening?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.3.1 Yes/ No questions (with can, may, will)
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 13.3.1 Yes/ No questions (with can, may, will) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify Yes/No questions, with can, may and will from a text, b) respond to Yes/No questions using can, may and will, for clarity in communication, c) realise the use of can, may and will to seek information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  use songs/short poems to practice the use of Yes/No questions with can, may and will,  point out questions which require a YES/NO response from a written text,  ask and answer Yes/No questions related to the theme using can, may and will,  restate sentence structures containing Yes/No questions from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to,  role play activities that will elicit use of can, may and will. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you ask your friends for help?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.4.1 Guided Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 13.4.1 Guided Writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct form of words to be used in writing simple sentences, b) rearrange words to form simple sentences for fluency in writing, c) realise the importance of writing correct and meaningful sentences to express meaning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  write the correct words with the target sounds from a dictation,  play a sentence- building drill game using the correct form of words,  match pictures with the correct sentences,  rearrange jumbled words to form simple sentences,  individually form simple sentences related to the theme (3-5 sentences) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What makes a sentence correct?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target sounds used in words for effective communication, b) articulate the words with the target sounds in oral communication, c) use the vocabulary for oral communication in relevant contexts, d) advocate for appropriate use of correct pronunciation in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a variety of words, songs, poems and stories with the sounds: /dʒ/ , /s/ , /ŋ/  practise pronouncing the target sounds in mouth- position models demonstrated by the teacher or a video clip,  practise pronouncing words in response to picture cues with peers,  use the vocabulary learnt to construct simple sentences.  sing songs/chants using words related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce words correctly? 2. Why is it important to learn new words?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 14.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds in preparation for reading, b) read sentences in a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression for fluency, c) realise the role of fluency in reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify and read words with the sounds/dʒ/ , /s/ , /ŋ/ from a text,  practise reading a text containing words with the target letters sounds adhering to the correct pronunciation,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non- decodable words,  engage in timed reading (30 words per minute), displaying the right facial expressions and tone,  participate in a readers theatre where he or she reads some lines or stanzas of a poem. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What makes it easy to read fluently?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 14.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story based on the title and picture, b) read words that have the target sounds in a text related to the theme, c) respond to direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension, d) adopt reading pictures and texts for enjoyment and information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss the title and pictures in the text and make predictions of what will happen,  read a story and identify words that have the sounds /dʒ/, /s/, /ŋ/,  read simple stories or passages aloud,  talk about their own experiences in relation to the story, with peers,  respond to direct and indirect questions from a print or non print text using contextual clues,  role play, with peers, the events from a story read. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we tell that someone has understood a story? 2. What helps us to understand a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.3.1 Adverbs of Place
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 14.3.1 Adverbs of Place (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the adverbs of place in sentences to show awareness, b) use adverbs of place to describe the position of objects and people for effective communication, c) realize the importance of proper use of adverbs of place to describe the position of objects and people in the environment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify different positions of things in the classroom,  point out the adverbs of place in sentences,  practise using adverbs of place to construct sentences describing objects in the classroom,  sing songs ,role play and recite poems related to the theme with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Where do you find different things in the classroom? 2. Why is it important to place things in the right place?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.4.1 Guided Writing ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 14.4.1 Guided Writing ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words related to the theme in simple sentences, b) write simple meaningful sentences as guided for effective communication, c) realise the importance of writing for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify the target vocabulary in sentences,  write simple meaningful sentences( not more than 5 words),  practise writing sentences from a substitution table,  fill in gaps to complete sentences,  form simple meaningful sentences in relation to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to write meaningful sentences? 2. What makes it easy to write clear sentences?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.1.1 Pronunciat ion and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 15.1.1 Pronunciat ion and vocabulary (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the target sounds in an oral text, b) articulate words with the target sounds correctly to discriminate sounds, c) use the vocabulary learnt in relevant contexts. d) realize the role of vocabulary in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to and pronounce words with the target sounds: /l/, / s/, /r/ as modeled by the teacher or audio recording,  practise sound discrimination using minimal pairs,  use the vocabulary relevant to the theme in short sentences,  play language games to practise new words,  recite rhymes, sing songs and say tongue twisters with the target sounds with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the words that we can make from the sound given?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 15.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target sounds accurately, b) read sentences in a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression for effective communication, c) realise the importance of fluency in reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify words with the sounds /l/, / s/, /r/ from a text,  read a text containing words with the target letters sounds adhering to the correct pronunciation,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non- decodable words, in small groups,  engage in timed reading (30 words per minute) displaying the right facial expressions and tone.  participate in a readers theatre where he or she reads some lines or stanzas of a poem. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why are punctuation marks important in reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.2.2 Comprehension ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 15.2.2 Comprehension ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words that have the target sounds in a text related to the theme, b) make predictions about a story using the title and the pictures, c) respond to direct and indirect questions from a text to show comprehension, d) adopt reading pictures and texts for enjoyment and information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  read simple sentences aloud while paying attention to new words and correct pronunciation of words with sounds :/l/, /r/, /s/,  discuss the title and the pictures of the story to make predictions,  read a text (of about 60 words) aloud,  infer the meanings of new words using contextual clues,  answer direct and indirect questions using contextual clues,  draw pictures to show what is happening in the story,  read a text or view pictures for enjoyment and information. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do the pictures tell us about the story? 2. What does the title tell us about the story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.3.1 Interjections of surprise ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 15.3.1 Interjections of surprise ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify interjections of surprise in a variety of texts, b) use interjections of surprise in simple sentences related to the theme, c) adopt the use of interjections of surprise in day today communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a short dialogue from an audio recording containing interjections of surprise,  repeat sentence structures containing interjections of surprise from a story, poem or conversation they have listened to,  respond appropriately to interjections of surprise as modelled,  use digital devices to search for emojis showing surprise,  practise making different familiar faces showing surprise with peers,  construct sentences using interjections of surprise,  recite rhymes and poem related to the theme using interjections of surprise. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can you tell that someone is surprised? 2. What are the things that can make someone surprised?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.4.1 Guided Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 15.4.1 Guided Writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct order of word in sentences, b) write sentences of not more than five words related to the theme, c) realize the importance of writing correct and meaningful sentences to express meaning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify the target vocabulary in sentences,  match pictures with the correct sentences  write meaningful sentences ( not more than 5 words),  fill in gaps to complete sentences,  form simple meaningful sentences in relation to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why are words important in writing?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.strand: Ability to compose a simple paragraphs
chunks.sub_strand: Composes paragraphs of 5 to 6 sentences
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to compose a simple paragraphs. SUB-STRAND: Composes paragraphs of 5 to 6 sentences. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Composes paragraphs of 3-4 complete sentences SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Composes paragraphs of 1 or 2 complete sentences KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Writes some words but unable to construct coherent sentences

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: Uses full stops, question marks and exclamation mark correctly
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to punctuate sentences appropriately. SUB-STRAND: Uses full stops, question marks and exclamation mark correctly. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Uses full stops, question marks and exclamation mark in most sentences correctly SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Frequent reminders are needed to use full stops, question marks and exclamation mark in most sentences KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1, 2 or the 3 terminal punctuation marks are missing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.strand: Ability to use legible and neat handwriting
chunks.sub_strand: Shapes, forms and spaces all letters correctly
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to use legible and neat handwriting. SUB-STRAND: Shapes, forms and spaces all letters correctly. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Shapes, forms and spaces most letters correctly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Letters difficult to read A few reversals and irregular spaced words KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Letters difficult to read Numerous reversals and irregularly spaced words. chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Myself and neighbours Role of neighbours
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Myself and neighbours Role of neighbours. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) mention positive experiences with their neighbours for safety, b) illustrate the qualities of a good neighbour for self- efficacy, c) appreciate the qualities of a good neighbour for harmonious coexistence. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen/watch short stories highlighting the roles of a neighbour,  give the names of their immediate neighbours and mention what they like about them,  Tell the class the activities their family does together with their neighbours,  Watch a video clip / listen to a resource person and discuss on qualities of a good neighbour,  Watch videos talking about having a safe neighbourhood,  Discuss cases of right and wrong behaviours towards their peers and in their neighbourhood, ● Ask their parents/ guardians to help them identify ways to relate with both their peers and adult neighbours. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are neighbours important in our life?

chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Panchmahabhoot Agni (Fire)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1. 0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Panchmahabhoot Agni (Fire). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) state Agni (fire) as a source of energy in creation as gift from Paramatma, b) employ safe forms of Agni for harmony with nature, c) appreciate the Sun (Surya) the source of Agni as fuel for life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  prepare a chart showing the ways Agni is used at home and in places of worship,  listen to a resource person/ watch a video clip describing Agni and the importance of Agni in life,  Visit places of worship to see the ways Agni is used in worship and present in class,  Practice safe and age-appropriate use of Agni at home/school, ● Research from parents the appropriate uses of various forms of Agni and present the findings in class, ● Assist peers with special needs to understand the advantages and how Agni could be harmful. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is Agni important in our lives?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Enlightened Beings - Shri Ram - Shri Krishna - Lord Mahavir - Lord Buddha -Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Manifestations of Paramatma. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Enlightened Beings - Shri Ram - Shri Krishna - Lord Mahavir - Lord Buddha -Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) list the main qualities of the Enlightened Beings for reverence, b) relate the Enlightened Beings with their contributions to the society for social cohesion, c) desire to emulate the qualities of the Enlightened Beings in their lives for inspiration. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● identify the selected Enlightened Beings using flash cards/pictures, ● use a digital device/parents input to research in groups on the qualities of the selected Enlightened Beings and present the findings in class, ● prepare a table to match the Enlightened beings with their contributions to the society, ● identify health related issues that children are facing and how contributions of Enlightened Beings are used to mitigate them, ● colour the images of the Enlightened Beings and create a portfolio, ● assist peers with special needs in painting and coloring images of Enlightened Beings. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does learning about Enlightened Beings influence your life?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Other names of Paramatma - Parvati Maa - Lakshmi Maa - Shri Ganesh - Sarswati Maa - Durga Maa -Shabad Guru
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Manifestations of Paramatma. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Other names of Paramatma - Parvati Maa - Lakshmi Maa - Shri Ganesh - Sarswati Maa - Durga Maa -Shabad Guru. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) list the names of the Devis/Devtas for familiarisation, b) identify the murtis of Devis/Devtas for self-efficacy, c) acknowledge the listed Devis/Devtas as manifestations of Paramatma for strengthening their faith. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● write down the names of Paramatma flashed on large cards in class, - Watch a prescribed video clip safely on the murtis of selected Devis/Devtas, ● match the murtis to the names of Paramatma on a table in groups, ● colour images of murtis and display in class, ● ask the parents to tell them the roles of the learnt Devis/Devtas and present the findings in class, ● roleplay on some events from the lives of Devis/Devtas, ● assist peers with special needs in painting and coloring images of Devis/Devtas. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are murtis important in worship?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1Basic Concepts -Ramayana -Bhagavad Gita
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Scriptures. SUB-STRAND: 3.1Basic Concepts -Ramayana -Bhagavad Gita. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) list basic concepts from each of the two Scriptures listed for memorisation, b) narrate stories on basic concepts from the two Scriptures for righteousness, c) appreciate the Scriptures as sources of inspiration for guidance in life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a discourse from a resource person on the basic concepts in Scriptures,  discuss in groups the basic concepts of the Scriptures Ramayana and Bhagavad Gita,  list the concepts of Ramayana and Bhagavad Gita and present to the class  make presentations depicting the inspiration they associate with the Ramayana and Bhagavad Gita.  visit places of worship to learn about the significance of the Ramayana and Bhagavad Gita from a resource person.  roleplay on short stories from Ramayana and Bhagwad Gita on annual function day.  assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the basic concepts from Ramayana and Bhagwad Gita in their class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the role of Scriptures in our daily living?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Handling of Scriptures - Ramayana - Bhagavad Gita
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Scriptures. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Handling of Scriptures - Ramayana - Bhagavad Gita. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) mention the key protocols in handling the Scriptures for self- drive, b) display the appropriate handling of Scriptures for reverence, c) acknowledge appropriate handling of all Scriptures for respect and veneration. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  ask parents/guardians/ a resource person to explain/demonstrate the protocols involved in handling the Scriptures at home and at places of worship,  watch/listen to a video clip on how the Scriptures are handled in different situations of use,  demonstrate in class the protocols on how Scriptures are handled using prototypes and observing cleanliness,  engage their parent/ guardian to take a video on practising how they can handle Scriptures appropriately in specific situations,  discuss in groups reasons for handling the Scripture appropriately, ● practice the recitation of hymns that are part of the protocols of handling Scriptures, ● Assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching recitation of hymns. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What makes the handling of scriptures different from other reading materials?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Moral Stories Ramayana and Bhagavad Gita
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Scriptures. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Moral Stories Ramayana and Bhagavad Gita. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify short stories on morals from Scriptures for character formation, b) narrate short stories on moral teachings from the listed Scriptures for ethical living, c) desire to embrace stories with morals from the Scriptures as sources of guidance and inspiration. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read selected age-appropriate short stories on morals from the Scriptures,  listen to short stories from the listed Scriptures on morals by a resource person /from digital devices,  retell the short stories they have either read or listened to from the scriptures,  narrate and point out the lessons they learn from the short stories,  role plays the stories to practise morals learnt from the listed Scriptures,  practice Sharing and caring in pairs to exchange appropriate items used in school in an ethical manner,  discuss the lessons they can draw from the moral stories relating to their daily life in the family and the community,  assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the lessons that can be drawn from the moral stories. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to learn about moral stories? 2. How are stories from Scriptures useful in character building?
