chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1 Protocols of Worship Gayatri Mantra - Navkar Mantra - Buddha Mantra (Namakkara) - Mool Mantar
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Worship. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Protocols of Worship Gayatri Mantra - Navkar Mantra - Buddha Mantra (Namakkara) - Mool Mantar. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the basic mantras from each of the four faiths for understanding, b) recite the basic mantras from the four faiths enhancing devotional practice, c) appreciate the recitation of the mantras for spiritual wellbeing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch / listen to the reciting or chanting of these basic mantras in their correct inotations from the four faiths,  write down the listed mantras from the four faiths,  practise the reciting of the mantras in turns using appropriate musical instrument in class/school assembly,  discuss in groups the importance of basic mantras in the life of the devotees,  ask parents/guardians/resource person the meaning and role of the listed basic mantras in the life of the devotees, ● in the company of a parent /guardian visit places of worship to learn about the importance of reciting mantras, ● assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the importance of reciting mantras. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is reciting mantras important in someone's faith? 2. What do you learn from reciting the basic mantras?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Places of Worship
chunks.text: STRAND: 4. Worship. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Places of Worship. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) name the features of places of worship for familiarization, b) illustrate the features of the places of worship from the four faiths, c) Acknowledge the importance of features at all places of worship. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in the company of a parent/ guardian/resource person, visit the places of worship to observe the main features found inside and outside,  take notes/videos/photos of the observed features,  prepare a portfolio which matches the features observed during the visit and their respective names/ faiths,  draw selected features and present in the class,  discuss the basic use of those listed features found at the places of worship,  assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the importance of features found inside and outside in any place of worship. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to have places of worship? 2. Why are the features of various places of worship important?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3 Religious Festivals -Dushera -Diwali -Bandi Chhor Diwas -Ganesh Chaturthi
chunks.text: STRAND: 4. Worship. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Religious Festivals -Dushera -Diwali -Bandi Chhor Diwas -Ganesh Chaturthi. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) name religious festivals from the four faiths for recognition, b) display appropriate greetings for the different festivals of the four faiths, c) appreciate the role of religious festivals for social cohesion. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  refer to appropriate resource material (learners’ book, digital device) to read about the following religious festivals,  use digital devices to gather information on religious festivals from the four faiths,  visit places of worship and interact with a resource person to get additional information about celebration of the religious festivals,  roleplay the appropriate greetings/events from the history of the festivals,  watch a video clip showing the rituals performed during festivals in the four faiths,  observe safety measures during celebration of festivals, for e.g on Diwali while dealing with fire crackers and lighting oil lamps,  sensitize their peers with special needs about the safety measures to be observed during celebration of festivals. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does celebrating religious festivals contribute to your wellbeing?

chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 SADACHAAR. SUB-STRAND: 5.1General Etiquette -at home -at school. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify general etiquettes observed at home/school, b) illustrate general etiquette in different situations at home/school, c) appreciate the role of general etiquette for harmonious living. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● brainstorm on the common terms of general etiquette, ● sing songs that are used to encourage the practice of general etiquette in their homes and school, ● write short sentences carrying the terms of general etiquette applying to home and school environment, ● role play the general etiquette applicable both at home and at home, ● watch video clip/listen to KICD radio programs/on the general etiquettes as can apply at home and school, ● discuss the benefits of observing general etiquette both at home and at school, ● observe and practice general etiquettes with their special needs classmates, ● assist their peers with special needs about the benefits of observing general etiquette both at home and school. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How is the use of general etiquette significant both at home and at school?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  refer to appropriate resource material (learners’ book, digital device) to read the selected short stories on etiquettes from the four faiths,  use digital devices to watch clips of the selected short stories on etiquettes,  narrate stories with morals on etiquettes to the peers,  prepare a skit based on the selected short stories on etiquettes,  role play scenes from identified moral stories and pick out the etiquette displayed and make a list to present in class, ● research on more moral stories and share in class, ● engage peers with special needs according to their abilities while roleplaying moral stories. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What role does moral stories play in one’s life?

chunks.sub_strand: 5.3 Sharing
chunks.text: STRAND: 5. SADACHAAR. SUB-STRAND: 5.3 Sharing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify situations where they can practise Sadachaar by sharing, b) implement sharing in events in their environment for social cohesion, c) appreciate the significance of sharing for spiritual growth. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  brainstorm in groups and present situations/occasions where Sadachaar involves sharing,  watch a video clip on a festival that shows participants sharing meals, gifts and company of each other,  role play sharing of selected age- appropriate items in class,  list the benefits of sharing appropriate items at home, in school and community,  in the company of a parent/ guardian/teacher participate in community events involving sharing, ● visit an orphanage/ home of the elderly and share their time, resources and service with the vulnerable groups, accompanied by parents/ guardians, ● assist their peers with special needs to participate in activities that are suitable to their abilities during their visit to orphanage. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we share with others? 2. In how many ways can we practice sharing?

chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 YOGA. SUB-STRAND: 6.1Basic Concepts of Yoga -Physical (Asanas, Pranayama) -Mental (Meditation, Pranayama) - Spiritual (Ethics, Lifestyle, Meditation,Self- realisation (Moksha). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of sub strand the learner should be able to: a) define Yoga and its basic concepts for confidence, b) categorise basic concepts of Yoga for peace and harmony, c) appreciate basic concepts in Yoga for enhancing well-being and happiness. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video clip on the each of the basic concepts of Yoga, Brainstorm the differences in the basic concepts of Yoga,  listen to a Yoga expert explaining the basic concepts of Yoga,  colour selected postures of types of Yoga,  categorise the basic concepts of Yoga that can help them to inculcate values like unity, respect and responsibility,  research with the assistance of a parent or guardian the value of Yoga in life,  assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the basic concepts in Yoga. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does Yoga impact our physical, mental and spiritual aspects of life?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  ask parents/ guardians/ resource persons to list the requirements of performing Yoga,  watch a video clip on the performance of age-appropriate Yoga observing all prerequisites,  practice age-appropriate Yoga while observing the pre-requisites under the supervision of a resource person,  work with the parent/ guardian to create a diary / schedule for performing age-appropriate Yoga practices,  discuss with peers with special needs in class on how they can enjoy Yoga practice KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are the pre- requisites of Yoga necessary?

chunks.sub_strand: 1 . 1a.n1d L i s t e Snpineagk ing to Instructions
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening. SUB-STRAND: 1 . 1a.n1d L i s t e Snpineagk ing to Instructions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify people found at home, b) follow simple instructions to accomplish tasks relating to home activities, c) use formal and informal greetings at home appropriately, d) enjoy listening and responding to instructions for communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  label pictures of people found at home,  listen to a variety of simple instructions relating to accomplishing home tasks through various media (oral, audio and audio- visual),  respond verbally or non-verbally to instructions,  play the “broken telephone game” (whisper game) with peers in class,  play singing games and recite rhymes related to formal and informal home greetings,  work collaboratively to role play formal and informal greetings at home. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is listening to instructions important? 2. Why do we greet people at home?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe pictures of different items found at home,  work jointly with peers to talk about the pictures observed,  sort and group pictures of items found at home,  match pictures of things found at home with their names,  colour and paint pictures of things found at home,  read names of pictures on things found at home, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we describe objects?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to pre-recorded clips with common syllables forming simple words,  imitate the syllables from an audio clips,  work with peers to blend the syllables to form words,  segment words into syllables,  work collaboratively to match syllables from flashcards to form complete words,  conduct a mini tour within the school to identify things found in school,  play a singing game involving pronouncing simple words related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we go to school?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we listen to stories? 2. Why is it important to observe etiquette in a conversation?

Why should we use courtesy in communication? 2. How do we form sentences?

chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Quran. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Arabic Alphabets (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the Arabic alphabets in three letter words in readiness for reading the Qur’an, b) listen actively to three letter words to enhance fluency in reading the Quran, c) read correctly three letter words with vowels in readiness for reading the Qur’an, d) appreciate the role of Arabic alphabets and vowels in the reading of the Qur’an. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● Arabic alphabets in three-letter words from flash cards/charts/digital devices and read them. ● listen to three-letter words with vowels from a digital device/resource person/teacher/peer and imitate them, ● read three-letter words with harakat or vowels (fat-hatain, dhumatain, kasratain and sukun) from flash cards and correct one another, ● pick three letter words from a box and read them, ● pick alphabets with harakat (vowels), form three-letter words and read them, ● sort and group three letter words from a basket/box and pronounce them. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should one learn Arabic alphabets?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Reads, recite and memorise all the verses of the selected surahs correctly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Reads, recite and memorise some of the verses of the selected surahs correctly. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Reads, recite and memorise a few verses of the selected surahs correctly.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Hadith on obedience to parents
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Hadith on obedience to parents (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) recite the Hadith on obedience to parents as a basis for moral development, b) practise the Hadith on obedience to parents in day- to-day life, c) appreciate the Hadith on obedience to parents to earn rewards from Allah (SWT). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● recite the Hadith on obedience to parents individually; ‘Allah (SWT)’s pleasure is in parents’ pleasure and Allah (SWT) anger is in parents’ anger,’’ ● pick flashcards to complete the Hadith on obedience to parents, ● roleplay situations depicting obedience to parents, ● story tell instances where obedience is practised in their daily life. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you show obedience to parents/teachers?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Hadith on cleanliness
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Hadith on cleanliness (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) recite the Hadith on cleanliness as a basis for moral development, b) Apply the teachings of the Hadith on cleanliness in day-to-day life, c) appreciate the Hadith on cleanliness to earn rewards from Allah (SWT). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● read after the teacher the Hadith on cleanliness displayed on a chart, ● recite the Hadith on cleanliness: ‘Cleanliness is part of faith…” and correct each other, ● sing songs on the importance of cleanliness and personal hygiene, ● engage cleaning activities such as cleaning the school compound, washing hands etc. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you uphold cleanliness? 2. Why should a Muslim maintain cleanliness?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Belief in Allah (SWT). Attributes of Allah (SWT) (Al-Khaaliq, Al-Razaaq)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Belief in Allah (SWT). Attributes of Allah (SWT) (Al-Khaaliq, Al-Razaaq) (7 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) mention the attributes of Allah (SWT) that describes Him as the Creator and the Provider to strengthen their Iman, b) use the selected attributes of Allah (SWT) in day-to-day life, c) appreciate the bounties Created and Provided by Allah (SWT). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to the teacher/resource person/peer/digital device mentioning the attributes of Allah (SWT), (Al-Khaaliq, Al-Razaaq) and repeat after him/her ● sort and match the attributes of Allah (SWT) with their corresponding meaning using flashcards individually or in pairs, ● observe the creation of Allah (SWT) outside the classroom and mention their names, ● model/draw/paint/colour the creation of Allah (SWT) observed outside the classroom, ● watch pictures/videos of Allah (SWT)’s creation and mention their names, ● sing and listen to qasida with the attributes of Allah (SWT) as Creator and Provider. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you benefit from Allah (SWT)’s creation?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Belief in Angels (Raqib and Atid)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Belief in Angels (Raqib and Atid) (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) name the angels of Allah (SWT) responsible for recording of deeds to strengthen Iman, b) mention the duties performed by angels Raqib and Atid for spiritual nourishment, c) appreciate the duties performed by angels Raqib and Atid as a Pillar of iman. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guide to: ● listen to and sing qasida on the angels Raqib and Atid. ● pick names of the selected angels from a pocket board and read the names aloud. ● play games depicting good and bad deeds and differentiating them such as ‘nyama nyama nyama’. ● Match and sort the duties of the selected angels using flush cards KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the duties of angels? 2. What are the benefits of doing good deeds?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1 Pillars of Islam Shahada Swalah Saum Zakat Hajj
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Pillars of Islam Shahada Swalah Saum Zakat Hajj (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) name the five pillars of Islam to strengthen their faith, b) recite the five pillars of Islam in sequence. c) appreciate the five pillars of Islam as a foundation of Islam. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● sing songs or poems on the pillars of Islam, ● arrange pillars of Islam using flash cards in their sequence, ● participate in a game involving the mentioning of the five pillars of Islam in sequence, ● take turns to recite the five pillars of Islam and correct one another, ● draw a house/tree with 5 pillars representing the five pillars of Islam, colour and display in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the things that a Muslim should do to obey Allah? 2. How can you identify a true Muslim?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Shahadah
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Shahadah (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) recite the Shahadah as a pillar of Islam to strengthen their faith, b) demonstrate the occasions when the Shahadah is proclaimed in day-to- day life, c) appreciate the use of Shahadah in the life of a Muslim. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● sing songs or poems on the shahada ● pick flashcards from a pocket board to from the shahada ● take-turns to recite the Shahada and correct one another, ● roleplay occasions when the Shahada is said (for example when converting to Islam, in the tashahud, in the adhan, at the onset of death) and share experiences. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. When do we say the shahada? 2. Why do Muslims say the Shahada?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3 Wudhu (steps and performance of wudhu)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Wudhu (steps and performance of wudhu) (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) name the steps of wudhu in preparation for swalah, b) perform wudhu systematically as a prerequisite for performance of prayers, c) appreciate wudhu as a purification requirement before performing swalah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video clip showing the correct steps in the performance of wudhu and describe what they have observed,  watch the teacher/resource person/peer demonstrating the steps of wudhu (washing the hands, rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nostrils, washing the face, washing the two arms, wiping the head, wiping the ears, washing the feet) and repeat,  pick flashcards with steps of wudhu and arrange them in sequence,  sing qasida on steps of wudhu with appropriate gesture/movement  demonstrate the performance of wudhu in the correct order, record themselves and share with friends using a digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you do before you pray? 2. Which body parts are washed during wudhu?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5. 1 Relationship 5.1.1 Love for Allah (SWT)’s bounties
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (Moral Teachings). SUB-STRAND: 5. 1 Relationship 5.1.1 Love for Allah (SWT)’s bounties (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) identify five bounties of Allah (SWT) in the immediate environment to enhance love for Allah (SWT), b) utilise the bounties of Allah (SWT) appropriately to earn His blessings, c) appreciate the bounties of Allah (SWT) as a sign of love to mankind. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch video clips/pictures/paper cuttings showing bounties of Allah (SWT) (for example, plants, animals, self-body parts) and name them, ● play games involving touching and naming body parts as part of Allah (SWT)’s bounties (For example. ‘head- shoulder’) ● carry out simple activities using their hands, legs and eyes to appreciate the bounties of the body parts, ● listen/sing qasida/ recite poems on Allah (SWT)’s favours, ● draw and colour, trees, animals as part of creation of Allah (SWT) from the immediate environment, ● cut, mount pictures of plants and animals; and display in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which bounties of Allah (SWT) are in your immediate environment? 2. How do you take care of Allah (SWT)’s creation?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.2 Love for parents
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings). SUB-STRAND: 5.1.2 Love for parents (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) state five ways of show love to their parents/guardians, b) demonstrate ways of showing love to parents/guardians in day-to-day life, c) appreciate love accorded to parents/guardians in their day-to- day life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to short stories on love to parents and mention the ways described in the stories, ● roleplay ways of showing love to parents/guardians (for example, children greeting their parents, giving gifts to them, helping with small errands at home; responding to their call, obeying them etc), ● make paper cutouts with different ways of treating parents and mount them on a charts, ● sort from a box/basket paper cutouts with different ways of treating parents, isolating good from bad ways, ● sing qasidas and songs on love for parents, ● keep a journal record on ways they have shown love to their parents/guardians. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we treat our parents? 2. How do you show love to your parents?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2 Care for the Environment- home
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings). SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Care for the Environment- home (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) outline ways of maintaining cleanliness in the home for healthy living, b) practice cleanliness of home compound to facilitate healthy living, c) appreciate the importance of maintaining a clean home environment as an act of ibadah SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● mention the items used for cleaning the home environment and draw them, ● clean their home compound, record themselves using digital devices and present in class, ● improvise simple cleaning items and display them in the classroom, ● sing qasidas on the importance of cleanliness. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we keep our compound clean? 2. Why should we keep our school compound clean? 3. What items do we use to clean the home?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1 Birth of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 Siirah (Life of Prophet S.A.W). SUB-STRAND: 6.1 Birth of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the name given to the Prophet (S.A.W) at birth, b) narrate the event of the birth of the Prophet (S.A.W), c) appreciate the birthplace of the Prophet as the holy city of Muslims SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● pick out the name of the Prophet (S.A.W) from a set of flash cards containing other names, ● listen to the story about the events of the Amul-fiil (Year of the Elephant) from a video clip/teacher and narrate the events of Amul- fiil ● are guided to name the date, month and year of birth of the Prophet (SAW) ● draw and colour the Kaaba, elephant and birds ● sing qasida on the birth of the Prophet (S.A.W) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What events took place during the birth of the Prophet (S.A.W)

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1 Eid ul-Fitr
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 Islamic Festivals. SUB-STRAND: 7.1 Eid ul-Fitr (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the Islamic month on which Eid ul-Fitr falls as part of the history of Islam, b) mention the activities carried out during Eid ul-Fitr festival in the Islamic calendar, c) appreciate Eid ul-Fitr celebrations as an important festival among Muslims.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1 Eid ul-Adha
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 Islamic Festivals. SUB-STRAND: 7.1 Eid ul-Adha (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the Islamic month on which the Eid ul-Adha falls as part of the history of Islam, b) mention the activities carried out during the Eid ul-Adha festival in the Islamic calendar, c) appreciate Eid ul-Adha celebrations as an important festival among Muslims. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch video clips on the celebration of Eid ul- Adha and mention the date, month and activities observed, ● listen to the activities undertaken during the Eid ul-Adha from a resource person/teacher and narrate the activities that take place before and during the Eid festival, ● role play the activities that take place during the Eid celebrations (for example, taking bath, wearing clean clothes, attending the Eid prayer, reciting the takbir, slaughtering, feasting, exchange of gifts etc). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you prepare for Eid celebrations? 2. Why do Muslims celebrate Eid ul- Adha?

chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Kifungu cha Hadithi
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Kifungu cha Hadithi. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa katika kifungu, b) kutunga sentensi sahihi akitumia msamiati uliotumiwa, c) kusikiliza kifungu anachosomewa cha maneno kati ya 15-20 na kupata ujumbe, d) kujibu maswali kuhusu hadithi aliyosikiliza, e) kuchangamkia kusikiliza kifungu ili kujenga ari ya kusoma. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kushirikiana na wengine kujadili picha zilizojumuishwa kwenye hadithi, ● kutabiri kitakachotokea kwenye hadithi, ● kuthibitisha utabiri wake baada ya kusikiliza hadithi, ● kutunga sentensi akitumia msamiati uliotumika kwenye hadithi, ● kusikiliza kifungu cha maneno kati ya 15-20 kikisomwa na mwalimu au kupitia vifaa vya kiteknolojia ● kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu, ● kujadiliane kuhusu hadithi waliyosomewa katika kikundi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Unatarajiwa kufanya nini unaposomew a hadithi? 2. Unawezaje kupata ujumbe katika kifungu cha hadithi unachosome wa?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze; a) kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, b) kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, c) kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya ufahamu ili kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa (k.v. mimi, wenzangu) kutoka kwenye kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno, kapu maneno akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 13- 16 kuhusu suala lengwa na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kumweleza mzazi au mlezi kuhusu ujumbe aliopata kutokana na kifungu alichosoma. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni mambo gani unayoweza kujifunza katika hadithi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1 Matumizi ya Kikomo (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Matumizi ya Kikomo (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua alama ya kikomo katika maandishi, b) kuandika alama ya kikomo ifaavyo katika daftari, c) kutumia ipasavyo alama ya kikomo katika sentensi, d) kufurahia kutumia alama ya kikomo ipasavyo katika sentensi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua alama ya kikomo (.) katika sentensi kitabuni, kwenye chati au kifaa cha kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kuandika sentensi daftarini au kutumia kifaa cha kidijitali kisha aweke alama ya kikomo, ● kutumia alama ya kikomo ipasavyo mwishoni mwa sentensi akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kumwonyesha mzazi au mlezi alama ya kikomo na kuitumia ipasavyo katika sentensi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Alama gani zinazotumika katika kuandika sentensi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4.1 Matumizi ya -angu na -etu (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 5.4.1 Matumizi ya -angu na -etu (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua matumizi ya -angu na -etu katika miktadha mbalimbali, b) kutumia -angu na - etu katika mazungumzo kwa ufasaha ili kuimarisha mawasiliano, c) kufurahia kutumia - angu na -etu katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua matumizi ya -angu na - etu kwa kurejelea vitu katika mazingira yake, ● kuigiza matumizi ya -angu na -etu akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi kwa kutumia vitu anavyomiliki k.v. kitabu changu – vitabu vyetu; rafiki yangu - marafiki zetu, ● kusoma sentensi zinazotumia maneno - angu na –etu, ● kukamilisha sentensi zenye matumizi ya -angu na –etu, ● kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia -angu na -etu. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni maneno gani unayotumia kuonyesha kuwa kitu ni chako au ni chenu?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sauti lengwa katika kadi maneno, b) kutamka sauti lengwa ipasavyo ili kuimarisha mazungumzo, c) kutamkasilabi za sautilengwa ipasavyo, d) kutamka ipasavyo maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa, e) kuchangamkia nafasi ya matamshi bora f) katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kushiriki katika kutambua sauti lengwa (/s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/) katika kadi maneno, ● kusikiliza matamshi ya sauti lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kutamka sauti lengwa akiwa na mwalimu kisha akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusikiliza silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kidijitali k.v. kinasasauti na rununu, ● kutamka silabi alizozisikiliza ipasavyo akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kutamka ipasavyo maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni sauti zipi unazojua kutamka?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sauti lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi, b) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa c) kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, d) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa e) kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti, f) kusoma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo, g) kuchangamkia kusoma kwa ufasaha ili kufanikisha mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua sauti lengwa (/s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/) katika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,  kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akishirikiana na wenzake,  kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti akishirikiana na wenzake,  kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 20 kwa dakika na kwa kuizingatia viakifishi) akishirikiana na wenzake, kusoma hadithi kutoka kwenye kitabu, kifaa cha kidijtali, nk akishirikiana na wenzake, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni kwa nini unafaa kutamka maneno vizuri unaposoma?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3.1 Tahajia Imla (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 6.3.1 Tahajia Imla (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua maneno yasiyozidi silabi tatu kutokana na suala lengwa, b) kuandika kwa usahihi maneno yasiyozidi silabi tatu kwa kuunganisha silabi kuunda neno, c) kufurahia kuandika maneno kwa usahihi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua maneno yasiyozidi silabi tatu kutokana na suala lengwa kwa kusomewa na mwalimu au katika kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kusikiliza maneno yasiyozidi silabi tatu ya kiwango chake yakisomwa na mwalimu au kutoka kwa kifaa cha kidigitali (k.v radio) na kuyaandika, ● kushirikiana na wenzake kuandika maneno yasiyozidi silabi tatu ya kiwango chake, kwa kuunganisha silabi kuunda neno, ● kuyakosoa maneno aliyoyaendeleza visivyofaa. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni maneno gani ya silabi tatu unayajua?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 6.4.1 Matumizi ya -zuri na – baya (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 6.4.1 Matumizi ya -zuri na – baya (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua matumizi ya – zuri na – baya katika kifungu, b) kutumia –zuri na – baya katika sentensi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano, c) kufurahia kutumia –zuri na –baya katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua matumizi ya -zuri na -baya kwa kurejelea vitu katika mazingira yake, ● kutumia -zuri na -baya akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi kurejelea vitu katika mazingira yake, ● kusikiliza matumizi ya –zuri na – baya kwa kutumia kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kusoma sentensi zinazotumia maneno - zuri na –baya, ● kukamilisha sentensi zenye matumizi ya -zuri na –baya, ● kujaza mapengo kwa kutumia - zuri na –baya, ● kumtajia mzazi au mlezi vitu nyumbani kutumia –zuri na – baya. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni maneno gani unayotumia kuelezea vitu vinavyokupendeza au visivyokupendeza?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1.1 Maagizo (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1 Maagizo (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua maagizo mepesi yanayotolewa darasani, b) kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi yanayotumiwa darasani, c) kubainisha maagizo yanayopaswa kufuatwa katika mazingira yake, d) kuthamini umuhimu wa maagizo katika maisha ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua maagizo kwa kutazama video ya maagizo, ● kutoa na kufuata maagizo (kama vile simama, keti, andika na chora) akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi, ● kueleza kuhusu maagizo yafaayo na yasiyofaa kufuatwa, ● kushiriki katika azungumzo ya matokeo ya kufuata na kutofuata maagizo, ● kuimba na kuigiza nyimbo zinazohusu maagizo. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni maagizo yapi yanayotaki wa kufuatwa na yasiyotaki wa kufuatwa katika mazingira tofauti?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 7.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, b) kutabiri yatakayotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu kwa kuzingatia picha, c) kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, d) kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, e) kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya ufahamu ili kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kusikiliza au atazame nyimbo kuhusu usafi wa mwili kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kuimba wimbo kuhusu usafi wa mwili akiwa na wenzake, ● kutabiri kitakachotokea katika hadithi akizingatia picha kwenye kifungu akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 17- 22 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa (k.v oga, nawa osha, maji, sabuni) akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano akishirikiana na wenzake, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unapenda kusoma kuhusu nini?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3.1 Kuandika maneno ipasavyo (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Kuandika maneno ipasavyo (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua maneno yanayotokana na suala lengwa, b) kuandika maneno yanayohusu suala lengwa kwa kuunganisha silabi ili kuunda neno, c) kufurahia uandishi wa maneno katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua maneno mepesi yanayotokana na suala lengwa (kama vile: oga, nawa, osha, maji, sabuni), ● kuandika maneno yanayotokana na suala lengwa daftarini au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali kwa kuunganisha silabi kuunda neno akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili na kurekebisha makosa katika maandishi yake, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Ni maneno gani unayoweza kuandika kwa kuunganisha silabi? 2. Kwa nini ni muhimu kujifunza kuandika?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4.1 Ukanushaji (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 7.4.1 Ukanushaji (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua ukanusho wa nafsi ya kwanza umoja na wingi katika vifungu, b) kutumia ukanusho wa nafsi ya kwanza umoja na wingi katika kifungu kwa usahihi, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya ukanusho wa nafsi ya kwanza umoja na wingi katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutenda vitendo atakavyoagizwa na mwalimu kuashiria nafsi ya kwanza umoja,  kutenda vitendo vyake mwenyewe na kusema anachokifanya,  kutambua ukanusho wa nafsi ya kwanza umoja,  kushirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kukanusha sentensi katika nafsi ya kwanza umoja,  kukamilisha sentensi zinazoashiria ukanusho wa nafsi ya kwanza umoja kwa kuelekezwa na mwalimu,  kusikiliza sentensi kwa kutumia kifaa cha kidigitali zilizokanushwa akielekezwa na mwalimu. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Unafanya nini sasa? 2. Kama haukufanya mambo uliyotaja ungesemaje?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.1.1 Matams hi bora (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Matams hi bora (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sauti lengwa katika kadi maneno, b) kutamka sauti lengwa ipasavyo ili kuimarisha mazungumzo, c) kutamka silabi za sauti sauti lengwa ipasavyo, d) kutamka ipasavyo maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa, e) kuchangamkia nafasi ya matamshi bora katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kushiriki katika kutambua sauti lengwa (/j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/) katika kadi maneno, ● kusikiliza mwalimu au mgeni mwalikwa akitamka sauti lengwa, ● kutamka sauti alizozisikiliza pamoja na mwalimu na mwishowe kutamka akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kutumia vifaa vya kidijitali (k.v. papaya) kusikiliza matamshi bora ya sauti lengwa, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kwa ninini muhimu kutamka maneno ipasavyo?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 8.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sauti lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi, b) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, c) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa sauti inayosikika, d) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo, e) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo, f) kuchangamkia kusoma SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua sauti lengwa (/j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/) katika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 25 kwa dakika na kwa kuzingatia viakifishi) akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma hadithi kutoka kwenye kitabu, kifaa cha kidijtali, nk akishirikiana na wenzake, akizingatia matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na kwa sauti inayosikika, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Matamshi bora na sauti inayosikika yana umuhimu gani katika kusoma?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.3.1 Tahajia (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Tahajia (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua tahajia sahihi katika sentensi, b) kuandika sentensi tatu kuhusu suala lengwa akizingatia tahajia sahihi, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya tahajia sahihi katika uandishi wa sentensi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua sentensi zinazohusu suala lengwa zenye tahajia sahihi kwa kutumia nyenzo kama vile:kadi za majina,mti maneno,kapu maneno,chati,kifungu au kifaa cha kidigitali, ● kusoma sentensi zenye tahajia sahihi kuhusu suala lengwa, ● kunakili sentensi zenye tahajia sahihi kuhusu suala lengwa kwenye daftari, ● kutunga sentensi tatu sahihi kuhusu suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kuandika sentensi alizotunga kwa kuzingatia tahajia sahihi, ● kusoma sentensi alizoandika pamoja na wenzake katika kikundi kisha wenzake wazitolee maoni, ● kusahihisha sentensi alizoandika kwa kuzingatia tahajia, ● Kumwonyesha mzazi au mlezi sentensi sahihi alizoandika ili apate maoni yake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kwa nini ni muhimu kuyaandika maneno na sentensi kwa usahihi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.4.1 Matumizi ya hiki na hivi Vipindi 3
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 8.4.1 Matumizi ya hiki na hivi Vipindi 3. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua maneno hiki na hivi katika vifungu, b) kusoma vifungu vinavyojumuisha maneno hiki na hivi ili kuonyeshea ifaavyo, c) kutumia maneno hiki na hivi kuonyeshea vitu katika mazingira yake, d) kuchangamkia matumizi ya hiki na hivi katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua hiki na hivi kwa kutumia nyenzo halisi, kadi za majina, kapu maneno au chati, ● kusikiliza kifungu kinachohusu matumizi ya hiki na hivi katika kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kusoma vifungu vinavyojumuisha hiki na hivi kisha abainishe matumizi ya hiki na hivi, ● kuonyesha vitu mbalimbali kama vile vyakula na kuvitungia sentensi katika kikundi k.m. chakula hiki – vyakula hivi, ● kumtungia mwenzake sentensi katika kikundi kwa kutumia hiki na hivi, ● kutoa maoni kuhusu sentensi zilizotungwa na wenzake, ● kukamilisha vifungu vyenye mapengo kwa kutumia hiki na hivi wakiwa wawiliwawili k.m. chakula (hiki, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unajua majina yapi ya vitu vinavyoweza kuashiriwa kwa kutumia maneno hiki na hivi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 9.1.1 Mazungumzo
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Mazungumzo. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua suala lengwa ili azungumze kulihusu, b) kuzungumza kuhusu suala lengwa akizingatia matamshi bora na ishara zifaazo, c) kujieleza kwa ujasiri, kasi ifaayo na sauti inayosikika, d) kuchangamkia mazungumzo na matamshi bora katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kusikiliza mazungumzo mafupi kuhusu suala lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kutazama video kuhusu mazungumzo yanayohusisha watoto, ● kuwasilisha mazungumzo yake kwa wenzake katika kikundi kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora na ishara zifaazo, ● kujieleza kwa ujasiri, kasi ifaayo na sauti inayosikika, ● kusikiliza mazungumzo ya wenzake na kutoa maoni. ● kushiriki katika mazungumzo kwa kuzingatia maagizo atakayopewa na mwalimu, ● kujieleza kwa ujasiri ili kufanikisha mawasiliano akiwa na mzazi au mlezi jikoni. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Unapenda kuzungumza kuhusu mambo gani ukiwa na wenzako? 2. Unazingatia mambo gani unapozungumz a mbele ya wenzako?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Pre-Number Activities
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Pre-Number Activities (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) sort objects according to similar attributes in different situations, b) match objects with similar attributes in the environment, c) order objects according to given criteria in different situations, d) create patterns of different sizes and shapes using real objects, e) appreciate the use of sorting and grouping items in day-to-day activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, collect different types of safe objects from the immediate environment, ● group objects according to attributes such as size, colour, use, shape and texture, ● pair objects with similar attributes such as size, colour, use, shape and texture, ● arrange objects according to size from smallest to biggest and from biggest to smallest, ● make patterns of different shapes and sizes using real objects, ● in pairs/groups, assist in arranging items like fruits, cereals, for example beans, maize and rice according to size, colour, shape and storage at home. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we group objects? 2. How can we arrange objects?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Whole Numbers
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Whole Numbers (25 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) count numbers forward up to 50, b) count numbers backwards from 30, c) represent numbers 1 to 30 using concrete objects, d) read and write numbers 1 to 50 in symbols, e) read and write numbers 1 to 10 in words, f) identify missing numbers SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, collect concrete objects from the immediate environment to use in counting activities, ● in pairs/groups, count by 1’s and 2’s up to 20 starting from any point using concrete objects such as number cards, as well as body parts, ● take turns in counting numbers forward up to 50, ● in pairs/groups, count numbers backwards from 30, ● in pairs/groups, play games that involve KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: In what ways can we count from 1 to 20?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Addition
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Addition (25 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) model addition as putting objects together, b) use ' +' and ' =' signs in writing addition statements, c) add 2 single digit numbers in different situations, d) add 3 single digit numbers in different contexts, e) add a 2 digit number to a 1 digit number without regrouping with sum not exceeding 50, f) work out missing numbers in patterns involving addition of whole numbers up to 50, g) play games involving addition using digital devices or other resources. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, safely put two groups of objects together and count to get the total, ● use ' + ' and ' = ' signs in writing addition statements, ● add 2 single digit numbers by counting on, ● add 3 single digit numbers using concrete objects, ● add 3 single digit numbers by counting on, ● add a 2 digit number to a 1 digit number without regrouping horizontally and vertically with sum not exceeding 50, ● in pairs/groups, make number patterns involving addition with numbers up to 50, ● play games involving addition using digital devices and other resources. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you add a 2 digit number to a 1 digit number?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 Subtraction
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 Subtraction (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) model subtraction as 'taking away' using concrete objects, b) use the ' - ' and '='signs in writing subtraction sentences, c) subtract single digit numbers, d) subtract a 1 digit number from a 2 digit number without regrouping, e) work out missing numbers in patterns involving subtraction of whole numbers up to 50, f) play games involving subtraction using digital devices and other resources. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, model subtraction using concrete objects, ● use ' - ' and '=' signs in writing subtraction sentences, ● in pairs/groups, subtract by counting backwards, ● in pairs/groups, subtract using concrete objects, ● create subtraction sentences related to basic addition facts, ● use number cards or charts safely to workout subtraction of a 1 digit number from a 2 digit number, ● in pairs /groups, create patterns involving subtraction. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you subtract a one digit number from a two digit number?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Length
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Length (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) collect objects of different lengths from the immediate environment, b) compare length of objects using longer than, shorter than and same as, c) measure length using arbitrary units, d) appreciate measuring length using arbitrary units. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/ groups, collect objects of different lengths from the immediate environment, ● in pairs/ groups, compare objects directly to identify objects which are longer than, shorter than or same as other objects, ● in pairs/ groups, measure lengths using arbitrary units such as hand spans or walking steps and discuss the measurements from the various groups, ● in pairs/ groups, use arbitrary units to measure lengths of different objects in their immediate environment. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you compare the length of two objects? 2. What can be used to measure the length of the teacher’s table?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Mass
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurements. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Mass (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) collect objects with different mass from the immediate environment, b) compare mass of two objects using heavier than, lighter than or same as, c) measure mass using arbitrary units, d) appreciate measuring mass using arbitrary units in the environment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● collect safe objects of different mass from their immediate environment, ● in groups, discuss and use safe objects to identify those heavier than, lighter than or same as, ● in groups, use an identified empty container of known mass to measure the mass of other objects such as mass of beans, maize or flour as accurately as possible, ● play games involving mass using digital devices. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can you compare the mass of two or more objects? 2. How can you show that an object is heavier than, lighter than or same as your mathematics textbook?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Capacity
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Capacity (12 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) collect containers of different capacities from the immediate environment, b) compare capacity of two containers using more than, less than and same as, c) measure capacity using arbitrary units, d) re-use empty containers of different capacities to keep items. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, collect safe containers of different sizes from the environment, ● in pairs/groups, empty and fill water in different containers to establish which holds more, which holds less and which holds the same, ● in pairs/groups, fill basins with water using different small containers. The learners to count the number of small containers they use to fill the basin, ● in pairs/groups, discuss and re-use containers of different capacity at home and school to keep items. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we find out which of two containers hold more, less or same as?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Time
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Time (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify days of the week, b) relate days of the week to various activities, c) identify months of the year, d) appreciate activities that are done on different days of the week. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● sing songs/ rhymes related to days of the week, ● tell and write days of the week the way they follow each other, ● in pairs/groups, identify activities that take place during the days of the week such as raising flag on Monday and Friday, ● in groups, sing songs/rhymes related to the months of the year, ● discuss and tell their birth month. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which day of the week do you raise the school flag? 2. Which day of the week do you worship?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.5 Money
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.5 Money (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify Kenyan currency coins, b) identify Kenyan currency note up to sh.50, c) count Kenyan currency coins one at a time, d) use money in buying up to 2 items without balance, e) appreciate the use of money in buying items from shops. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, recognise and sort out different Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20 and sh.40 according to their value, ● in pairs/groups, recognise a sh.50 note and tell its value, ● in pairs/groups, tell how many coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, sh. 40 by counting, ● discuss the price of items in the model classroom shop up to sh.50, ● in groups to role play buying up to 2 items from the model classroom shop without balance. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you identify Kenyan currency coins and notes?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Lines
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Geometry. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Lines (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify straight lines in different situations, b) draw straight lines on different surfaces, c) identify curved lines in different situations, d) draw curved lines on different surfaces, e) recognise straight and curved lines from real objects in the environment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● stand behind one another facing the same side and identify what they have formed as a straight line, ● in pairs/groups, mark two points on the ground and use a stick to join the two points to make a straight line, ● practise drawing straight lines on the ground and in their books, ● in groups, form a semicircle, draw a line around it and identify the line drawn as a curved line, ● practise drawing curved lines on the ground and in their books, ● in groups, observe and identify lines from different objects in the environment. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you make a line?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary ( 2 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary ( 2 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) distinguish words with the target letter -sound combinations in conversations, b) use vocabulary related to the theme to communicate in various contexts, c) respond to specific simple two- directional instructions using new words in oral communication, d) realize the importance of listening attentively and pronouncing words correctly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to audio-visual recordings of songs, story/teacher read aloud stories, among others, with the target letter –sound combination,  pick words with the target letter – sound combination: o bl as in blue, o sp as in spoon, o sc as in school, o sk as in sky, o ck –as in kick,  practice using the target letter-sound combinations to form word,  construct simple sentences using new words,  develop a talking tree collaboratively with peers using the new words,  respond to two-directional instructions without interrupting as modeled by the teacher or peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we listen attentively when other people are talking?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) recognize words with the target letter-sound combinations for ease of reading, b) read a grade-appropriate text with the target letter-sound combinations at the right speed, expressively and accurately, c) realise the importance of reading fluently in a variety of genres. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video clip/listen to an audio recording/teacher model of the target sounds,  pick out words featuring the target letter- sound combinations: bl, sp, sc, sk, ck,  practise sitting in the appropriate posture, hold a book in the right position and turn the pages carefully while reading,  read short texts observing stress and intonation,  engage in timed reading (65 words per minute) displaying the right expressions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we read at the right speed? 2. Why should we read a text accurately?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions and anticipate possible outcomes in a story for comprehension, b) use contextual clues to infer meaning of vocabulary words related to the theme, c) answer direct and indirect questions for comprehension, d) realize the importance of reading for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss pictures and the title of a text with peers and make predictions,  read a text and locate phrases and sentences to get the meaning of new words,  locate sentences containing answers to direct questions,  interact with the text and answer indirect questions using contextual clues. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do pictures help us to know what the story is about? 2. How do we get the meaning of words from a text?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 The verb ‘to be’ (is, are)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 The verb ‘to be’ (is, are) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognize the correct use of the verbs to be is and are in sentences, b) use the present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ correctly, to construct simple sentences, c) adopt the use of the present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ in their day-to-day conversation. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a story, poem or conversation from audio recording/ teacher model containing is and are,  identify sentences showing present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ from the text,  describe own and other learners’ demonstrated actions using is and are,  ask and answer questions using is and are, collaboratively with peers observing turn taking,  practise the use of is and are during role play, language games or songs. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we talk about what is happening at the present?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise descenders in long words in a text, b) form all descenders correctly in long words, legibly and neatly for correct word formation, c) realise the importance of writing long words correctly, legibly and neatly for different purposes. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch videos on how to write long words with descenders from a digital device, or as modelled by the teacher or peers and identify descenders in long words in a text,  copy long words forming all the descenders correctly, legibly and neatly,  write words with descenders from a dictation correctly, legibly and neatly,  write long words related to the theme in response to a picture prompts. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we write clearly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Listening And Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter-sound combinations accurately in various contexts, b) articulate words with target letter- sounds combination for clarity in communication, c) use new words related to the theme to communicate in various contexts, d) respond to specific two- directional instructions in oral communication, e) realise the importance of listening attentively for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an audio recording/teacher model of the target letter-sound combinations, o /tʃ/ as in match o /əʊ/ goat, no o / ʃ/ as in shop o cl as in clean  pronounce the target letter-sound combinations taking turns,  pick out words with the target letter-sound combinations,  take photos/record video clips about activities in the home and discuss its content,  use dialogues/ rhymes/ tongue twisters/ language games and songs to practise vocabulary KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we listen attentively? 2. Why should we pronounce sounds and words

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letter-sound combinations from a text in preparation for reading, b) pronounce words with the target sounds accurately, c) read a text accurately at the right speed, displaying the appropriate feelings or emotions for fluency, d) realise the importance of reading fluently. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video clip on reading fluency and respond to questions from the teacher and peers,  pick out words featuring the target letter- sound combinations: /cl/ and /ɔʊ/ from various texts,  practise reading a short print or digital text featuring words with the target blend expressively and fluently,  engage in timed reading of a text displaying appropriate feelings or emotion,  practise reading texts with peers for fluency. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we show feelings when reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.2 Comprehension ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.2 Comprehension ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make connections between the text and their daily life experiences, b) infer meanings of new words from the context, c) read a text to answer direct and indirect questions correctly, d) adopt reading simple, short narratives and informational texts in a variety of genres. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss pictures and the title of a text with peers and make predictions,  read simple digital or print texts related to the theme, and locate phrases and sentences to get the meaning of words,  locate sentences containing answers to direct questions and answer the questions,  interact with the text and answer indirect questions,  summarise the story in a few words,  brainstorm on the relevance of the story to their day-to-day activities. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we answer question from a text? 2. How do we make sure we understand what we read?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1. The verb ‘to be’ (was, were)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1. The verb ‘to be’ (was, were) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct use of the verb ‘to be’ (was, were) in sentences, b) use correct subject-verb agreement to construct simple sentences about activities in the home, c) realize the importance of subject- verb agreement in conversation for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a digital text containing ‘was’ and ‘were’ and identify sentences with the target grammar item,  type sentences based on pictures on a digital device (using was and were),  use the verb to be to construct sentences from actions demonstrated by peers,  play a language game using the verb to be (was, were). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What were you doing at home yesterday?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise ascenders in long words in a text, b) write long words correctly, legibly and neatly forming all ascenders for correct word formation, c) realize the importance of writing long words correctly, legibly and neatly for different purposes. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at samples of correct, clear, and legible handwriting from a text,  Observe peer/teacher demonstration of well- shaped letters,  model ascenders using different materials,  copy words and letter patterns ascenders featuring the target letter -sound combinations ‘dr’, ‘fr’, ‘fl’, ‘gl’,  copy sentences with ascenders from charts/ flash cards/ chalkboard,  write words related to the theme in response to a picture prompts. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to shape letters well? 2. What do you consider to be a good handwriting?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target letter- sound combinations in words from an oral text, b) pronounce words with the target letter- sound combinations accurately, c) use new words related to the theme in short sentences, d) respond to specific simple two- directional instructions using new words in oral communication, e) realize the importance of listening attentively and responding appropriately for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an oral text featuring the target letter- sound combinations, o /s/ as in dress, o /l/- call, tall o ‘fl’ as in flew o / eɪ / as in way, grey  say words with the target letter-sound combinations,  sing simple songs or recite poems with words which have the target letter- sound combinations,  pronounce new words related to the theme from flash cards/picture cues/sound prompts,  discuss meaning of new words with the target sounds with peers,  construct sentences using the new words,  listen and respond to two-directional instructions as modelled by KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we listen attentively when other people are talking?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) identify words with target letter- sound combinations in sentences, b) read words related to the theme fluently, with accuracy and expressions. c) realise the correspondence between spoken words and written words for fluency in reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  point out words from the text with target letter- sound combinations (‘fl’, ‘ey’)  watch videos or listen to the teacher model reading with fluency and say the words,  read a print/digital text aloud at the benchmark level of 65 words per minute and pick out decodable and non-decodable words,  use word attack skills such as look and say to recognise and read words related to the theme,  play word ladder and pronounce words or listen to audio/visual recording of words without letter sound correspondence. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we read fluently?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story based on the title and pictures, b) infer the meanings of words from the context, c) respond to direct and indirect questions for comprehension, d) adopt reading texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read the title and look at the pictures to make predictions about the story,  discuss the possible outcome of the story with peers,  read a text and locate phrases and sentences to get the meaning of new words,  locate sentences containing answers to direct questions and use them to answer questions,  respond to indirect questions using contextual clues,  role play the events in story for comprehension. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to understand what we read?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1. Singular and plural objective pronouns
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1. Singular and plural objective pronouns (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the correct use of singular and plural objective pronouns in sentences, b) use singular and plural objective pronouns to construct simple sentences related to the theme, c) realise the importance of singular and plural objective pronouns in communication, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a story/poem/conversation featuring objective pronouns, (me, us, you, him/her, them)  pick out singular and plural objective plurals in the text,  discuss how pronouns have been used in the text with peers,  construct correct sentences using singular and plural objective pronouns orally with peers and give feedback,  answer questions using objective pronouns. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we talk about a person without mentioning their name?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise ascenders and descenders in long words, b) write long words forming all ascenders and descenders, correctly, legibly and neatly, c) realise the importance of forming all ascenders and descenders appropriately in writing long words. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  watch videos on how to write long words with ascenders and descenders from a digital device, or as modeled by the teacher or peers,  practice writing the letters in the air  observe displayed flash cards and copy the letters,  copy long words with the target letter-sound combinations (fl- and - ey),  practise writing long word forming ascenders and descenders with peers,  write words related to the theme from a dictation, in response to a picture prompt. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we write words?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter- sound combinations in oral texts, b) articulate words with the target letter -sound combinations for effective communication, c) pronounce the words related to the theme accurately, d) use the new words to construct sentences in various contexts, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pronounce words with the target letter- sound combinations as modelled by the teacher or peers, o / ŋ / ing as in thing;/ ŋ o / iː/ as in happy in words ending with letter y o st as in stick o gl as in glass  say tongue twisters/poems/songs containing the target letter-sound combinations, with peers,  pronounce the words related to the theme accurately,  construct simple sentences orally using the new words, with peers and give feedback, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.2 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2. Reading. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.2 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words containing the target letter-sound combinations in preparation for reading, b) read a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) adopt reading simple, short narratives and informational texts in a variety of genres. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  select words featuring the target letter-sound combinations (/ ŋ /,/ iː/, -y, st, gl-) in a text, with peers,  practise reading words with the letter-sound combinations, with peers,  engage in timed reading (65 words per minute), observing stress and intonation,  read a short print or digital text featuring words with the target letter-sound combinations expressively and fluently,  practise reading sentences aloud containing non-decodable words with target letter-sound combinations. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce sounds correctly? 2. Why should we read a story at the right speed?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify words related to the theme in a text, b) make predictions and anticipate possible outcomes in a text for comprehension, a) use contextual clues to infer meanings of words, b) answer direct and indirect questions for comprehension, c) adopt retelling a story to check understanding. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe pictures and the title of the text and make predictions on the outcome of the story with peers,  read a printed or digital text related to the theme,  infer the meanings of new words using contextual clues,  respond orally to direct questions based on a text they have read,  locate sentences containing answers to direct questions,  respond to inferential questions using contextual clues,  make connections between the story and their experiences. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we tell what the story is about?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 Simple Past Tense
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Simple Past Tense (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise simple past tense verb forms from texts, b) use simple past tense to discuss past activities, c) realise the use of past tense in everyday communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify simple past tense verbs from print and digital text,  select sentences containing simple past tense from a text or conversation  construct sentences using simple past tense on demonstrated actions and report to peers,  construct sentences from a substitution table with peers and give feedback,  engage in games, involving time and months of the year to change verbs from simple present to simple past tense, with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we talk about what happened in the past? 2. What did you do last week?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.4.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 4.4.1 Handwriting (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise aspects of good handwriting for effective communication, b) write words in clear and legible handwriting, c) form words related to the theme from the target letters, d) realize the importance of writing clearly and legibly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe samples of texts with good handwriting,  identify aspects of good handwriting such as letter formation, spacing, alignment, capitalization  copy letter patterns of the target letter-sound combinations (gl, y),  form words related to the vocabulary learnt from the target letters,  write words related to the theme in response to a picture prompt. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we write words?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons).
