chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Listening to Instructions
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Listening to Instructions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) respond to simple sequenced instructions related to items found in school, b) use verbal and non- verbal cues to give instructions to peers in school, c) embrace the importance of responding to instructions in daily living . SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  role play giving and responding to instructions about greetings in school,  listen attentively to recorded clips on a series of instructions on items found in school,  respond to instructions related to things found in school,  recite simple poems about things found in school,  give instructions to peers using verbal and non-verbal cues,  respond to riddles to identify items found in school,  Audio record themselves as they take and give instructions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to follow instructions?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Picture Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Picture Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify pictures of items found in school for comprehension, b) make predictions on stories before reading to enhance comprehension, c) appreciate the importance of turn-taking as they read for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe thematic pictures of items in school environment collaboratively,  name items in the pictures with peers,  discuss the events in the pictures with peers,  take turns to practice reading pictures of items found in school,  use digital device to access pictures of items found in school,  read pictures on the chart based on the theme,  create a story from a picture with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is found in our school?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Writing Names of Items
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Writing Names of Items. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify names of items found in the school for comprehension, b) write names of items in the school environment in lower case and upper case letters, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe and identify items in the school environment,  draw, name and colour pictures of items found in the school,  write names of the items in lower case and upper case letters as displayed in the chart, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we use lower and upper case letters?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Riddles
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Riddles. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) respond to simple instructions related to school activities, b) solve riddles related to school for information, c) appreciate using riddles in communication for pleasure. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The leaner is guided to:  practice with peers using different verbal and non-verbal cues to respond to instructions about school activities,  use digital devices to find and participate in language games that require following instructions,  Play a game that require learners to listen and respond to instructions, For example: ‘Simon says’  Listen and solve riddles related to school activities with peers,  Create own riddles collaboratively and solve them KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we use riddles in our community?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Read Picture Stories
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Read Picture Stories. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read picture stories about school activities for comprehension, b) create a coherent story about school activities from jumbled pictures for expression, c) appreciate reading picture stories to acquire information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe and relate pictures to what they know about school activities,  read picture stories related to activities done at school with peers,  create a story line collaboratively from sequenced pictures about school activities and read it aloud,  re-organize jumbled pictures to create a story related to school activities,  use audio visual devices to find and interpret picture stories  related to school activities and read them. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we read pictures to tell a story? 2. Why is it important to participate in school activities?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Writing Simple Sentences
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Writing Simple Sentences. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) arrange words in correct order to form simple sentences for communication, b) write simple sentences about SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  Model lower case and upper case letters with peers,  form logical sentences from jumbled words on flashcards,  identify sentences from charts and copy them,  practice writing simple sentences about school activities using KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we use upper and lower- case letters in sentences? 2. Why is it important to arrange words in correct order in a sentence?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Listening to Stories
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Listening to Stories. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) retell a story about domestic animals for expression, b) respond to oral questions based on the story for comprehension, c) develop interest in keeping domestic animals. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a story about domestic animals ,  retell the story listened to with peers,  talk about the importance of domestic animals at home,  imitate characters in the story,  respond to questions on the stories listened to,  role play the story as they record themselves using a digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we listen to stories?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Loud Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Loud Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify key ideas from the text read for comprehension, b) read simple sentences on domestic animals, c) adopt reading of texts for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to :  pick cards from a basket containing simple sentences based on the theme,  read simple sentences in turns,  infer the meaning of vocabulary from a text,  talk about the key ideas from the text with peers,  answer oral questions on the text,  discuss the meaning of the texts read with peers,  Search for simple sentences based on the theme on a digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we read?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Spelling Words
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Spelling Words. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify and spell words related to theme accurately, b) write familiar and unfamiliar words using phonetic knowledge, c) value the importance of correct spelling in writing texts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe a word tree and read the words,  say the letters forming words from the word tree,  copy the words neatly and legibly,  spell and write familiar and unfamiliar words collaboratively,  collaborate with peers to identify spelling errors and correct them,  play spelling games with peers,  complete word puzzles collaboratively. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to spell words correctly?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Self-Expression
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Self-Expression. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the personal hygiene activities in the poem, b) recite a poem on personal hygiene for self- expression, c) recite poems for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to poems on personal hygiene,  select the personal hygiene activities in the poem with peers,  take turns to recite poems on personal hygiene expressively and appreciate one another,  use digital devices collaboratively to record poems based on the theme,  role play hygiene practices. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is personal hygiene important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.1 Loud Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Loud Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read words related to personal hygiene aloud for accuracy, b) use word attack to read sentences about personal hygiene for comprehension, c) develop interest in reading texts correctly and loudly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read words on personal hygiene practices aloud in turns and peer review,  engage in a fishing game, to pick and read words related to personal hygiene from flash cards,  form words based on the theme using sounds,  paint letters in words using different colors,  construct sentences from a substitution table collaboratively,  use digital devices to find the tap and read game and practice reading words related to personal hygiene correctly, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we form words?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Handwriting. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) write sentences with correct spacing between words, b) use upper case and lower case letters appropriately in sentences, c) desire to use clear and legible handwriting. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Learner is guided to:  practice writing sentences with correct pacing between words,  use digital devices to access writing activities and practice joining letters to form meaningful words,  copy letter word and sentence patterns from wall charts,  practice a variety of handwriting activities to improve their writing using upper case and lower case letters collaboratively,  write sentences dictated by the teacher, paying attention to spacing, use of lower case and uppercase letters and legibility. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to write well?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Listening to Instructions
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Listening to Instructions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) respond to simple sequenced instructions on safety at home verbally and non-verbally, b) narrate stories on safety measures at home for expression, c) develop interest in listening and responding to instructions about safety at home. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to :  name some accidents that can happen at home,  attentively listen to instructions on safety at home verbally and non-verbally,  respond to simple instructions on safety at home,  tell stories on safety at home,  role play safety measures on accidents at home,  use digital devices to take videos as they role play. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we follow instructions?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Reading Simple Text
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Reading Simple Text. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read simple texts about safety at home for comprehension, b) respond to oral comprehension questions from the text, c) develop interest in reading texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read simple texts with peers about safety at home,  identify key messages from the text read on safety at home,  use digital devices to access texts on safety at home,  answer comprehension questions on safety at home from texts read,  share key messages from texts read with peers,  role-play safety measures on possible accidents at home. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to observe safety at home?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1 Creative writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: compose simple sentences about safety at home for communication, a) arrange sentences in a sequence to form creative texts for expression, b) appreciate creativity in writing for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe and talk about pictures on home safety with peers,  write simple sentences on home safety,  sequence sentences to form a creative paragraph,  use digital devices collaboratively to type simple sentences about safety at home,  display own work for peer assessment and appreciation. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we write creatively?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Number Concept
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Number Concept (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify numbers 1 to 100 in symbols in different situations, b) represent numbers 1 to 100 using concrete objects from the environment, c) play number games using number cards or digital devices, d) appreciate the use of numbers in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs or groups, recognize and read numbers 1 to 100 from number cards or charts, ● in groups, collect safe concrete objects from the environment, ● in groups, count concrete objects of given numbers in symbols, ● match a group of objects to their number value, ● in groups, discuss, choose and play number games in turns using number cards or digital devices. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we represent numbers using objects?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Whole Numbers
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Whole Numbers (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) count numbers forward up to 100 in different situations, b) count numbers backward from number 50, c) read and write numbers 1 to 100 in symbols in different situations, d) identify the place value of numbers in ones and tens, e) read and write numbers 1 to 20 in words, f) work out missing numbers in number patterns up to 100, g) appreciate number patterns in playing number games. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, count numbers forward up to 100 starting from any point, ● in pairs/groups, count numbers backward from 50 starting from any point, ● in pairs, recognize and read numbers 1 to 100 in symbols from number cards or charts, ● in groups, name and write the numbers in the place value of ones and tens ● in groups, discuss the place value of digits written on the number cards, ● read and write numbers 1 to 20 in words, ● work out missing numbers in number patterns up to 100, ● in pairs or groups, make number patterns and share with other groups, ● play games involving whole numbers using digital devices or other resources, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we get the next number in a number pattern?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Addition
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Addition (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) add a 2 digit number to a 1 digit number without and with regrouping with sum not exceeding 100, b) add a 2 digit number to a 2 digit number without and with regrouping, with sum not exceeding 100, c) add two multiples of 10 whose sum does not exceed 100, d) work out missing numbers in patterns involving addition of whole numbers up to 100, e) appreciate the addition of numbers in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs, write addition sentences given in horizontal form into vertical form according to place value, ● add a 2 digit number to a 1 digit number without regrouping, ● add a 2 digit number to a 1 digit number with regrouping, ● in pairs/groups, discuss and come up with different ways of adding two 2 digit numbers without and with regrouping, ● in pairs/groups, add 2 multiples of ten whose sum does not exceed 100, ● play games involving addition using digital devices or other resources, ● in groups, make patterns using numbers up to 100 and share with other groups. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How are horizontal addition sentences written vertically? 2. When do we regroup during addition?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 Subtraction
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 Subtraction (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) subtract a 1 digit number from a 2 digit number without regrouping, b) subtract a 2 digit number from a 2 digit number without and with regrouping, c) subtract a lower multiple of 10 from a higher multiple of SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● individually or in groups, subtract a 1 digit number from a 2 digit number without regrouping, ● in pairs or groups, subtract a 2 digit number from a 2 digit number without regrouping using place value apparatus, ● in pairs or groups, subtract a 2 digit number from a 2 digit number with regrouping using place value KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you work out missing numbers in number patterns involving subtraction?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.5 Multiplication
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.5 Multiplication (12 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) represent multiplication as repeated addition using numbers 1, 2, 3, by 2 and 3, b) write repeated addition sentences as multiplication using ‘ ’ sign, c) multiply 1 digit numbers by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, d) multiply 1 digit numbers by 10, e) appreciate arranging objects in groups of 3’s, 4’s, 5’s and 10’s in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs or groups, use counters or other concrete objects to represent multiplication as repeated addition, ● in pairs, model multiplication as repeated addition using concrete objects. ● use ‘ ’ sign in writing repeated addition sentences as multiplication, ● in groups, multiply 1 digit numbers by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ● use locally available materials to model a multiplication chart and display in the learning environment, ● in groups, multiply 1 digit numbers by 10 to form multiples of 10, ● play games involving multiplication using digital devices or other resources, ● visit the local market to see how different fruits and other items are arranged in groups of 3's, 4's, 5's or 10's for selling, and assist in KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How is multiplication represented as repeated addition?

chunks.sub_strand: 1.6 Division
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.6 Division (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) represent division as equal sharing up to number 20 by 2, b) represent division as SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in groups, share a given number of objects equally by each picking one object at a time until all the objects are finished. Each learner to count how many objects he/she got, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you share a given number of objects equally?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.7 Fractions
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.7 Fractions (12 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify a as part of a whole in different situations, b) identify a as part of a whole in different situations, c) use fractions in day-to-day activities, d) appreciate the application of fractions in daily life activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs, use papers, pencils and a pair of scissors to make circular paper cut-outs while observing safety, ● in pairs, fold the circular paper cut- outs into two equal parts and identify one of the parts as a half of the whole written as , ● in pairs, make rectangular paper cut-outs and fold them into two equal parts to get a half of a whole written as , ● in pairs, fold circular paper cut-outs to get 4 equal parts and identify one of the parts as a of a whole, ● in pairs, practise making halves and quarters of a whole, ● play games involving fractions using digital devices or other KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we get a fraction from a whole?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Length
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Length (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) measure length using fixed units, b) identify the metre as a unit of measuring length, c) measure length in metres, d) appreciate measuring length using fixed units in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs or groups, use sticks of equal length to measure lengths of different objects and record the measurements, ● in pairs or groups, use sticks of different lengths to measure length, including a 1- metre sticks, ● use locally available materials to make 1- metre sticks and use them to measure the length of various objects within the classroom and record the measurements, ● measure the length of different objects at home, record the measurements and discuss with peers in school. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How is the length of an object measured?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Mass
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Mass (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) measure mass using fixed units, b) identify the kilogram as a unit of measuring mass, c) measure mass of different objects in kilograms, d) appreciate measuring mass using fixed units in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, collect safe materials from the environment for measuring mass, ● in pairs/groups use locally available materials to improvise a beam balance, ● in pairs/groups, use items of the same mass and an improvised beam balance to measure different masses, record and discuss the results, ● in pairs/groups, use an item equivalent to a 1-kilogram mass and a beam balance to measure mass of different objects in kilogram accurately, ● visit a shop or market and assist vendors measure items such as beans, maize, rice, flour using fixed units, for example an empty 1-kilogram container, ● measure the mass of different items in kilograms using a 1 kilogram container, ● play digital games involving mass in kilograms. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to know the mass of an object?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Capacity
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Capacity (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) measure capacity using fixed units, b) identify the litre as a unit of measuring capacity, c) measure capacity in litres, d) appreciate measuring SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups collect containers of different sizes for use in measuring capacity, ● in pairs/groups, use small containers of equal capacity to fill bigger containers of same capacity but different shapes with water, count the number of small containers used to fill the big containers, ● in pairs/groups, use 1 litre containers to fill bigger containers with KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do containers have different capacities? 2. Which commodities can be measured in terms of litres?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Time
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Time (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) relate the months of the year to special occasions, b) recite the number of days in each month of the year, c) read the calendar in terms of day and date, d) measure time using arbitrary units, e) identify the minute and hour hand in clock face, f) read time by the hour from the clock face, g) write time by the hour shown by an analogue and digital clock, h) appreciate keeping time in day-to-day activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, discuss special occasions that take place in different months of the year, ● in pairs/groups, sing songs and rhymes related to the number of days in the months of the year, ● in pairs/groups, discuss how to read, tell and write dates from the calendar. ● in pairs/groups, discuss and relate time by hour using the length of a shadow of an object such as a tree in the environment, ● discuss places where clocks are displayed and how they look, ● observe a clock face and discuss the minute and hour hand, ● discuss how to read, tell and write time by the hour using both the analogue and digital clock, ● discuss the importance of keeping time in different activities. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we tell time?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.5 Money
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.5 Money (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify Kenyan currency coins and notes up to sh.100, b) count the number of sh. 10 and sh. 20 coins in different situations, c) count the number of sh. 50 and sh. 100 notes in different situations, d) add two denominations of money with a sum not exceeding sh. 100, e) use money to buy up to 3 items without balance, f) appreciate the use of money in buying items. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, recognize and sort out Kenyan currency coins and notes up to sh.100, ● in groups, make sh. 10 and sh. 20 coins paper cut-outs, sort and count the number of sh. 10 and sh. 20 coins paper cut-outs, ● in groups, make sh. 50 and sh. 100 notes paper cut-outs, sort and count the number of sh. 50 and sh. 100 notes paper cut-outs, ● add two denominations of money with a sum not exceeding sh. 100, ● in pairs or groups, role play buying up to 3 items without balance from the model shop in the classroom, ● record a video during a role play of classroom shopping activities. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How different are Kenyan currency denominations?

chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Lines
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Geometry. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Lines (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) model straight lines in different ways, b) draw straight lines in different ways, c) model curved lines in different ways, d) draw curved lines in different situations, e) appreciate the use of lines in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs /groups, safely model straight lines using sticks, plasticine or clay or papier mache and strings, ● in pairs /groups, safely model curved lines using plasticine or clay or papier mache and strings, ● individually model straight and curved lines by holding their hands in different ways; upward, horizontal, diagonal, ● draw straight and curved lines on manila papers and books using pencils, crayons and rulers or sticks, ● use digital devices or other resources to draw lines. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How are lines used?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● recognise and name different shapes in the environment (triangles, squares, circles and ovals), ● in pairs or groups, discuss types of lines in different shapes (triangles, squares, circles and ovals) ● in turns, name different shapes of objects or on surfaces in their classroom, ● draw triangles, squares, circles and ovals on manila papers and display in the learning environment, ● in groups, make patterns using triangles, squares, circles and ovals, colour them and share with other groups, ● play games involving pattern making KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can patterns be made using shapes?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Luke 10:30-37 in turns,  watch a video on the story of the Good Samaritan,  role play the story of the Good Samaritan,  mention lessons learnt from the story of the Good Samaritan,  tell how they help people in need,  sing a song about the Good Samaritan. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  picture read Mathew 14:22-33,  discuss why the disciples were frightened (Mathew 14:26) in groups,  watch a video on Jesus walking on water,  draw a picture of Jesus walking on water in groups,  sing a song about Jesus walking on water. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why were the disciples of Jesus frightened?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to:  read Mark 5:35-43 in turns,  retell the story of raising Jairus’ daughter,  write Mark 5:41on a speech bubble and display it in the CRE corner,  watch a video clip on the raising of Jairus daughter,  sing a song on the raising of Jairus’ daughter. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How did the Jairus portray faith in God?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  list in groups the importance of celebrating Easter,  list the activities that take place during Easter celebrations,  share experiences of how they celebrate Easter,  picture read Mathew 28:1-6 in pairs,  write Matthew 28:6 on flash cards and read aloud,  sing songs about Jesus resurrection. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do Christians celebrate Easter?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) narrate the story of Ananias and Sapphira, b) practise honesty by taking offerings given by parents to Church, c) explain the importance of respecting other people’s property, d) desire to exercise honesty in day-to-day life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  picture read the story of Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5:1-11,  watch a video clip about Ananias and Saphira,  mention lessons learnt from the story of Ananias and Sapphira,  in groups sing a song on honesty,  say why they should not use church offerings for other purposes,  in groups role play ways of respecting other people’s properties. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should you practise honesty as a Christian? 2. Why should you respect other people’s property?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  write Psalms 136:1 on flash cards and read it aloud in class,  in pairs tell why they should thank God,  write on flash cards reasons for thanking God, family, friends and teachers,  make cards to thank God and mount them at the CRE corner,  sing songs of thanking God through singing games,  role play in groups various ways of thanking God for family, friends and teachers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you thank God for your family, friends and teachers?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  observe and read pictures of the unforgiving servant (Matthew 18:21-31),  watch a video on the unforgiving servant,  role play the story of the unforgiving servant,  always say, ‘Sorry’ when they wrong others,  write Colossians 3:13 on flash cards and read aloud in turns,  say what to do when wronged KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you forgive others?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  list people they can trust for their own safety,  mention the people to report to in case they are molested or touched inappropriately,  learners to role play, ‘How to behave when confronted by a strangers,  sing the song, “Trust and obey………….”, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you ensure personal safety?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  recite the Lord’s prayer (Mathew 6:9-13),  read the Lord’s prayer from a chart displayed in class,  role play ways of showing respect to God during prayers,  say the Lord’s prayer at home or in church,  sing songs related to the Lord’s prayer. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to pray? 2. How do you show respect to God during prayer?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Acts 2:1-4 in turns,  watch a video clip on the coming of the Holy Spirit,  mention the work of the Holy Spirit in pairs,  read Galatians 5:22 and list the fruit of the Holy Spirit,  draw a tree and write the fruit of the Holy Spirit (love, joy, peace, patience and kindness),  learners to model and label five fruits of the Holy Spirit (love, joy, peace, patience and kindness),  sing songs about the Holy Spirit. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is the Holy Spirit important in the life of a Christian?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter –sound combinations in oral texts, b) pronounce the words with the target letter-sound combinations in preparation for reading, c) use the new words learnt to communicate confidently in various contexts, d) realize the role of listening attentively and speaking clearly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to an oral text with words containing the target –letter sounds combinations as modelled by peers, teacher or audio recording,  point out words with the target sound combinations from a conversation watch videos on conversations with words featuring the target letter- sounds: bl, br, ch, cl,  practise saying words with the target letter-sound combinations, with peers,  play word game with peers involving target sound,  use new words to construct sentences with peers and give feedback to each other,  develop a talking tree using vocabulary learnt. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with target letter- sound combinations in a text, b) read a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) realise the correspondence between spoken words and written words in various contexts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to :  watch a video clip/listens to an audio recording/teacher model of target sounds,  pick out words containing the target letter- sound combinations: bl, br, ch, cl, from a written text,  read words with the target letter–sound combinations from either print or digital stories,  engage in timed reading of a text (90 words per minute) displaying the right emotions and feelings, with peers,  take part in word building activities using pocket charts, print and digital flash cards. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we show emotions when reading a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify characters and setting in a text for comprehension, b) make predictions and anticipate possible outcomes of a story, c) use context clues to infer meanings of words in a text, d) answer simple direct and indirect questions based on a text, e) adopt talking about a text read for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at pictures and title of a text and predict the likely order of events in a story, with peers,  read a print or digital text, related to the theme,  identify the main idea/ topic/ purpose in a text,  discuss the setting and characters in a story, with peers,  respond to direct questions by locating sentences with the answers,  answer indirect questions using prior knowledge of the target theme,  list key words or phrases related to the theme from a grade appropriate text. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1) How can we tell how a story, poem or conversation will end? 2) How can we tell where events have taken place? 3) How can we tell the characters in a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Subject-verb agreement

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise sentences with subject- verb agreement in a text, b) use subject-verb agreement to construct sentences related to the theme, c) realize the role of subject-verb agreement in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to :  read and pick out the target grammar item from a text,  list sentences featuring the grammar items from a text,  construct sentences based on pictures showing singular and plural subjects, with peers,  construct sentences using singular and plural objects at home and at school,  play a language game on subject- verb agreement. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1) What order should words follow in a sentence? 2) What makes a sentence correct?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognize words with the target letter-sound combinations in words and sentences, b) pronounce the target letter- sound combinations in words and sentences, c) use the vocabulary learnt to communicate appropriately in various contexts, d) respond to simple specific three- directional instructions in oral communication, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to the teacher model or an audio recording the target letter- sound combinations (‘dr’, ‘fl’, ‘fr’ and ‘gl’)  pronounce the target letter-sound combinations by taking turns,  listen to and say tongue twisters with the target letter-sound combination,  sing simple songs or recite poems with target letter-sound combinations,  construct simple sentences with peers using the new words and give feedback to each other,  dramatise or role play sharing of KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify words with the target letter sound combinations for ease of reading, b) read a grade- appropriate text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) adopt reading simple, short texts in a variety of genres. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video or listen to an audio clip as teacher or peer models words featuring the target letter-sound combinations- ‘dr’, ‘fl’, ‘fr’ and ‘gl’,  pick out words containing the target letter-sound combinations from a written text,  engage in timed reading of a text displaying appropriate expression, with peers,  read texts of different genres paying attention to punctuation, facials expressions, pace, pitch, and volume individually, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we check our speed while reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify words related to the theme, b) make predictions and anticipate possible outcomes in a story for comprehension, c) use contextual clues to infer meanings of new words, d) answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension, e) adopt the reading texts for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read a printed or digital text and pick out words related to the theme,  look at pictures and title of a text and say what will happen in the story,  infer meanings of new words using contextual clues,  discuss the text with peers and locate sentences containing answers to the direct questions based on the text,  answer inferential questions based on the text read using contextual clues,  make connections between events in the text and real life experiences,  engage in a language game using the vocabulary learnt. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we tell how a story/ poem will end? 2. How can we tell where the events in a story are taking place?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen for the forms of verbs ‘do’ from an audio recording/ video clip or as modelled by the peers or the teacher,  construct sentences related to the theme using the different forms of the verb ‘do.’  recite poems/sing songs about the theme, while using the different forms of the verb ‘do’,with peers,  type sentences formed using the different forms of the verb ‘do’ onto a digital device in pairs,  play a language game with peers using the different forms of the ‘verb to do.’ KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What duties do you like doing? 2. What duties have you done this week?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we write words?

How do we learn new words? 2. Why should we listen attentively?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is reading without hesitation important?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the main idea, topic/purpose of the text for inference, b) retell events in a story to check understanding, c) explain sequence of events in a text, d) realize the importance of reading a variety of texts for information. chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with target letter- sound combinations in preparation for reading, b) read a text related to the theme accurately, at the right speed with expression for fluency, c) realize the role of reading fluency in learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read words with the target letter- sound combinations(‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘thr’), with peers, point out words with target letter-sound combinations from a text,  engage in timed reading (90 words per minute) displaying the right emotions and feelings,  read a text paying attention to punctuation and tone,  read grade appropriate texts related to occupation in the library and share what you have read with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to read fluently?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify characters and setting in a text for comprehension, b) make predictions and anticipate possible outcomes of a story, c) use context clues to infer meanings of new words in a text, d) answer direct and indirect questions based on a text read, e) share what they have read in a text. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at pictures and title of a text and predict the likely order of events in a story, with peers  talk about the setting and characters using a variety of clues, with peers,  infer meanings of new words in a story,  read a story and answer direct question by locating sentences containing the answers,  respond to indirect questions using context clues,  point out the main idea, topic, purpose in a text,  connect events in the story with real- life experiences. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we tell what is going to happen next in a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1 Singular and plurals of irregular nouns
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Singular and plurals of irregular nouns (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify irregular nouns in a print/ digital text, b) use singular and plural forms of irregular nouns to talk about the theme for effective communication, c) realise the importance of irregular nouns in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out irregular nouns and their plural forms from a text,  form plurals of specific words taking the singular and plural forms of irregular nouns with peers,  construct sentences about the theme using the plural forms of irregular nouns, listen to a story/poem and respond to questions based on singular and plural forms of irregular nouns,  recite poems/read texts/sing songs containing plurals of irregular nouns, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we talk about many things?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4.1 Hand writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 5.4.1 Hand writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise aspects of good handwriting for effective communication, b) write words in clear and legible handwriting, c) realise the importance of writing clearly and legibly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at samples of texts with good handwriting,  identify aspects of good handwriting,  copy letter patterns of words with the target letter- sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘thr’),with peers,  listen to a dictation on verbs in the present and past tense and write them,  write words related to the theme in response to a picture prompt,  type words and phrases using digital devices, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we write words in a sentence?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter -sounds combinations in given words correctly, b) pronounce the words with the target letter-sound combinations in preparation for reading, c) use vocabulary words related to the theme in relevant contexts, d) respond to simple specific three- directional instructions SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify and pronounce words with letter- sound combinations sounds: (/dr/, /gr/, /shr/) as modelled by the peers/ teacher/ audio recording,  use words which have the target letter-sound combinations to create sentences, with peers,  recite alliterative words that have the sounds (/dr/, /gr/, /shr/),  listen to audio/video recording of a KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What words do we use to talk about technology? 2. Why is it important to pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letter-sound combinations in a text, b) read a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) realise the importance of reading accurately, at the right speed and with expression for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out words with letter- sound combinations /dr/, /gr/, /shr/, from a chart,  blend target sounds to read words with target letter- sound combinations ,with peers  read words with letters –sound combination correctly,  read a text displaying the right facial expressions and tone,  engage in timed reading with peers taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words,  Participate in reader’s theatre and record what you have read in a personal journal. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION:  How should we read?  What benefits do we get in reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story based on the title and pictures, b) respond to direct and indirect questions to show comprehension, c) adopt reading pictures and texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  predict what will happen after discussing the title and pictures in the story,  infer meanings of new words in a text,  answer direct by locating the sentences with the answers in a story,  respond to indirect questions from a text using prior knowledge,  summarise a story/ poem/conversation and record ,  talk about their own experiences in relation to the story. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do the pictures tell us about the story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words that express future time/actions for effective communication, b) use ‘will’/’shall’ to talk about future time/ events, c) value the role of ‘will’and ‘shall’ in communicating future time/intentions. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  recognise sentences with words that express the future time from a text,  talk about what they plan to do after school to express the future time,  ask and answer questions using words that express future time,with peers,  sing a song/rhyme using ‘will’ and ‘shall’,  listen to story, poem or conversation read by the teacher and respond to questions using ‘will’/’shall’. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What will you and your classmates do at break time?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.4.1 Spelling
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 6.4.1 Spelling (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) spell words with the target letter- sound combinations for effective writing, b) write words related to the target theme appropriately for legibility, c) adopt writing words clearly, legibly and correctly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  spell the words with the letter combinations dr, gr, shr,  fill in a crossword puzzles using words with the target letter sound combinations,  write the words related to the theme from a dictation,  make words related to the theme from jumbled letters,  copy words legibly and correctly from charts/ flash cards,  generate as many words as they can from a set of their names, with peers,  participate in a spelling bee activity with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is the correct spelling words important?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter-sound combinations from an oral text, b) use new words in relevant contexts to talk about safety, c) respond to simple specific three- directional instructions in oral communication, d) realize the importance of listening attentively and correct pronunciation for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guide to:  listen to a text featuring the target letter-sound combinations as modelled by the teacher, peer or from an audio recording,  Pick out and pronounce words or phrases with the target letter-sound combinations (dw , tw ,nk and sq) from the text,  use words related to the theme to talk about safety,  listen to the vocabulary used in short sentences/ short paragraphs/teacher read aloud stories and practise using it in a language game with peers,  engage in role play on stories KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What words do we use to talk about safety? 2. Why is it important to pronounce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter-sound combinations in a written text, b) read a grade- appropriate text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) adopt the reading of a variety of texts for reading fluency. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to words with the target letter-sound combinations (dw, tw, nk and ‘sq’ )from a digital device or as modeled by the teacher or peer,  identify and pronounce words and phrases with the target letter-sound combinations,  read a text, displaying the right facial expressions and tone when reading,  engage in timed reading a text ( 90 words per minute) taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words,  participate in a readers theatre with peers where you read a text, story or poem related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to read words properly? 2. What helps someone to read fluently?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3.1 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the main idea in a text to show comprehension, b) make predictions about a story based on the title and pictures for comprehension, c) respond to direct and indirect questions to show comprehension, d) adopt reading pictures and texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at pictures and read the title of a story to make predictions of what will happen in the text,  read/ listen to a story from a digital device /as narrated by peers/teacher,  respond to direct and indirect questions from a text in short simple sentences,  get clues from the story read to answer direct and indirect questions,  identify the main idea in a story, poem or conversation on safety, with peers,  talk about their own experiences in relation to the theme and the story. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you think will happen in this story? 2. What do the pictures tell us about the story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4.1 Conjunctions (but, because)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.4 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 7.4.1 Conjunctions (but, because) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the target conjunctions from a written text, b) join phrases using the target conjunctions for effective communication, c) realize the importance of communicating ideas using the conjunctions. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch video clip/role and identify sentences and phrases with the target conjunctions,  use the conjunctions ‘but’ and ‘because’ in sentences,  play a language game featuring the target conjunctions, with peers,  take part in filling in a substitution table joining phrases using the conjunctions ‘but’ and ‘because’ with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: When do we use the words but/because in sentences?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4.1 Spelling
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 7.4.1 Spelling (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise correct spelling of words with the target letter- sound combinations from a written text, b) write compound sentences related to safety using target conjunctions for clarity in communication, c) attempt to write clearly, and legibly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify words with the target letter- sound combinations( dw-, tw-, -nk, and sq-) from a text,  spell 4-6 letter words with the target letter-sound combinations from a dictation,  organise jumbled letters to make 4-6 letter words with the target letter-sound combinations,  spell 4-6 letter words related to the theme, with peers,  copy 4 -6 letter words legibly and correctly,  form words using the target letter-sound combination, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we spell words correctly?

What words do you use to talk about domestic animals? 2. Why is correct pronunciat ion important in speech?

chunks.sub_strand: 8.2.1 Fluency

Why should we read fluently? 2. Why do we pause when we read?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do the pictures tell us about the story? 2. What do you think will happen in the story?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) distinguish sentences with quantifiers in a written text , b) use quantifiers in sentences to talk about care for animals, c) attempt to use quantifiers in sentences to convey different meanings. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify quantifiers as used in a variety of sentences,  ask and answer questions using the quantifiers in sentences,  observe pictures related to the theme and construct sentences using quantifiers, with peers,  generate sentences from a substitution table,  type sentences with quantifier onto a digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Which words do you use to talk about things that can be counted?

chunks.sub_strand: 8.4.1 Spelling
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 8.4.1 Spelling (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) spell words with the target letter-sound combinations for effective writing, b) write words related to the theme clearly and legibly, c) adopt writing words clearly, legibly and correctly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  spell the words with the target letter-sound combinations (-ft, -ct, -lt, -rd),  make words related to the theme from jumbled letters, with peers,  write 4-7 letter words from a dictation,  copy words legibly and correctly,  form words using letters of their names, with peers. chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.3.1 Opposites
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Opposites (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the opposites of different words for effective communication, b) use opposites to construct sentences related to the theme, c) realize the role of opposites in communicating ideas. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify opposites from a group of words in a text,  tell stories about wildlife conservation using the opposites of a variety of words, with peers  construct sentences using the opposites of words related to the theme, with peers,  use opposites to respond to questions from a story, poem or a conversation,  play a language game that involves identifying opposites of different words. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to learn about opposites of words?
