chunks.sub_strand: 10.3.1 Prepositions (next to, around, near, by, along, after, under)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 10.3.1 Prepositions (next to, around, near, by, along, after, under) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify prepositions in a text, b) use prepositions to describe the position, location and direction of things accurately, c) realize use of prepositions to describe the position and location of people, places and things. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  recognise prepositions in relation to positions of different objects in the classroom, at school or home.  listen to and answer oral questions related to prepositions in a story/poems/song,  place objects at different points in relation to the prepositions learnt and ask their peers to use suitable prepositions to locate them,  construct sentences using prepositions in relation to a prompt and give feedback,  sing short songs/rhymes with prepositions,  play language games containing prepositions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Where do you keep different things at home?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.4.1 Punctuation
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 10.4.1 Punctuation (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target punctuation marks in a text, b) use the target punctuation marks correctly in writing, c) adopt the use of punctuation marks in writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify the capital letters, full stops, question marks and exclamation marks from sample writings on wall charts/chalk board/digital or print resources,  practise using the target punctuation marks correctly in written exercises, with peers.  play games that involve placing the target punctuation marks correctly in a text,  write sentences using the target punctuation marks,  engage in role play in which target punctuation marks are used, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which questions do people ask when they have been invited for a festival? 2. How do we write sentences correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter-sound combinations in an oral text, b) pronounce words with the target letter-sound combinations in preparation for reading, c) use new words related to the theme in relevant contexts, d) realise the importance of using the new words in conversations for effective SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners are guide to:  identify and pronounce words and phrases with the target letter- sound combinations as modelled by the peers/ teacher or audio recording:-nkl, -pt,- nth, -nd,  listen to the new words in short sentences/ short paragraphs/ teacher read aloud stories and give their meanings,  construct sentences using the new words to talk about play time and games,  practise the new words in KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What can we tell from people’s faces and hand movements as they talk? 2. What words do you use to talk about playtime and sports?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.2.2 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 11.2.2 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letter-sound combinations in preparation for reading in a written text, b) read a grade- appropriate text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) adopt reading simple short narratives for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out and read aloud words with the target letter-sound combinations: -nkl, -pt,-nth, -nd from a text,  read words with letter –sound combinations correctly,  read a text, displaying the right facial expressions and tone when reading,  engage in timed reading taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks as they read a text,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words,  participate in a readers theatre with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What makes it easy to read well? 2. What helps someone to read fluently?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 11.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story based on the title and picture, b) infer meanings of new words using contextual clues, c) respond to direct and indirect questions from a text for comprehension, d) summarise information from a text for comprehension, e) adopt reading pictures and texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at the story title and pictures and guess what will happen in the story,  get meanings of new words using contextual clues,  respond to direct and indirect questions from a text,  retell a story, poem or conversation based on the theme with peers,  summarise the story read in one sentence.  talk about their own experiences in relation to the story.  role play scenarios in a story. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you think will happen in the story? 2. What do you think we shall learn from the story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.3.1 Comparatives and superlatives (-er and –est)
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 11.3.1 Comparatives and superlatives (-er and –est) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise comparatives and superlatives used to describe people and things from a text, b) use comparatives and superlatives for effective communication, c) realise the importance using comparatives and superlatives to describe people, things and places. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read a story/ poem/conversation from a text book or a digital device and identify comparatives and superlatives,  identify comparatives and superlatives used in varied sentences,  talk about objects/people using superlatives and comparatives,  construct sentences using comparatives and superlatives with peers,  role play a scenario related to the theme using compratives and superlatives,  play a language game that require the use of comparative and superlatives. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Which words can we use when comparing ourselves with others?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.4.1 Guided Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 11.4.1 Guided Writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the names of the objects in pictures related to the theme, b) write names from picture prompts to demonstrate mastery of vocabulary, c) realize the importance of writing correctly SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  name different objects in pictures provided.  respond to the prompts presented and write names of objects,  draw, colour and name the objects related to the theme, with peers,  fill in gaps using the correct words,  match pictures with their names. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to correctly write names of objects?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.1.1 Punctuation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 12.1.1 Punctuation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target letter -sound combinations in given words for effective communication, b) pronounce words with the target letter-sound combinations in preparation for reading, c) articulate vocabulary related to the theme correctly, d) use vocabulary related to the theme in relevant contexts, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen attentively for the target letter sounds combinations (gr- pr- , -ew’) in different words from an audio recording,  say words with the target letter sound combination and record using digital devices,  listen to the new words in short sentences/ short paragraphs/ teacher read aloud stories and give their meaning,  practise new words in response to picture cues,  dramarise scenarios using the vocabulary words to talk about technology KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we listen attentively when other people are talking?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 12.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letter -sound combinations correctly, b) read a variety of texts containing words related to the theme accurately ,at the right speed and correct expression, c) adopt reading grade -level texts in a variety of genres. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out words with the target letter-sound combination (gr- pr-, -ew) from print or digital stories,  read words with the target letter-sound combination,  read a text, display the right facial expressions and voice when reading,  engage in a timed reading taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks when reading the text,  play a word ladder game involving pronunciation from audio/visual recording of words learnt.  participate in and record a readers theatre where he or she reads from a text. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we need to pronounnce words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.2.1 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 12.2.1 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions on the outcomes of a story based on the theme, b) identify events in a text for comprehension, c) infer the meanings of new words as used in the text, d) answer direct and indirect questions based on a text, e) acknowledge the importance of the information they have read in the text SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at pictures and title of a text and say what will happen in the story ,with peers,  talk about events in a story ,  talk about the setting and the characters using picture clues,  find the meaning of new words as used in a text,  read the text and answer direct and indirect questions,  retell the story, with peers KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we tell where events have taken place in a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.3.1 Possessive pronouns
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 12.3.1 Possessive pronouns (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify sentences featuring possessive pronouns in a text, b) use possessive pronouns correctly in writing, c) realize the use of possessive pronouns in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  talk about the things that belong to them/ their parents/guardians, using possessive pronouns (mine, yours, ours, hers, his),  role play ownership of items and objects in the classroom, with peers,  construct sentences related to the theme using possessive pronouns, with peers,  ask and answer questions using the possessive pronouns,  sing songs/rhymes using the possessive pronouns,  play language games involving use of possessives. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you talk about things that belong to you / other people?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.4.1 Paragraphs
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 12.4.1 Paragraphs (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the general idea in jumbled sentences, b) write the sentences sequentially to form a paragraph, c) advocate for the role of writing as a part of the learning process. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  study the jumbled sentences to establish the idea in each  discuss the main idea conveyed in the jumbled words,  explore various possibilities with peers to get the correct order of the jumbled sentences,  re-write the jumbled sentences according to the correct order. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to put sentences in the correct order when writing?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 13.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) distinguish words with the target letter-sound combinations for effective communication, b) pronounce words with the target letter-sound combinations accurately, c) identify vocabulary related to the theme correctly, d) use the new words related to the theme in short sentences, e) value the importance of using proper pronunciation and correct vocabulary in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen and pick out words with the target letter sound combinations(-lf, - rf, spl-) from an audio clip/ poem/ story,  practise saying words with the target sounds with peers,  generate and list words with the target sounds,  categorise different words according to each of the target sounds,  use new words to construct of sentences,  engage in role plays and use words related to the theme, with peers,  recite rhymes/sing songs which contain vocabulary related to the theme, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we use sounds to learn new words?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 13.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify words with the target letter-sound combinations in a text, b) read a grade-appropriate text accurately, at the right speed and with expressions, c) adopt reading fluently for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  pick out words with letter- sound combinations : (-lf, -rf, spl-) from a text,  read words with letters –sound combination correctly,  engage in timed reading of a text with minimal hesitations, displaying the right facial expressions and voice,  take appropriate pauses at punctuation marks as they read a text,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words,  participate in reading a text in readers’ theatre with peers and record on a digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to read at the right speed?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 13.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story based on the title and pictures, b) respond to direct and indirect questions about the text to show comprehension, c) summarise a text for comprehension, d) adopt reading texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  look at the title of the story, pictures and guess what will happen in the story,  locste sentences in the tet to answer direct questions,  get clues from the story to answer indirect questions,  summarise a story, poem or conversation using a concept map with peers,  participate in a ‘five finger retell’ activity,  talk about their own experiences in relation to the story. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do pictures and the title of a story help us to know what will happen in the story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.3.1 ‘Wh’ questions (why, whom, how)
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 13.3.1 ‘Wh’ questions (why, whom, how) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify sentences containing Wh- questions from a text, b) use Wh- questions in sentences for effective communication, c) realize the role of WH- questions in seeking information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to recorded conversations containing the Wh- questions,  identify sentences containing Wh- questions,  engage in meaningful question and answer dialogues using of ‘why’, ‘whom’ and ‘how’ in with peers,  role play activities that lead to the use of of ‘why’, ‘whom’ and ‘how’,with peers,  answer questions of ‘why’, ‘whom’ and ‘how’ appropriately,  sing/recite short poems to practice the use of ‘why’, ‘whom’ and ‘how’. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to ask questions correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.4.1 Guided writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 13.4.1 Guided writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words related to the theme from a written text, b) write simple paragraphs related to the theme clearly, c) realize the importance of writing simple paragraphs for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out various words related to the theme from a text,  write 3-5 simple short and correct meaningful sentences in response to a prompt,  list the sentences logically in preparation for writing, with peers,  write simple sentences to form a paragraph,  use the five steps of the writing process: planning, drafting, revising, editing and writing the final piece. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we write sentences correctly? 2. How do we form a paragraph?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise words with the target letter- sound combinations in a text, b) pronounce words with the target letter- sound combinations in preparation for reading, c) use new words related to the theme in relevant contexts, d) realize the importance of listening attentively, and correct pronunciation in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify and pronounce words and phrases with the target letter-sound combinations (spr and str’) as modelled by the peers/ teacher or audio recording,  use words which have the target letter combinations to talk about talent,  practise using vocabulary related to the theme in short sentences,  recite rhymes/sing songs with peers using the vocabulary related to the theme,  play language games matching vocabulary learnt to pictures and objects, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What words do you use to talk about talents? 2. What helps us to remember the meaning of words?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 14.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letter-sound combinations in a text, b) read a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, c) adopt reading simple, short narratives for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out and read words with taget letter-sound combinations (spr and str’) from a text,  read words with letter–sound combinations correctly,  read a text, display the right facial expressions and tone,  engage in timed with peers reading taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks,  practise reading sentences containing decodable and non- decodable words.. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What makes it easy to read well?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 14.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make predictions about a story based on the title and picture, b) identify the main idea in a text for comprehension, c) infer meanings of new words from the context, d) respond to direct and indirect questions on a text for comprehension, e) adopt reading texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The earner is guided to:  predict what will happen in a story after discussing the title and pictures with peers,  identify the main idea in a text, with peers,  use contextual clues to get meanings of new words,  respond to direct and indirect questions from a text using contextual clues,  talk about own experiences in relation to a story, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do pictures tell us about a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.3.1 Adverbs of manner
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.3 Language use. SUB-STRAND: 14.3.1 Adverbs of manner (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify adverbs of manner in a written text in preparation for writing, b) use adverbs of manner to describe actions, c) realize the use of adverbs in writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a descriptive story, poem or conversation read by the teacher or from a digital devices and point out adverbs,  construct simple sentences about talents using verbs matched to adverbs of manner,  role play familiar situations using given verbs, with peers and describe the actions using adverbs of manner appropriately,  make sentences from a substitution table,  take part in language games that allow turn taking while using adverbs of manner. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which words do you use to talk about how things are done? 2. Why is it important to clearly describe how something is done?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 14.4.1 Guided writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 14.1 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 14.4.1 Guided writing (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the steps of composition writing in preparation for writing, b) write a short narrative related to the theme following the five steps of the writing process, c) realize the importance of correctly writing simple paragraphs for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  pick out new words from a text,  write words picked correctly and legibly,  write 3-5 meaningful sentences using the new words in response to a prompt,  write own paragraphs of 3-5 sentences using the steps in the writing process,  write simple guided composition of about 5-10 sentences,  use the five steps of the writing process: planning, drafting, revising, editing and writing the final piece. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we plan before writing a composition?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 15.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise the target letter- sound combinations from a text, b) identify words related to the theme from an oral text, c) engage in meaningful conversations using new words, d) realize the importance of proper pronunciation and SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify words with the target letter-sound combinations (‘scr-, ‘que-’) from a list,  practise saying words with the target letter- sound combinations with peers,  listen to peers for correctness of pronunciation of the the target letter- sound combinations,  explore the other sounds that can combine with target sounds to make new words, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we use sounds learnt to make new words?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.2.1 Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 15.2.1 Fluency (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words with the target letter-sound combinations in a text, b) articulate words with the target letter-sound combinations for clarity of meaning, c) read a text accurately, at the right speed and with expression, d) adopt reading simple, short narratives for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  select words with the target letter- sound combinations (‘scr’ and ‘que’) from a print or digital text,  pronounce words with the target letter- sound combinations,  take part in timed reading, with peers,  read narratives/poem / dialogue paying attention to pace, pitch and volume. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to read words accurately? 2. What makes it easy to read well?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.2.2 Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 15.2.2 Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) predict the outcome of a story based on available clues, b) identify the order of events or information in a text for comprehension, c) infer the meanings of new words and phrases from the context, d) answer direct and indirect questions based on a text, e) adopt reading texts for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  predict what will happen in a story, based on pictures and title of a text, with peers,  read a print or non-print story aloud,  talk about the setting and characters in a story,  discuss the plot of a story with peers,  use context clues to find the meanings of words,  locate sentences containing answers to direct questions,  answer indirect questions using contextual clues,  retell a story read, with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we get the meaning of new words in a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.3.1 Interjections of displeasure
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.3 Language Use. SUB-STRAND: 15.3.1 Interjections of displeasure (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words that are often used to express displeasure, b) use words that express displeasure appropriately, c) value the role of interjections in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a descriptive story, poem or conversation read by the teacher or from a digital device and identify interjections of displeasure,  role play situations of displeasure and use the appropriate expressions/ words,  construct sentences using interjections of displeasure,  take part in a language game that allows turn taking while using interjections of displeasure. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you show that you are not happy about something?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 15.4.1 Guided Writing (factual paragraph)
chunks.text: STRAND: 15.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 15.4.1 Guided Writing (factual paragraph) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify facts from various processes and contexts in preparation for writing, b) order the factual ideas logically for clarity of communication, c) write a paragraph using factual sentences, d) realize the use of factual texts in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify facts from various processes and contexts collaboratively with peers,  list the facts logically,  make oral presentations of the facts,  select the most appropriate sentences for the pictures,  write simple sentences based on oral presentations of facts to form a paragraph. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we write fluently?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Self- awareness Scriptural stories Story of Hanuman ji Mai Bhago ji
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Self- awareness Scriptural stories Story of Hanuman ji Mai Bhago ji. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) state qualities of themselves for self-awareness, b) interpret love and care for self and others for peaceful co- existence, c) acknowledge oneself and others as part of Paramatma’s creation. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to Scriptural stories on self-awareness, ● discuss in groups the aspects of self-awareness from the Scriptural stories, ● discuss qualities that make their bodies the temple of Paramatma. ● share what they like about themselves and write short sentences in respect of each other,. ● role play in pairs/groups to demonstrate love and care for each other in a responsible manner, ● draw themselves, colour their drawings and display them in class, ● Assist peers with special needs to role-play in age-appropriate activities that help to enhance self-awareness in them. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to respect oneself?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Panchmahabhoot Akash (Sky/Space)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Panchmahabhoot Akash (Sky/Space). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Name celestial bodies in Akash(space/sk y) as part of Paramatma’s creation, b) Illustrate the elements of Panchmahabho ot for better understanding, c) Appreciate the celestial bodies in Akash(sky) as part of Paramatma’s creation. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● Use digital devices to watch videos/animations of celestial bodies and share their observations. ● Research on the following celestial bodies and make observations in the sky on Sun, Moon, Stars, Jupiter, Saturn, Constellations. ● Draw and colouring the celestial bodies. ● Research on the following elements of Panchmahabhoot and present in class; Sky, wind/air, sun, water, earth. ● Create an observation journal for observing heavenly bodies across the month and report back to class at the end of the month using digital devices. ● Prepare a sky observation KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does the sky change throughout the day and across different seasons?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Mention qualities of the selected Enlightened Beings for spiritual nourishment, b) Relate the qualities of the selected Enlightened Beings to solutions to daily challenges in school, c) Nurture virtues associated with enlightened beings in their SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● Use digital devices to view and watch pictures/flashcards/videos, ● Read and discuss qualities in the stories from the lives of above- mentioned Enlightened Beings and present in class, ● Role play the qualities of Enlightened Beings as solutions to daily challenges experienced in school, ● sing songs that glorify the qualities of the Enlightened Beings, ● crossmatch the qualities of the Enlightened Beings with the respective faiths, ● visit places of worship to learn from resource persons the qualities and relevance of enlightened Beings in their daily life, ● write a simple composition on 3 qualities from the Enlightened Beings, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to learn about Enlightened Beings? 2. How do stories and teachings about Enlightened Beings inspire us to be better?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How are religious symbols important to the devotees?

chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Scriptures. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Basic Concepts -Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) list four main concepts of the selected Scripture for understanding, b) interpret the main concepts of the Scriptures to enhance critical thinking, c) acknowledge the Scripture as a source of divine teaching. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● use digital devices to watch/ listen to audio-visual aids depicting the basic teachings from, ● refer to the learner’s book to study the main concepts in the Scripture, ● discuss main concepts from scripture in groups, ● prepare presentations showcasing the main concepts from the Scripture that addresses a simple challenge in the school, ● use flashcards to list four basic concepts drawn from the selected scripture, ● visit places of worship to learn the basic concepts from a resource person accompanied by the teacher/ parent/ guardian, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to understand the basic concepts of Scriptures?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Handling of Scriptures Ramayan Kalpasutra Dhammapada Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Scriptures. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Handling of Scriptures Ramayan Kalpasutra Dhammapada Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) State protocols for handling the Scriptures for self- efficacy, b) Illustrate the process of handling the Scriptures for reverence, c) acknowledge the importance of handling all Scriptures appropriately. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch and listen to videos / resource persons on appropriate ways of handling the scriptures.  ask parents/ guardians to monitor their practice on how to handle and open the scriptures.  take videos/pictures of adults who are handling the Scriptures appropriately.  visit places of worship and engage with a resource person to learn about the handling of Scriptures in the four faiths.  roleplay the appropriate handling of Scriptures.  engage in group discussions about the handling of Scriptures.  Assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the protocols for handling Scriptures. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should Scriptures be handled with reverence and respect?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Moral Stories
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Scriptures. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Moral Stories. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify short stories on morals from the selected Scriptures for inspiration, b) narrate short stories from the selected Scriptures for righteousness, c) appreciate moral stories from the Scriptures for spiritual development. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read short stories from selected scriptures and discuss in groups to identify the morals,  listen to moral stories from peers / teachers / resource persons from Scriptures,  use digital devices to watch/listen to videos/audio recordings of short stories adapted from the Scriptures in groups,  Discuss the moral lessons drawn from the short stories.  Narrate short stories with moral teachings learnt from Scriptures.  Practice morals learnt from Scriptural stories they have encountered in daily life,  Assist learners with special needs as per their abilities through peer teaching to make them understand the lessons drawn from the short stories KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do moral stories influence communal living? 2. How can moral stories from Scriptures improve our lives?

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Worship. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Daily Religious Practices Mantras Japa Dhyan Prayer. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) list the benefits of daily religious practices in their life, b) demonstrate religious practices observed at home for spiritual growth, c) desire to engage in religious practice in their daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● Use digital devices to watch/listen to resource person giving a discourse on the benefits of daily religious practices and take notes, ● discuss with parents the importance of daily religious practice, ● engage in group discussions on the benefits of religious practices, ● Visit places of worship under the guidance of their parents to identify religious practices that are age-appropriate, ● draw charts to showcase religious practices and their benefits. display the charts in class, ● prepare a journal to track their daily religious practice. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do performing daily religious practices help us in our life? 2. Why is it important to observe religious practices at community level

chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Religious and Cultural Festivals Raksha Bandhan Uttarayan, Vaisakhi, Holi, Vesak, Holla Mohalla
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Worship. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Religious and Cultural Festivals Raksha Bandhan Uttarayan, Vaisakhi, Holi, Vesak, Holla Mohalla. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) enumerate celebrated religious and cultural festivals for familiarisation, b) interpret the celebration of religious and cultural festivals for social cohesion, c) acknowledge religious and cultural festivals harmonious living. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch the celebrations on different cultural festivals using digital devices, ● discuss in groups about religious and cultural festivals, ● share in groups the names given to those festivals, ● plan a visit to observe simple religious rituals at places of worship in the company of parent/guardian/ teacher, ● participate in the celebration of the religious and cultural festivals. ● make a collage to represent the identified religious and cultural festival and prepare a portfolio. ● tell short stories in pairs about the significance of the cultural festivals, ● Sensitize their peers with special needs about the safety measures to be observed during celebration of festivals. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do religious and cultural festivals foster harmony in society?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to stories using digital devices on general etiquette focusing on ● practise general etiquette by roleplaying ways of expressing apology/forgiveness/ kindness/gratitude in daily life. ● select from the talking walls/quotes/flashcard words of apology, forgiveness and gratitude. ● prepare personal charts on words expressing general etiquette such as forgiveness/humility/ kindness/ gratitude and share in class. ● make cards in pairs to show the ways of apologising and forgiving/requesting and thanking others and share the KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to practise general etiquette?

chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Sadachaar. SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Role of Etiquettes. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) mention the roles of etiquette at home, school and places of worship, b) demonstrate general etiquettes at home, school and places of worship, c) appreciate the role of general etiquette at school homes and places of worship. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● name various etiquette that are practice at home.school and places of worship, ● watch a short video at home, school and places of worship using a digital device as they observe general etiquette, ● discuss in groups the importance of Etiquette, ● role play in group general etiquette in class as they are guided by the teacher, ● recite a poem on the importance of etiquette, ● compose songs on general etiquette and sing in the class with the guidance of their teacher, ● assist peers with special needs to roleplay on general etiquette as per their ability to perform. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to practise etiquette in our daily lives? 2. How does etiquette enhance wellbeing both at school and at home?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (HRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1 Pranayama (Breathing Exercises)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 Yoga. SUB-STRAND: 6.1 Pranayama (Breathing Exercises). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) sate the importance of Pranayama in promoting physical and mental well- being, b) display Pranayama to promote calmness and emotional well- being, c) appreciate the practice of Pranayama for personal well-being. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  mention importance of Pranayama that they are familiar with,  use digital devices/ consult their parents or guardians to gather information on the performance of pranayama and its benefits,  discuss in groups the findings on pranayama,  demonstrate Pranayama to promote calmness and emotional well-being,  watch and listen to a video on the performance of Bhramari and Bhastrika,  practise the performance of Bhramari and Bhastrika under the instruction of an expert,  prepare a schedule for systematic practice of Bhramari and Bhastrika KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How is normal breathing different from Pranayama? 2. How does regular practice of pranayama benefit us?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  use digital devices/ parent/ guardian/ teacher to gather information on the importance of Asana,  discuss in groups the benefits of Asanas for the body wellbeing,  watch and listen to an instructional video / yoga expert on the performance of Surya Namaskar.  practise Surya Namaskar correctly in groups.  demonstrate Surya Namaskar for self-efficacy  prepare a schedule for systematic practice of basic Asanas with the help of a parent/ guardian/ instructor,  visit a yoga training centre accompanied by a parent KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does Asanas contribute to our physical well- being?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  use digital devices/ parent/ guardian/ instructor to gather information on the observance of basic meditation and its benefits in life,  discuss in groups the findings on the benefits of basic meditation,  watch and/ listen to a video on the performance of basic and age-appropriate meditation,  follow basic instructions for meditation on the breath (Anapana Sati),  share their experiences of basic meditation on the breath (Anapana Sati) in groups,  prepare a schedule for systematic practice of basic meditation in the company of a parent/ guardian/ instructor, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should young learners practise meditation regularly?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Imitation of expressions
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Imitation of expressions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify simple expressions used when introducing self and others, b) respond to questions using expressions appropriately for comprehension, c) appreciate using expressions to introduce self and others. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  collaborate with peers to listen to recorded clips on introducing self and others,  identify instances when they have to introduce self or others,  introduce self and others formally to peers in class,  listen to conversations from a radio lesson about the importance of introducing self and others,  respond to questions from the radio lesson with peers,  take turns to describe thematic pictures to tell a story on introducing self and others,  role play a short skit where they introduce themselves and their friends to others,  conduct a peer review to help each other improve on their introductions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to introduce self and others?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Independent Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Independent Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the main idea in a simple passage on the theme for comprehension, b) read supplementary readers related to the theme SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  skim and scan for information from simple texts,  read a passage and supplementary readers to pick out main ideas,  with peers practice identifying the main idea in passages and give peer review,  read level readers, independently and answer questions collaboratively,  search for short paragraphs on the theme from digital platforms,  identify vocabulary from a text and infer their meaning, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the benefits of reading on your own? 2. How do you identify the main idea from a passage?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Sentence Formation
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Sentence Formation. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) arrange words to form sentences based on the theme for expression, b) write simple sentences based on the theme for communication, c) enjoy forming sentences correctly for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  collaborate to identify words related to introducing self and others from charts,  use thematic words to form simple sentences about introducing self,  team up to arrange word cards to form simple sentences about introducing self and others,  Form sentences using words in the flash cards,  use digital devices to find ‘drag and drop’ games to re-arrange jumbled sentences to form correct sentences on introducing self and others,  participate in fishing games to fish and arrange word cards and form simple sentences about introducing self and others with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we arrange words to form sentences?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Stories
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Stories. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words related to the types of occupations in the community, b) respond to questions about characters from a story for comprehension, c) use creative words and expressions to tell a story on occupations in the community, d) develop interest in story telling for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  team up to listen to stories related to occupations in the community from recorded clips, guest speaker or teacher,  identify words related to types of occupations and characters used in the story,  take turns to listen to stories on the occupations in the community,  respond to questions from the story  use creative words and expressions to retell stories in correct sequence,  with peers, use digital devices to find stories on occupations in the community,  recreate and retell them using creative words and expressions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why are occupations important? 2. How do we tell stories in sequence?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Writing Simple Stories
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Writing Simple Stories. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) spell thematic words in sentences correctly for accuracy, b) Write texts legibly using correct spacing and shaping of letters for effective communication, c) develop interest in writing simple stories about topical issues SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  Trace and model letters correctly,  Team up to write legibly using correct spacing and shaping of letters and peer review,  read a simple story and identify main ideas.  write words from a dictation provided by the teacher,  use the words to write simple stories about occupations in the community, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is the importance of spacing words when writing? 2. Why is it important to spell words correctly? 3. How do we use connecting words in sentences?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Presentation skills
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Presentation skills. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify skills used during presentations for effective communication, b) make a presentation using audience awareness skills for communication, c) embrace the importance of presentation skills in oral communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to each other’s presentations about wild animals,  identify presentation skills that have been used and give peer review,  practice presenting the short notes confidently and in sequence,  team up to talk about types of wild animals using correct articulation and voice projection and give peer review,  listen to a resource person, audio/visual clips, on riddles,  use digital devices to record themselves as they pose and respond to riddles and give feedback. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to know your audience when making a presentation?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Reading comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Reading comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) create personal collections of thematic words from texts on wild animals for reading, b) respond to questions from passages about types of wild animals for comprehension, c) embrace reading for comprehension texts for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  practice locating thematic words from texts and creating personal word banks,  team up to read short passages and respond to comprehension questions,  work with peers to practice reading texts on wild animals accurately and fluently, and give peer review,  make personal opinions about stories read on wild animals,  team up to identify favourite animals and give personal opinion.  read texts to identify thematic vocabulary and use them to construct sentences,  manipulate and use digital devices to identify texts and read. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to read texts fluently and accurately? 2. How do we read texts with understanding to give personal opinions?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Spelling Instruction
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Spelling Instruction. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) spell words in sentences about wild animals for accuracy, b) write short passages on wild animals using correct spelling, c) Value the importance of SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  team up to brainstorm on new words related to wild animals and practice spelling them correctly,  write sentences and short paragraphs legibly with correct spelling,  sort words related to wild animals into well spelt and misspelt words and make corrections collaboratively,  Manipulate digital devices to engage in spelling games and give peer review,  participate in class language games to KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to spell words correctly? 2. How does spelling of words influence comprehension of written texts?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Active listening
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Active listening. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) listen actively to identify the main idea from aural texts on road safety, b) respond to comprehension questions from oral passages on road safety, c) desire to develop active listening skills for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  observe pictures about road safety and talk about them with peers.  listen actively to comprehension passages and identify main ideas on road safety.  use digital devices to listen to recorded clips based on the theme,  respond to comprehension questions from a passage on road safety,  practice sharing personal experiences related to road safety,  manipulate digital devices to record each other as they share own experiences with others,  recite poems based on the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we observe road safety?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.1 Reading for fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Reading for fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify road safety measures from a comprehension passage, b) read a passage on road safety at correct speed for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe road signs pictures on charts and interpret them with peers,  read a comprehension passage based on the theme and answer questions,  read a paragraph in correct speed in turns,  Identify road safety measures from the passage,  conduct readers theatre for fluency KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we identify specific information from texts?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 Writing to give Information
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Writing to give Information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) create a paragraph on road safety using appropriate punctuation, b) write a text legibly and neatly for effective communication, c) value the importance of writing effectively to give information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to :  with peers observe displayed thematic sentences to correct the punctuation errors,  write sentences in upper case and lower case letters,  compete and challenge peers to write sentences legibly and neatly,  work collaboratively to create short paragraphs of a story using punctuation marks (capitalization, commas, full stop) and give peer review,  engage in a fishing game to practice combining short sentences to create a paragraph about road safety in logical sequence,  type in sentences on digital devices with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the role of punctuation in writing?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1Expressing Self Creatively
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1Expressing Self Creatively. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) respond to questions about seasons of the year for expression, b) make a presentation on activities carried out during different seasons of the year for comprehension, c) show interest in listening to texts for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to oral texts about seasons of the year,  listen to a guest speaker presentation on different seasons of the year,  answer oral questions based on oral texts listened to,  sings songs on seasons of the year with peers,  discuss and role play activities carried out in different seasons of the year in sequence,  sequentially present short narrations on activities carried out in different seasons of the year,  use digital devices to record peers as they make presentations,  play tongue twisters with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we listen to texts? 2. Why is it important to sequence ideas while speaking?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Reading to Acquire Information
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Reading to Acquire Information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a simple text about seasons and activities of the year with accuracy, b) give the meaning of sayings used in texts on seasons of the year for information, c) develop an interest for reading simple texts for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  observe pictures based on the theme with peers and talk about them,  conduct a reading theatre on texts based on the theme and answer comprehension questions,  infer meaning of vocabulary in contexts,  identify sayings in the text with peers,  take turns to explain the meaning of sayings used in the text related to the theme,  use digital devices to find information about seasons and activities of the year. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What materials do we read for enjoyment? 2. Why is it important to explain the meaning of sayings in context?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Selected Surah Al- Masad (read, recite, and memorise)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Qur’an. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Selected Surah Al- Masad (read, recite, and memorise) (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) read Surah Al- Masad correctly for application, b) memorise Surah Al- Masad in preparation for day-to-day life, c) appreciate Surah Al- Masad for spiritual nourishment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to Surah Al- Masad from the teacher/resource person/digital device/peer and repeat after him/her, ● take turns to recite Surah Al- Masad repeatedly and correct each other to enhance memorization, ● use cards with words to fill in gaps to complete verses in Surah Al- Masad, ● sort and arrange the verses of Surah Al- Masad from pocket boards then read them. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the benefits of learning Surah Al- Masad?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen Surah An-Nasr from the teacher/resource person/digital device/peer and repeat after him/her, ● take turns to recite Surah An-Nasr repeatedly and correct each other to enhance memorization, ● use cards with words to fill in gaps to complete verses in Surah An-Nasr, ● sort and arrange the verses of Surah An- Nasr from pocket boards then read it. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the benefits of learning Surah An- Nasr?

chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Hadith on Ihsan
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Hadith on Ihsan (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) read the Hadith on Ihsan for spiritual nourishment, b) apply the teachings of the Hadith on Ihsan to strengthen ones’ consciousness of Allah (SWT) c) appreciate the Hadith on Ihsan as a way of SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read the Hadith on Ihsan from digital devices/flipcharts/manila paper/chart/PowerPoint.  “...To worship Allah (SWT) as if you see Him for if you do not see Him He sees you.”  take turns to recite the Hadith on Ihsaan and correct one another,  listen to short stories depicting Ihsan and news tell in class,  share personal experiences where they practised Ihsaan, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should a Muslim worship Allah (SWT) as if he/she sees Him?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Hadith on Respect
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Hadith on Respect (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) read the Hadith on respect for spiritual nourishment, b) apply the teachings of the Hadith on respect to strengthen ones’ consciousness of Allah (SWT) (SWT), c) appreciate the benefit of respect in nurturing harmony in the society. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● read the Hadith on respect from digital devices/flipcharts/manila paper/chart/PowerPoint; ‘He is not among us he who does not show mercy to our young ones and does not respect the elders,’ ● take turn to recite the hadith on respect and correct each other to enhance memorization, ● listen to story on events where respect is depicted and roleplay, ● share experiences where they have practised respect, ● sing qasida/poems on the benefits of the hadith on respect. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How should one behave in the company of elders/parents/teachers?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1. Believe in the Last Day
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.1. Believe in the Last Day (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) give reasons why a Muslim should believe in the Last Day, b) mention the events which will take place during the Last Day, c) appreciate the performance of good deeds in readiness for the Last Day.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2. Believe in His Power (Qadar)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.2. Believe in His Power (Qadar) (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify reasons why a Muslim should believe in Allah’s Power, b) mention the things that show the Power of Allah (SWT) from their immediate environment, c) appreciate the Power of Allah (SWT) as a pillar of Iman. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to the teacher/resource person narrating reasons why a Muslim should believe in the Power of Allah, ● watch video clips on the wonders/powers of Allah (SWT) and narrate what they have observed. ● draw and colour some unique creations of Allah from their immediate environment. ● story tell/role play events which happened to them and manifested the Powers of Allah (SWT), ● pick and sort the things that indicate the powers of Allah (SWT) using flash cards, ● sing/recite qasida/anashid/poems that depict the powers of Allah (SWT). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are some of the unique creations of Allah? 2. Which bounties depict the power of Allah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1 Pillars of Islam Swalah (pillars and phrases used in postures of swalah)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Pillars of Islam Swalah (pillars and phrases used in postures of swalah) (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the pillars of prayers as a basis for validity of swalah, b) name the phrases used in each posture of swalah, c) appreciate the reward related to performing swalah in their daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch a video clips showing the correct pillars in the performance of swalah and phrases used in each posture of swalah (Allahu Akbar, subhana Allah wabihamdihi, sami’a Allah liman hamida, subhana Rabi’a Ala wa bihamdihi, Rabi ghfrili, tashahhud, taslim), ● pick the pillars of swalah (niyyah, qiyam, takbiratul ihram, reciting al-Fatiha, rukuu, raising from rukuu, sujud, siting between the sujud, sitting while reciting the last tashahhud, tashahhud, prayers for Ibrahim, taslim, tumaninah, tartib) from a flashcards and arrange them in sequence, ● role play the performance of swalah, ● self record using a digital device while performing swalah and share with friends. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we perform swalah? 2. What phrases are used while performin g swalah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Pillars of Islam 4.1.2 Postures and phrases in swalah (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the correct phrases for each posture of swalah, b) Recite the phrases for each posture of swalah c) appreciate the correct way of performing swalah by reciting the correct phrases in each posture. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch a videoclips showing the performance of swalah and phrases used in each posture of swalah (takbiratul ihram, subhana Allah wabihamdihi, sami’a Allah liman hamida, subhana Rabi’a Ala wa bihamdihi, Rabi ghfrili, tashahhud, taslim), ● Sort and match the phrases from a flashcard ( takbiratul ihram, subhana Allah wabihamdihi, sami’a Allah liman hamida, subhana Rabi’a Ala wa bihamdihi, Rabi ghfrili, tashahhud, taslim) with correct postures. ● self record using a digital device while saying the phrases for each posture and share with friends. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we perform swalah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1 Islamic etiquette 5.1.1 Manners of entering and leaving the Masjid
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (Moral Teachings). SUB-STRAND: 5.1 Islamic etiquette 5.1.1 Manners of entering and leaving the Masjid (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) state the importance of a mosque in their day to day life, b) demonstrate the appropriate manners when entering and leaving the masjid in day-to-day life, c) appreciate the use of Islamic manners and dua when entering and leaving the masjid as an act of ibadah SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch video clips on how to enter and leave the mosque and then mention what they have observed on the manners of entering and leaving the masjid (for example, recite the dua for entering the mosque, entering on your right foot first, observe silence while in the mosque, leave the mosque on your left foot first, recite the dua for leaving the mosque), ● reciting the dua for entering the mosque (Allahumma ftahly abwaba rahmatik), and the dua for leaving ( Allahumma inna nas aluka min fadhlik) displayed on a chart/PowerPoint, ● pick and arranged words from flashcards to complete the dua for entering and leaving the mosque ● dramatise the manners of entering and leaving the mosque together with the duas. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is a masjid important to a Muslim? 2. What are you not allowed to do while in the masjid

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1 Islamic phrases (HasbunAllah wa ni’imal wakil, La haula wa la Quwwata illa billahi)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (Moral Teachings). SUB-STRAND: 5.1 Islamic phrases (HasbunAllah wa ni’imal wakil, La haula wa la Quwwata illa billahi) (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) state the circumstances under which the selected Islamic phrases are said in their day to day life, b) read the selected Islamic phrases correctly to build reliance on Allah (SWT), c) appreciate the use of the selected Islamic phrases in their day to day experiences. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch a video clip then recite the selected Islamic phrases, (HasbunAllah wa ni’imal wakil; La haula wa la Quwwata illa billahi), ● role play the situations when it’s appropriate to use the selected Islamic phrases, ● turn-take to read the selected Islamic phrases from charts and correct each other, ● use words in flashcards to complete the selected Islamic phrases and read them. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should a Muslim say HasbunAllah wa ni’imal wakil?

chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (Moral Teachings). SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Relationship 5.2.1 care and dua for the sick (4 lessons). chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1 Early life of the prophet (SAW)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 SIIRA (Life History of the Prophet). SUB-STRAND: 6.1 Early life of the prophet (SAW) (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) mention the activities that were carried out by the prophet (S.A.W) during the early stages of his life, b) identify qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W) that can be learnt from his early life, c) appreciate the qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W) in shaping the life of a Muslim. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen from a digital device/teacher/resource person short story of the prophet’s early life (for example, as a shepherd, journey with his uncle to Syria for trade) and retell, ● turn take narrating activities that were carried out by the prophet in his early life- shepherd, merchant, ● pick and read flash cards with the list of the qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W) derived from his early life (for example. hardworking, trustworthy, truthfulness, humble, obedient and patient), ● sing qasidas/poems on the qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W) in his early life. ● draw and colour domestic animals such as camel and goats. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What was the character of the Prophet during his early life?

chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 Islamic Festivals. SUB-STRAND: 7.1 Milad un –Nabii (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) outline the benefits for Miladun Nabii as a way of showing love to the prophet (SAW), b) demonstrate the activities that take place during Miladun Nabii as they learn the life history of the Prophet ( SAW), c) appreciate the qualities of the prophet as brought out by Miladun Nabii. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to peers and watch video clips on qasida in praise of the Prophet (S.A.W) and then sing the qasida, ● discuss the benefits of Miladun Nabii (for example, love and the respect for the prophet (SAW), reminds Muslims of the teachings of the prophet (SAW), teaches the Muslims the birth and life of the prophet (SAW), strengthen unity among Muslims, promotes the noble character of the prophet (SAW) etc), ● mention the qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W), As- Sadiq, Al-Amin, Aadil, Aalim, ● role play the activities that take place during Miladu-Nabi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you celebrate your birthday?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili

chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Maamkuzi na Maagano (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua maamkuzi na maagano mbalimbali yatumiwayo katika jamii, b) kutumia ipasavyo maamkuzi na maagano mbalimbali yatumiwayo katika jamii, c) kuthamini matumizi ya maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua maneno yanayotumiwa katika maamkuzi na maagano (k.v. Umeamkaje? Umeshindaje? Safiri salama, mchana mwema, usiku mwema) kutoka kwenye chati, vitabu, kadi maneno, mti maneno, michoro, picha au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kujadili na wenzake picha, michoro, video n.k. zinazoonyesha vitendo vya maamkuzi na maagano, ● kuigiza maamkuzi na maagano akiwa na wenzake ili kujenga umilisi wa kutumia maneno haya, ● kujadiliana na mzazi au mlezi wake maamkuzi na maagano kutoka kwa jamii yake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unajua maamkuzi na maagano yapi?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, b) kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, c) kutabiri kitakachotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu d) kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu, e) kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya ufahamu ili SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 51- 54 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa (k.v. uzalendo, umoja, undugu, ushirikiano, upendo) akiwa na wenzake,  kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano,  kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akishirikiana na wenzake,  kutabiri ujumbe wa kifungu kwa kutazama picha kwenye kitabu, vifaa vya kidijitali au chati akiwa na wenzake,  kuthibitisha utabiri wake kuhusu hadithi baada ya kuisoma,  kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, unapenda kusoma hadithi za aina gani? 2. Je, ni mambo gani unayoweza kujifunza kutokana na hadithi?

chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Hati Nadhifu (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua mambo yanayozingatiwa kufanikisha hati nadhifu, b) kuandika kifungu cha maneno kati ya 25-30 kwa hati nadhifu, c) kufurahia kuandika kwa hati nadhifu ili kufanikisha mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua mambo mbalimbali yanayozingatiwa kufanikisha hati nadhifu (k.v. muundo wa herufi, nafasi ifaayo kati ya maneno, nafasi zifaazo pambizoni, kutenganisha sentensi ifaavyo, usafi wa nakala ) kutoka kwenye kitabu, chati, vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kunakili kifungu cha maneno yasiyozidi 30 kwa hati nadhifu kutoka kwenye kitabu, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali, ● kuandika kifungu cha maneno yasiyozidi 30 akizingatia hatua za uandishi (k.v. maandalizi, nakala ya kwanza, urekebishaji, nakala safi) na kuwasomea wenzake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unazingatia mambo gani unapoandika kifungu?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni maneno gani unayoyatumia kuwataja wenzako bila kutumia majina yao halisi?
