chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Uandishi wa Insha. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua mambo ya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha, b) kuandika kisa cha kati ya maneno 85-90 kuhusu suala lengwa akizingatia kanuni za uandishi, c) kufurahia uandishi wa visa tofauti ili kuimarisha mawasiliano andishi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa kisa (k.v.wahusika,ujumbe,muundo), ● kusikiliza kisa kikitolewa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha, ● kusoma kielelezo cha insha kwenye kitabu, chati au katika kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kutambua kanuni muhimu za uandishi (k.v. hati nadhifu, maudhui, mtiririko n.k.), ● kuandika kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa na kujadili na wenzake; kisa hiki kifuate hatua tano za uandishi: maandalizi, nakala ya kwanza, urekebishaji, nakala safi na kuwasomea wenzake, ● kumsomea kifungu kisha amwonyeshe mzazi au mlezi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni mambo gani tunazingatia katika uandishi wa insha?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4.1 Ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 7.4.1 Ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika sentensi, b) kutumia ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika sentensi kwa usahihi, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi kutoka kwenye kadi maneno, mti maneno, kapu maneno, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo kuhusu ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au vifaa vya kidijitali na kutambua ukanushaji wa nafsi hiyo, ● kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia ukanushaji wa nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi katika sentensi ● kutunga sentensi akitumia nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi na ukanushaji wake (kwa mfano: yeye anaandika - yeye haandiki), ● kuigiza matumizi ya nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi na ukanushaji akiwa na wenzake, ● kumsomea mzazi au mlezi sentensi za nafsi ya tatu umoja na wingi zilizokanushwa kuashiria vitendo vya watu mbalimbali nyumbani. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unafikiri mwalimu wako alifanya nini jana? Kama hakufanya mambo uliyotaja ungesemaje?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa katika maneno, b) kutamka maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa kwa ufasaha, c) kusoma kifungu kifupi chenye maneno ya sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, d) kufurahia matamshi bora katika mawasiliano SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa (/mbw/,/nd/, /ny/) katika kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno, au kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua silabi lengwa, ● kutamka maneno aliyosikiliza yenye sauti lengwa; atamke na mwalimu na mwishowe atamke akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza kwa makini sentensi zenye maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua sauti lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusikiliza kifungu cha hadithi na kutambua sauti lengwa, ● kusoma kwa sauti kifungu kilicho na sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, ● kujirekodi akisoma hadithi zilizo KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, matamshi bora hukuzwa kwa njia gani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.3.1 Tahajia (Vipindi3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Tahajia (Vipindi3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua tahajia sahihi za maneno katika insha, b) kuandika insha akizingatia tahajia sahihi za maneno, c) kufurahia kutumia tahajia sahihi katika maandishi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua tahajia sahihi za maneno katika uandishi wa insha kwenye kitabu au kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili kuhusu tahajia sahihi ya maneno katika kifungu kitabuni au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kuandika insha akizingatia tahajia sahihi za maneno katika uandishi, ● kurekebisha insha akizingatia tahajia za maneno, ● kumsomea mzazi au mlezi KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kwa nini ni muhimu kuendeleza maneno ipasavyo unapoandika chochote?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 8.4.1 Matumizi ya neno hili na haya (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.4.Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 8.4.1 Matumizi ya neno hili na haya (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua matumizi ya neno hili na haya katika kifungu, b) kutumia neno hili na haya katika kifungu ili kuboresha mawasiliano, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya hili na haya katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua matumizi ya neno hili na haya (k.v. jicho hili – macho haya, jino hili – meno haya n.k.) katika kifungu kwenye chati au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma sentensi zinazoonyesha matumizi ya neno hili na haya katika kifungu akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia neno hili na haya akiwa na wenzake, ● kuandika kifungu kwa kutumia neno hili na haya na kujadili na wenzake ili kukitolea maoni, ● kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu alichokitunga ili akitolee maoni. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni maneno yapi yanayoambatanishwa na maneno hili na haya?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 9.1.1 Mazungumzo (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Mazungumzo (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua suala lengwa linalozungumziwa, b) kuzingatia matamshi bora katika mazungumzo, c) kujieleza kwa ufasaha kuhusu suala lengwa, d) kutumia ishara zifaazo katika mazungumzo, e) kuchangamkia mazungumzo katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua suala lengwa linalozungumziwa kupitia kwa picha kutoka kwenye kitabu, chati, vifaa vya kidijitali pamoja na wenzake, ● kuchukua muda wa kufikiri kuhusu suala la kuzungumzia, ● kupanga mawazo yake kuhusu suala lengwa na kuandaa hoja za kuzungumzia, ● kutamka maneno kwa kuzingatia matamshi yafaayo ya sauti mbalimbali, ● kueleza habari ambayo zinaleta maana na zenye kufuatana vizuri, ● kupandisha na kushusha sauti panapohitajika, ● kutumia ishara mbalimbali zinazohusina na maelezo yake kuhusu suala lengwa, ● kuzungumza na mzazi au mlezi wake akizingatia suala lengwa ili aimarishe mawasiliano KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je,unazingatia nini unapozungumza kuhusu masuala mbalimbali?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 9.2.1 Kusoma kwa ufahamu (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.2. Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 9.2.1 Kusoma kwa ufahamu (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi, b) kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha hadithi, c) kutabiri kitakachotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi kwa kuzingatia picha, d) kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha hadithi, e) kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya hadithi ili kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi kutoka kwenye chati, kadi maneno, mti maneno au kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano, ● kutabiri kitakachotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu kwa kuzingatia picha akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 70- 75 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa akiwa na wenzake, ● kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha hadithi akiwa na wenzake, ● kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha hadithi akiwa na wenzake, ● kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa na kujadili ujumbe. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni mambo yapi unayozingatia unaposoma kifungu chochote?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 9.3.1 Insha ya Masimulizi (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Insha ya Masimulizi (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua mambo ya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha, b) kuandika insha ya masimulizi kati ya maneno 85-90 akizingatia kanuni za uandishi, c) kuchangamkia uandishi wa insha ya masimulizi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kusikiliza masimulizi yakitolewa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au vifaa vya kidijitali, ● kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha ya masimulizi kutoka kwenye masimulizi aliyosikiliza, ● kusoma kielelezo cha insha ya masimulizi kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidijitali kuhusu insha ya masimulizi akiwa na wenzake, ● kutambua mambo muhimu katika uandishi wa insha k.v. mwandiko nadhifu, maudhui, mtiririko katika kielelezo cha insha aliyosoma, ● kuandika kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa; kisa hiki kifuate hatua za uandishi: maandalizi, nakala ya kwanza, urekebishaji, nakala safi na kuwasomea wenzake, ● kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kisa kifupi kuhusu suala lengwa ili akitolee maoni. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, unapenda kusimulia kuhusu nini? 2. Je,kisa ulichowahi kusimuliwa kilikuwa na mafunzo gani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 9.4.1 Matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya, na mbele ya (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 9.4.1 Matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya, na mbele ya (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika kifungu, b) kutumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika sentensi, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika matini, ● kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo unaotumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya kutoka kwa mgeni mwalikwa, mwalimu au vifaa vya kidijitali na kutambua matumizi yazo akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu kilichotumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake, ● kujadili na mwenzake matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya katika kifungu ili kutolea maoni, ● kujaza nafasi ili kukamilisha sentensi zilizotumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake, ● kutunga sentensi akitumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake, ● kuigiza matumizi ya juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya akiwa na wenzake kwa kutumia vitu anavyomiliki k.m; Mboga iko ndani ya gunia,Vitabu viko juu ya rafu, Kitabu kiko ndani ya mkoba, Gari liko mbele ya duka, ● kumtungia mzazi au mlezi wake sentensi kwa kutumia juu ya, ndani ya na mbele ya kwa kuzingatia vitu katika mazingira ya nyumbani. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni maneno yapi unayoweza kutumia kurejelea kitu/mtu aliye mahali fulani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 10.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 10.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa katika maneno na kifungu, b) kutamka maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa kwa ufasaha, c) kutumia maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa ili kufanikisha mawasiliano, d) kufurahia matamshi bora katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa (/mb/, /nz/, /tw/) katika kitabu, kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa yakitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali, ● kutamka maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa (km mboga, mbuzi, mbao, nzuri, mwanafunzi, twende, kutwa, katwa) akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusikiliza kwa makini sentensi zenye maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali na kutambua sauti lengwa akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza kifungu na kutambua sauti lengwa akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma kwa sauti kifungu kifupi kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akiwa na wenzake, ● kujirekodi akisoma kifungu KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni kwa nini tunatumia matamshi bora tunapozungumza?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 10.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 10.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sauti lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi, b) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, c) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kwa sauti inayosikika, d) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo, e) kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo, d) kuchangamkia kusoma kwa ufasaha ili kufanikisha mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua sauti lengwa (/mb/, /nz/,/tw/) katika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye maneno ya sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye maneno ya sauti lengwa kwa sauti inayosikika akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye maneno ya sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 55 kwa dakika na kwa kuzingatia viakifishi), ● kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo akiwa na wenzake , ● kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa akizingatia matamshi bora,sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara zifaazo. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kwa nini ni muhimu kusoma kifungu kwa ufasaha?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 10.3.1 Insha ya Maelezo (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 10.3.1 Insha ya Maelezo (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua vipengele vinavyozingatiwa katika uandishi wa insha ya maelezo, b) kuandika insha ya maelezo kati ya maneno 85-90 akizingatia kanuni za uandishi, c) kuchangamkia kuandika insha ya maelezo ipasavyo ili kuimarisha mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uandishi wa insha ya maelezo (k.v wahusika, ujumbe, muundo ) kwenye kitabu, kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza maelezo yakitolewa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kwenye vifaa vya kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake, ● kusoma kielelezo cha insha ya maelezo kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kutambua kanuni za uandishi wa insha ya maelezo (k.v. mwandiko nadhifu, mtiririko) akiwa na wenzake, ● kuandika insha ya maelezo kuhusu suala KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je,unatumia maneno ya aina gani unapotoa maelezo kuhusu kitu?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 10.4.1 Vinyume vya Vitendo (Vipindi 3)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 10.4.1 Vinyume vya Vitendo (Vipindi 3). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua vinyume vya vitendo katika matini, b) kutumia vinyume vya vitendo ipasavyo katika matini, c) kuchangamkia kutumia vitendo na vinyume vyake katika mawasiliano ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kutambua vinyume vya vitendo (k.v. fungua- funga, keti- simama, twika- tua) kwenye chati, kitabu au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusikiliza kifungu chenye vinyume vya vitendo kikisomwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa na wenzake, ● kusoma vinyume vya vitendo katika kifungu akiwa na wenzake, ● kukamilisha sentensi akitumia vinyume vya vitendo akiwa na wenzake, ● kutunga sentensi akitumia vinyume vya vitendo na kuzijadili na wenzake ili kuzitolea maoni, ● kuigiza vinyume vya vitendo vilivyotumiwa kwenye kifungu akiwa na wenzake, ● kumtajia mzazi au mlezi vinyume vya maneno alivyojifunza darasani. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unajua vinyume vipi vya vitendo?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.strand: Kuweza kuwasiliana kwa njia ifaayo (matamshi, kiimbo na kusikika)
chunks.sub_strand: Mwanafunzi anajieleza kwa ufasaha na utendeti, bila makosa ya kimatamshi ya sauti lengwa na anapozungumza anasikika ipasavyo na asemayo yanaeleweka vyema. Maelezo yake yana mantiki na yanafuatilika kwa urahisi. Anazungumza kama mzawa wa lugha hii
chunks.text: STRAND: Kuweza kuwasiliana kwa njia ifaayo (matamshi, kiimbo na kusikika). SUB-STRAND: Mwanafunzi anajieleza kwa ufasaha na utendeti, bila makosa ya kimatamshi ya sauti lengwa na anapozungumza anasikika ipasavyo na asemayo yanaeleweka vyema. Maelezo yake yana mantiki na yanafuatilika kwa urahisi. Anazungumza kama mzawa wa lugha hii. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Mwanafunzi anajieleza kwa ufasaha. Ana matamshi yafaayo yanayozingatia sauti lengwa . Aidha ana kiimbo mwafaka. Ana makosa machache ya kimatamshi na kiimbo lakini anasikika vyema na asemayo yanaeleweka. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi anajieleza kwa kusitasita. Anafanya makosa ya kimatamshi yanayotokana na sauti lengwa na kiimbo chake kina udhaifu. Mara kwa mara na hasisikiki vyema. Maana inaweza kukisiwa kutokana na asemayo. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ana stadi hafifu za kimatamshi na kiimbo. Anafanya makosa mengi ya kimatamshi. Anakosa mantiki /mfuatano ufaao katika kujieleza. Hasisikiki vyema na asemayo hayaeleweki.

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.strand: Kufahamu suala lengwa (majibu sahihi, matumizi ya msamiati mwafaka)
chunks.sub_strand: Anatoa maelezo sahihi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa mfano katika ufahamu wa kusikiliza. Anatoa majibu sahihi kwa maswali yote aliyoulizwa kwenye muktadha. Anautumia msamiati mpana wa mada lengwa kwa usahihi
chunks.text: STRAND: Kufahamu suala lengwa (majibu sahihi, matumizi ya msamiati mwafaka). SUB-STRAND: Anatoa maelezo sahihi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa mfano katika ufahamu wa kusikiliza. Anatoa majibu sahihi kwa maswali yote aliyoulizwa kwenye muktadha. Anautumia msamiati mpana wa mada lengwa kwa usahihi. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Anatoa maelezo sahihi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa mfano katika ufahamu wa kusikiliza. Anatoa majibu sahihi kwa idadi kubwa ya maswali aliyoulizwa kulingana na muktadha. Anatumia msamiati lengwa ipasavyo k.m hiki na hivi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Anatoa maelezo kwa baadhi ya maswali katika muktadha wa suala lengwa kwa mfano katika ufahamu wa kusikiliza. Anatoa majibu kwa baadhi ya maswali aliyoulizwa kulingana na muktadha. Anatumia baadhi ya msamiati wa suala lengwa. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ana changamoto kujibu maswali aliyoulizwa kutokana na ufahamu wa kusikiliza. Anautumia msamiati finyu wa mada lengwa.

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Number Concept
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Number Concept (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: use ordinal numbers to a) order objects according size, b) identify position of objects from 1st to 20th, c) write the position of objects in numbers symbols and in words, d) appreciate use of positions of items in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner to be guided to: ● in pairs or groups, discuss and arrange real objects collected from the environment according to size starting with the smallest to the largest and from the largest to the smallest, ● name the position of an object from a reference point using 1st, 2nd up to 20th, ● in groups of 20, race for a distance and assign each other the correct position using the words first, second up to twentieth position depending on when they finish the race. Write their positions in the race in symbols and in words, ● in pairs/groups, relate numbers 1 to 20 to positions first, second up to 20th and KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we tell our positions in a competition?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Whole Numbers
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Whole Numbers (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) count numbers forward up to 1000 starting from any point, b) count numbers backward in multiples of 100 from 1000, c) identify the place value of numbers up to hundreds, d) read numbers 1 to 1000 in symbols, e) read and write numbers 1 to 100 in words, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, count forward in 1’s, 10’s, and 100’s starting from any point up to 1000 using rope skipping game in a safe environment, ● in pairs/groups, practise through play using number cards counting numbers backward in multiples of 100 from 1000, ● in pairs / groups, discuss place value up to hundreds using place value apparatus in class, ● in pairs / groups, read numbers 1 to 1000 in symbols starting from any KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How would you get the total number of people in a group? 2. How do you tell the place value of a digit in a number?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Addition
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Addition (25 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) add a 3 digit number to up to a 2 digit number without regrouping with sum not exceeding 1000, b) add a 3 digit number to up to a 2 digit number with single regrouping with sum not exceeding 1000, c) add two 3 digit numbers without regrouping, d) add two 3 digit numbers with single regrouping SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● add a 3 digit number to up to 2 digit number without regrouping with sum not exceeding 1000 using place value apparatus, ● practice addition horizontally and vertically using place value apparatus, ● in pairs or groups or individually, practise adding a 3 digit number to up to a 2 digit number with single regrouping with sum KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you arrange numbers when adding downwards? 2. How can you get the next number in a given pattern?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 Subtraction
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 Subtraction (20 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) subtract a 2-digit number from a 3 digit number without regrouping, b) Subtract a 2 digit number from a three digit number with single regrouping, c) subtract a 3 digit number from a 3 digit number with single regrouping, d) subtract up to 3 digit numbers involving missing numbers with single regrouping, e) work out missing numbers in number patterns involving subtraction up to 1000, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in groups, work out subtraction of up to 3 digit numbers without regrouping using place value apparatus and share findings with others, ● in turns, work out subtraction of up to 3 digit numbers with single regrouping using place value chart, ● work out missing numbers in subtraction of up to 3 digit numbers with single regrouping using a variety of strategies, ● play games involving subtraction using digital KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. When do you regroup during subtraction? 2. How do you identify the missing number in a number pattern involving subtraction?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.5 Multiplication
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.5 Multiplication (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) model multiplication as repeated addition using numbers 1,2,3,4 and 5 by 4 and 5, b) multiply a single digit number by a single digit number, c) multiply single digit numbers by 10, d) appreciate multiplication of numbers as repeated addition. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs/groups, model multiplication as repeated addition of numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 by 4 and 5 using counters, ● in groups, multiply a single digit number by a single digit number using multiplication chart, ● in turns, practice multiplication of single digit numbers by 10 using multiplication tables, ● play games involving multiplication using digital or other resources. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can you work out multiplication using repeated addition? 2. How do model multiplication as repeated addition?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.6 Division
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.6 Division (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) represent division of numbers up to 50 by 4 and 5 as repeated subtraction b) divide a 2 digit number by a single digit number without a remainder, c) divide a 2 digit number by 10 without a remainder, d) appreciate division as repeated subtraction in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in groups, take away from a group a specific number of objects at a time until all are finished and then count the number of small groups formed and share their findings with others, ● in groups, discuss and model division as repeated subtraction of numbers up to 50 by 4 and 5 using counters and share their findings with others, ● in pairs/ groups, practise division of multiples of ten from 90 by 10 using multiplication tables, ● extended activity: learners can participate in communal activities related to feeding of animals which involves subtraction of KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can you represent division as repeated subtraction? 2. How can we use the multiplicatio n table to work out division questions?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 1.7 Fractions
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Numbers. SUB-STRAND: 1.7 Fractions (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify , and as part of a whole, b) identify , and as part of a group, c) appreciate fractions as part of a whole in daily activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs /groups, safely make circular cut-outs from manila papers, ● in pairs /groups, fold circular cut-outs into 2 equal parts and identify one part as of the whole, ● in pairs /groups, make rectangular cut- outs and fold them into 4 equal parts to get a quarter of a whole and identify each part as of the whole, ● in pairs /groups, make rectangular cut- outs and fold to get 8 equal parts and identify one part as of the whole, ● in pairs /groups, divide a number of objects into 2 equal groups and identify each of the small groups as of the whole group, ● in pairs /groups, divide a number of KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you represent a half, a quarter or an eighth of a group?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Mass
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Mass (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) measure mass in kilograms, b) add mass in kilograms, c) subtract mass in kilograms, d) estimate mass up to 5 kilograms, e) appreciate measuring mass of objects in kilograms. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● collect safe materials to be used to measure mass in their immediate environment, ● make masses of 1kg using sand or soil by measuring against the kilogram standard unit, ● in groups, measure mass of different objects in kilograms using a beam balance and share experiences, ● in pairs/groups, role play addition of mass in kilograms using items in the classroom model shop, ● work out the differences between the masses of items in the classroom model shop, ● compare the masses of items in the classroom model shop with a 5kg mass, ● estimate mass of items up to 5kg, ● measure the masses of items to confirm their actual mass, ● play digital games involving mass. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you make a 1kg mass using a beam balance?

chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Capacity (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) measure capacity in litres, b) add capacity in litres, c) subtract capacity in litres, d) estimate capacity up to 5 litres, e) appreciate measuring capacity of containers in litres. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in pairs /groups, collect safe materials in their immediate environment to be used to measure capacity, ● in pairs or groups, discuss and measure capacity of different containers using a 1 litre containers, ● in turns, practice addition of capacity in litres in real life situations, ● in turns, practice subtraction of capacity in litres in real life situations, ● estimate capacity of containers up to 5 litres, ● measure the actual capacity of the containers to confirm their capacity in litres, ● play digital games involving capacity in real life situations. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can the capacity of a container be measured?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Time
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Time (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the minute as a unit of measuring time, b) read and tell time using ‘past’ and ‘to’ the hour using the clock face, c) read and tell time using the digital clock or analogue clock, d) write time using ‘past’ and ‘to’ the hour, e) estimate time in hours, f) add time involving SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● in groups, draw a clock face on a manila paper or any other resource, divide the clock face into two equal parts using a line passing through the centre, and discuss what each division represents, ● in pairs/groups, discuss the divisions on the clock face, ● locate a minute on the clock face and discuss it as a unit of measuring time, ● in pairs/groups, discuss how to tell time on the clock face using “past” and “to” the KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we read and tell time using digital and analog clocks?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 2.5 Money
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Measurement. SUB-STRAND: 2.5 Money (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify Kenyan currency notes up to sh.1000, b) count money in different denominations up to sh.1000, c) add money involving SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● use locally available materials to model Kenyan currency denominations for use in learning, ● in pairs/groups, sort Kenyan currency notes according to their value up to sh.1000, ● in pairs/groups, count Kenyan currency notes in different denominations up to sh1000, ● in pairs/groups, subtract money up KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can money be represented in different denominations?

chunks.subject: Mathematics
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Position and Direction
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Geometry. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Position and Direction (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) move along a straight line from a point, b) identify the right and left side from a point, c) turn to the right from a point, d) turn to the left from a point, e) appreciate use of directions in real life situations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in pairs /groups, move along a straight line from a given point outside the classroom,  in pairs/groups, play a game of moving to the right and left sides from a point,  in pairs/groups, move straight outside the classroom then turn to the right,  in pairs/groups, move straight outside the classroom then turn to the left,  in pairs or groups, play games involving moving along a straight line and turning left or right,  play digital games involving movement on straight lines and turning to the left and right. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the importance of directions in real life situations?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Soil Conservation
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Soil Conservation (7 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify suitable materials for making compost manure b) Prepare compost manure for farming c) Appreciate importance of compost manure in farming. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss suitable materials for compost manure based on their local environment. • Collect and compost suitable materials and make compost manure using heap method. • Practise the learnt skills in making compost manure using slashed vegetation, kitchen wastes and any other available organic wastes and using it in their gardening activities. • Develop communication skills during the discussion; care for environment while collecting waste organic matter; and unity while working together in the composting activity. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can composting conserve the environment?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Water Conservation
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Water Conservation (7 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe drip irrigation as a way of conserving water b) Carry out drip irrigation to conserve water c) Appreciate use of drip irrigation in conserving water in farming. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Watch video clips or use print media or observe drip irrigation in neighbouring households to guide them discuss drip irrigation concept. • Innovate drip equipment using water pipes and available containers and use the drip irrigation in gardening activities • Develop creativity skills when innovating drip irrigation equipment; practice responsibility in task allocation; and personal safety while working with tools and equipment. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we use drip irrigation to conserve water?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Fuel Conservation
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Fuel Conservation (7 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify types of fuels used at home b) Use and conserve fuels in cooking c) Appreciate the importance of conserving fuel to minimize wastage of resources. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss to enumerate the types of fuels such as charcoal, firewood, gas, kerosene, used at home. • Practise ways of conserving fuels such as putting off fire when done and using fuel efficient equipment when cooking. • Develop problem solving skills as they solve problems of fuel by reducing wastage in use of fuel, show responsibility by practicing advance preparation of foodstuffs, observe safety in use of fuel. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does reducing fuel wastage conserve our resources?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 Conserving Wild Animals
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 Conserving Wild Animals (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify small wild animals that destroy crops b) Construct and use a scarecrow to keep off small wild animals from crops c) Appreciate the importance of living better with small wild animals. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Brainstorm and share experiences on small wild animals such as birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys, that destroy crops. • Discuss, construct a scarecrow using locally available materials and install the scarecrows in the immediate environment to keep off small wild animals. • Develop creativity skills as they design a scare crow, demonstrate responsibility in allocating roles to construct and practice animal protection by safely keeping off the small wild animal. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does reducing fuel wastage conserve our resources?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds b) Sow tiny seeds in a finely prepared seedbed. c) Adopt direct sowing in establishment of food crops. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss to enumerate food crops such as carrots and millet that are established through direct sowing of tiny seeds (crops that do not require transplanting). • Sow the tiny seeds in a finely prepared ground or container seedbed. • Develop learning to learn as they address challenges in establishing tiny seeds, develop tolerance and respect while undertaking the seedbed preparation task and resolve food security in growing a crop. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does direct sowing of tiny seeds enhance food production process?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Growing fruits
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Growing fruits (16 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify fruits that can grow the locality, b) Grow a fruit crop suited in the locality, c) Appreciate the importance of consuming fruits for nutrition. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Brainstorm and share information on different types of fruits that can grow in their locality. • Establish and take care a fruit crop that can suitably grow in the locality such as woody fruit tree (for example, tree tomato and guava) and climbing fruits (such as passion fruit, kiwi, grapes, black berries, rasp berries), • Develop self-efficacy when they produce own fruits for consumption; responsibility while caring for the growing fruits; and promote health by consuming fruits.. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we grow fruits?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Uses of Domestic Animals
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Uses of Domestic Animals (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify types of domestic animals in the community b) Relate various domestic animals to their uses c) Appreciate the importance of domestic animals for food production. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Share experiences on the types of domestic animals (cattle, sheep, goats, poultry) found in their community and their uses. • Match the domestic animals to their uses (cattle, sheep, goat and poultry). • Make class presentations using photos or other visuals importance of domestic animal. • Develop self –efficacy as they confidently make class presentations; respect others while listening to the presentations; and appreciate the uses of domestic animals KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does domestic animal contribute to food production?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Balanced Diet
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Balanced Diet (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Explain importance of eating a balanced diet b) Select food from different food-groups to make a balanced diet c) Appreciate the importance of eating a balanced diet. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss or use digital devices to search for importance of eating a balanced diet (variety and proportion). • Select foods from locally available foods that comprise a balanced diet. • Exhibit unity in making collaborative presentations of a balanced meal, and promote health awareness through the class presentations. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does a balanced diet impact on health?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.5 Boiling and Shallow Frying Food
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.5 Boiling and Shallow Frying Food (11 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe boiling and shallow frying as methods of cooking b) Cook food using boiling and shallow frying methods c) Embrace boiling and shallow frying in food production. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Watch video clip or demonstration on boiling and shallow frying methods of cooking. • Cook and serve boiled and shallow fried foods. • Demonstrate learning to learn by working cautiously while boiling and shallow frying ; following cooking steps; and promoting safety measures while working with fire and fats. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we cook foods using boiling and frying methods?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Personal Hygiene
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Hygiene Practices. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Personal Hygiene (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify health practices that promote personal hygiene b) Apply health practices that promote personal hygiene c) Embrace health practices to promote personal hygiene in daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Brainstorm and enumerate practices that promote personal hygiene such as hand washing, use of personal protective equipment, use of clean water and cleaning foods. • Demonstrate appropriate practices that promote personal hygiene such as hand washing, use of personal protective equipment, use of clean water and cleaning foods. • Demonstrate self -efficacy through practising good grooming ; and responsibility as they carry out health practices. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does personal hygiene promote good health?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Domestic Hygiene
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Hygiene Practices. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Domestic Hygiene (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe the various methods used for cleaning home environment b) Use appropriate methods to clean home environment c) Appreciate a clean environment in promoting domestic hygiene SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss the methods of cleaning home environment such as mopping, dusting, sweeping and disposal of refuse. • Apply the methods such as mopping, dusting, sweeping and disposal of refuse to maintain hygiene in the environment. The methods to be applied using improvised and locally available resources. • Develop creativity in the use of improvised resources while cleaning; accountability in taking care of living places; and environmental awareness in maintaining clean environment. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we maintain hygienic in the home environment?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Hygiene Practices. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify personal protective equipment in day to day life b) Clean personal protective equipment for hygiene purposes c) Appreciate clean personal protective equipment in promoting hygiene. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Search for information or observe a demonstration to identify common personal protective equipment such as gloves, dust masks, gum boots, head gear, overall and canvas shoes. • Apply appropriate methods to clean personal protective equipment such as gumboots or canvas shoes. • Develop digital literacy as they search for personal protective equipment; responsibility as they care for personal protective items; and personal safety skills as they exercise caution in the cleaning activity. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does cleaning of personal protective equipment promote hygiene?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Self-awareness 2 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Self-awareness 2 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) mention his/her name for identification and self- awareness, b) recognise that he/she is unique as a creation of God, c) acknowledge God as the Creator of our bodies, d) appreciate his/her uniqueness as God’s special creation. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  say their names,  state what is unique about them,  recite and meditate on Psalms 139:13 about being fearfully and wonderfully made,  read Genesis 1:27 about, ‘created in the image and likeness of God’  sing a song related to their uniqueness. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are you a special creation?

chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Thoughts and feelings 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 1 2. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Thoughts and feelings 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) identify good thoughts and feelings in day- to- day life, b) explain the importance of being joyful; Philippians 4:4, c) list lessons learnt from Ephesians 4:26, d) apply the lessons learnt to cope with emotions in SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  sing a song related to good thoughts and feelings,  list good thoughts such as sharing with others, helping parents, being happy, being thankful, respecting others,  write Philippians 4:4 on flash cards and recite it,  share experiences on how they KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you control your thoughts and feelings? 2. How do you cope with anger or sadness?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Making choices 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 3 4. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Making choices 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) list choices they make in day-to-day life, b) discuss results of choices they make in daily life, c) make right choices guided by Christian principles, d) acquire responsibility by making right choices. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in pairs, list choices they make in day-to –day life,  list results of choices that they make,  sing a song about good choices,  role play ‘making right choices that are acceptable to God.’ KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the effects of the choices you make?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 My Family family members 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 My Family family members 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) name family members in the nuclear and extended family, b) draw a family tree to understand relationships within the family, c) explain why it is important to honour parents; Ephesians 6:1-3, d) desire to respect family members for harmonious co- existence. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  sing a song related to family relationships,  name family members in the nuclear family,  name family members in the extended family (cousins, aunts, uncles, grandparents and great grandparents),  draw a family tree and write names of family members on it,  list ways of respecting family members,  type a poem on their digital devices about respect for family member,  watch a video clip of family members eating or praying together,  recite Ephesians 6:1-3 on respecting parents. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to know members of your family?

chunks.sub_strand: 1.5 Relationships within the Family 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Creation. SUB-STRAND: 1.5 Relationships within the Family 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) take care when alone with people of the opposite sex, b) mention ways of protecting oneself from sexual abuse, c) identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused, d) appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  sing a song related to respecting their bodies as the temple of the Holy Spirit,  in turns read 2 Samuel 13:4-14,  say whom to report to if they are touched inappropriately or sexually abused,  in groups tell how they should protect themselves from sexual abuse,  role play ways of protecting themselves from sexual abuse,  write 1 Corinthians 6:19 on flash cards and meditate on it,  watch a video clip of children being tempted with gifts, but they say NO! to the strangers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are healthy family relationships important?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) handle the Bible with respect since it is the inspired word of God, b) identify the books in the Old and New Testament, c) play a game on naming some Books in the Old and New Testament, d) recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES:  The learner is guided to:  sing a song related to respecting the Holy Bible,  role play ways of handling the Bible with respect,  in pairs observe and read charts containing books in the Old and New Testament,  play games on naming some Books in the Old and the New Testament,  recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16,  sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should you respect the Holy Bible? 2. Why is it important to know the books in the Bible?

chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 The Holy Bible. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Balaam’s Donkey 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read Numbers 22:1-6, 20-34 and retell the story of Balaam and his donkey, b) apply the story in their lives by obeying God’s instructions, c) acquire the value of love by speaking good things about others, d) Acknowledge God’s greatness by revering Him. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in groups read Numbers 22:1-6, 20- 34,  in pairs list the importance of obeying God and their seniors,’  role play the story of Balaam’s Donkey,  discuss why they should bless and not curse/speak ill about others as per Numbers 22:1-6, 20-34,  use a digital device and draw the scenarios in this story,  sing a song related to obedience. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why did the donkey talk?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  in turns read Judges 14:5-9,  model/draw a lion,  write a poem on ‘Samson kills a lion’,  watch a video clip about Samson,  sing a song on God’s power,  draw pictures of, Samson killing a lion. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How did Samson kill a lion?

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Christian Values. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Trust: 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) emulate Joseph by resisting sexual temptations as young SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in turns read Genesis 39:7-12 and retell the story of Joseph and Potiphar’s wife,  list people they can trust at home school and the community, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Whom do you trust at home and at school? 2. Why should you avoid talking to strangers?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Truthfulness 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Christian Values. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Truthfulness 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the importance of telling the truth always, b) resist lying as cited in Proverbs 12:19, c) desire to always speak the truth as outlined in Ephesians 4:25. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Ephesians 4:25,  say why they should tell the truth always,  in pairs say when they did not tell the truth and how to overcome lies,  write a poem on the importance of telling the truth always,  write Proverbs 12: 19 on flash cards and recite it. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you tell the truth always?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3 Obedience at home and school 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Christian Values. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Obedience at home and school 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) read Exodus 20:12 and state the benefit of honouring parents, b) obey parents and siblings for harmonious co-existence, c) practice responsibility by obeying teachers and other leaders in the school, d) outline the results of disobedience and desire obedient always. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Exodus 20:12 and state the benefit of honouring parents,  compose a poem on the benefits of obeying parents,  list results of obeying school rules,  in groups list results of disobedience,  sing the song on benefits of obedience. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you obey your parents and teachers?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.4 Jesus loves little Children 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Christian Values. SUB-STRAND: 4.4 Jesus loves little Children 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognize that God loves children; Matthew 19:13-15, b) demonstrate love for others by being kind to them, c) appreciate God’s love by obeying His teachings.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.5 Responsibility Personal and school properties
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Christian Values. SUB-STRAND: 4.5 Responsibility Personal and school properties (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify personal items and how they take care of them, b) identify school properties and how to take care of them, c) acquire responsibility by taking care of personal and school properties. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  display personal items e.g. pullover, pen, pencils, eraser, exercise books, text books,  in pairs list the use of each of his/ her personal and school items,  say why they should take good care of their personal and school items,  compose a poem on taking care of personal and school properties. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you take care of personal and school items?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.6 Holiness 4 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Christian Values. SUB-STRAND: 4.6 Holiness 4 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to; a) describe ways of glorifying God with their bodies, b) acquire the value of holiness by keeping away from situations that lead to sin, c) recite 1 Corinthians 6:19 on the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit, d) desire to lead holy lives free from sin. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in pairs read 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 and mention the lessons learnt,  in pairs list sins that do not please God,  in groups discuss how to avoid situations that lead to sin,  sing a song on holiness. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you lead holy lives as young people?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1 House of God 2 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 The Church. SUB-STRAND: 5.1 House of God 2 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline lessons learnt from Matthew 21:12- 14, b) participate in Church activities to grow spiritually, c) appreciate the Church as a house of worship. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Matthew 21:12-14 and list lessons learnt from the Bible text,  read 1Corithinians 14:26 and list activities they do in church,  in groups mention ways they serve God in Church,  in pairs list ways of respecting the church as a house of God,  write a poem about respecting the Church,  sing a song related to serving God. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is the Church a holy place?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2 The Early Church 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 The Church. SUB-STRAND: 5.2 The Early Church 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to; a) identify the first disciples of Jesus Christ from the scriptures provided, b) describe how the early church was started as outlined in Acts 2:38- 41, c) desire to turn away from sins as stated in Acts 2:38. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Matthew 10:1-4 and list the disciples of Jesus Christ,  sort the names of the 12 disciples by using flash cards,  search for the names of the disciples in a word puzzle,  watch a video clip on the twelve disciples,  read Acts 2:38-41on how the early church was started,  role play how the early church was started,  repent their sins as guided in Acts 2:38. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How was the early church started?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3 Standing Firm in Faith 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 The Church. SUB-STRAND: 5.3 Standing Firm in Faith 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) name the city where believers were first called Christians, b) retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith, c) explain why they should not join ungodly groups, d) Utilize the virtue of assertiveness and stand firm in faith. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  sing a song related to standing firm in the Christian faith,  read Acts 11: 26 and say where believers were first called Christians,  identify Antioch, from a Bible map,  in groups read Acts 7: 54-60 about how Stephen was stoned to death,  list lessons learnt form the stoning of Stephen,  explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalized groups, groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ,  list ways they can stand firm in their Christian faith. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should you stand firm in your Christian faith? 2. Why should you not join ungodly groups?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4 The Lord’s Prayer 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 The Church. SUB-STRAND: 5.4 The Lord’s Prayer 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read Matthew 6:9-13 on the Lord’s prayer, b) recite the Lord’s prayer and pray always, c) say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  sing a song related to the Lord’s Prayer,  read Matthew 6:9-13,  discuss why it is important to pray everyday,  pray for their parents/guardians, friends and relatives,  recite the Lord’s prayer daily,  list the number of times they pray and share with classmates. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you pray always as a Christian?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.5 Fruit of the Holy Spirit 3 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 The Church. SUB-STRAND: 5.5 Fruit of the Holy Spirit 3 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) list the fruit of the Holy Spirit as guided in Galatians 5:22-23, b) describe how they apply the fruit of the Holy Spirit in their lives, c) desire to be led by the Holy Spirit in their daily activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in pairs read Galatians 5: 22-23,  list the fruit of the Holy Spirit; love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, humility, self- control,  write the fruit of the Holy Spirit on flash cards and display it in class,  in groups list good things, they should do to others as Christians,  discuss how they apply the fruit of the Holy Spirit in daily lives,  compose and sing a song on the fruit of the Holy Spirit. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you have the fruit of the Holy Spirit?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (CRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.6 Self-control 2 lessons
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 The Church. SUB-STRAND: 5.6 Self-control 2 lessons. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) practice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23- 25, b) make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit, c) demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body, d) Desire to live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read Galatians 5:23-25,  role play,’ making decisions that portray self-control’  in groups list choices they make in their day- to- day lives,  list things that can defile them e.g. engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse  say how they can avoid defiling their bodies,  compose a song on self-control: Galatians 5:23-25. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should you have self-control?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in groups list some digital devices that they know or use,  in pairs discuss appropriate use of social media,  say why they should not chat with online strangers,  use a digital device to listen to a gospel song or watch a video clip based on the Bible. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should use social media appropriately?

chunks.sub_strand:  Words Search Puzzle  Checklists  Assessment Rubrics  Question and Answer
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.6 Holiness. SUB-STRAND:  Words Search Puzzle  Checklists  Assessment Rubrics  Question and Answer.
