chunks.text: STRAND: 8.0 Utsav (Festivals). SUB-STRAND: 8.2 Indian Traditional Calendar Days of the week in relation to planets. (No. of Lessons 10). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to: a) name the days of the week according to Indian traditional calendar, b) relate the days of the week with the corresponding planets for preservation of tradition, c) Appreciate Indian traditional calendar for its uniqueness. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  download the Indian traditional calendar and form a weekly plan.  create and decorate the calendar using digital devices wherever possible.  match the days with the corresponding planets  Make greeting cards as per the Indian traditional calendar to share among peers and family.  Compose a song in praise of the Indian traditional calendar. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How are the days of the week related to the solar system?

chunks.sub_strand: Identifies the rites and rituals appropriately
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to identify the rites and rituals during the celebration of different festivals. SUB-STRAND: Identifies the rites and rituals appropriately. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Identifies the rites and rituals. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Identifies some of the rites and rituals. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Identifies some of the rites and rituals with prompts.

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Relates the days of the week with some of the corresponding planets. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Relates the days of the week with some of the corresponding planets with guidance.

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Attentive listening
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Attentive listening. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information, b) respond to verbal instructions for information, c) appreciate listening to various cultural songs for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work with peers to list cultural foods on charts,  identify nouns in singular and plural forms ,  change the nouns identified into their singular or plural forms,  recite singing games based on the theme ,  respond to lead instructions in singing games as given by the soloist,  work collaboratively to collect varied songs on the theme from the community,  organise the songs collected in the class portfolio,  listen to recordings on various cultural foods in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How should we respond to instructions?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Reading for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Reading for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify vocabulary items in a text for comprehension, b) read a text based on the theme for information, c) appreciate reading texts SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify singular and plural forms of nouns from the texts ,  search for simple passages based on the theme from print or non-print sources,  list vocabulary items based on the theme on flashcards,  work with peers to create a vocabulary bank for the vocabulary identified,  in small groups, practice reading the texts fluently,  conduct peer reviews on each group’s presentation,  answer comprehension questions based on the passage,  make a list of cultural foods identified in the text, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you read to acquire information in texts?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Handwriting. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify letters of the alphabet in their language for effective communication, b) write simple sentences legibly and neatly for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  trace, model and paint letters of the alphabet in their language,  form simple words based on the theme,  in small groups, fish sentence cards with the simple words,  copy the sentences neatly and legibly,  work with peers to fill in blank spaces to complete sentences using vocabulary, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to write legibly and neatly?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Listening for information - instructions
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Listening for information - instructions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select instructions from an oral text for information, b) respond to instructions for comprehension, c) appreciate the need for clarity in providing instructions for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to audio recordings on using verbs to give instructions, ● give instructions on how to carry out a task in pairs e.g. what to do when it is raining, ● conduct a review on the task based on instructions given, ● list the verbs used in the instructions on charts with peers, ● play the ‘simon says’ language game or the ‘Chinese whisper language game’ to practice giving and responding to instructions, ● practise responding to instructions displayed from flash cards in pairs. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we give clear instructions in speech? 2. How is weather forecasting done in communities?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1Reading fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1Reading fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a story with expression and correct intonation for effective communication, b) respond to questions from a text for comprehension, c) appreciate reading a variety of texts for fluency. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  conduct a reader’s theatre to read a short passage on the theme with correct intonation,  identify important points from the text and write them down,  answer questions from a passage based on the theme,  role play reading a news bulletin report on the weather forecast creatively and with expression,  record the role play using a digital device for peer review, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we ensure we read fluently? 2. Why is reading fluently important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Punctuation
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Punctuation. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work with peers to copy sentences and underline the punctuation marks (full stops, comma and upper case) in sentences, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the importance of punctuation marks in writing?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Listening for comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Listening for comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify verbs from an oral text for comprehension, b) respond to questions from an oral passage for comprehension, c) appreciate listening to oral texts for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● listen to an oral passage from a pre- recorded audio or resource person on the theme, ● list down verbs identified from the oral text, ● work jointly with peers to construct oral sentences, ● play ‘the guessing language game’ where they use actions to describe verbs for peers to guess what verb it is, ● answer comprehension questions from the oral text, ● complete sentences orally by filling in the gaps using verbs, ● share experiences about personal safety in groups. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we ensure personal safety in school?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: Reading for comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: Reading for comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a dialogue based on the theme for comprehension, b) infer meaning of vocabulary from a text for comprehension, seek to read texts for information based on the theme. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● take turns to read dialogues as a class, ● answer comprehension questions based on the dialogues read, ● work closely with peers to identify vocabulary items from the text, ● create and fill word puzzles using vocabulary on theme collaboratively, ● match the vocabulary identified with their meaning, work together to use a simple dictionary to look up the meaning of the vocabulary. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you tell the meaning of a word from a text?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Sequencing ideas
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Sequencing ideas. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify main ideas in a simple paragraph for comprehension, b) compose a paragraph on the theme for self- expression, c) value the need to sequence ideas well in writing based on the theme. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work in partnership with peers to identify verbs in sentences from newspaper cuttings,  write sentences with simple verbs and share for peer review,  engage in a digital language game to drag and drop word segments to create simple sentences,  reorganise jumbled up sentences to make a well sequenced paragraph,  write a short paragraph on the theme with well sequenced ideas, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we sequence ideas in a story?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Self – expression
chunks.text: STRAND: 4 .1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Self – expression. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify similes and metaphors commonly used in their community, b) recite oral narratives fluently for pronunciation, c) appreciate use of similes and metaphors for self- expressions. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● Identify similes and metaphors used in their community , ● work jointly with peers to discuss different metaphors, ● practise using similes in sentences appropriately. ● write the similes and their meaning on wall charts, ● display the wall charts on similes in class for peer review through gallery walks, ● compose an oral narrative on the theme using similes and metaphors, ● stage the oral narrative in class for peer review. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why are school rules important? 2. Why is it important to use similes and metaphors in self- expression?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.1 Extensive reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Extensive reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify metaphors, similes , proverbs and sayings from level readers for comprehension, b) infer the meaning of vocabulary from context for comprehension, c) enjoy reading silently and widely for pleasure. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  create a collection of simple indigenous languages readers for the class library,  conduct a readers’ theatre to read the class indigenous book collection,  tease out vocabulary from the readers,  use simple level dictionaries to comprehend meaning of vocabulary,  fill code word tables or crossword puzzles using vocabulary in small groups  partner with peers to practice matching words with their meanings,  identify metaphors, similes, proverbs and sayings from the readers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we read silently? 2. What makes a book interesting to read?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 Creative Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Creative Writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand,the learner should be able to: a) identify proverbs and sayings for information, b) write an imaginative composition using proverbs and sayings, c) appreciate proverbs and sayings for cultural awareness. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify proverbs and sayings from the community,  list the proverbs and sayings on sentence strips for display in class,  organise their collection of proverbs and sayings in a group portfolio,  engage in a language game to find meaning of community proverbs and sayings,  write a composition on the theme using proverbs and sayings  share their compositions with peers for peer review,  publish the best compositions in a class reading club. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are proverbs and sayings important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Expressing self creatively
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Expressing self creatively. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe personal experiences and events for fluency, b) use ‘when’ as a conjunction in sentences for expression, c) enjoy describing events and experiences creatively. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● conduct a storytelling session to describe a personal event and experience with money, ● use digital devices to record narrations on event descriptions, ● work jointly with peers to play a language train game to connect sentences using the conjunction ‘when’, ● narrate events based on the theme using the conjunction ‘when’ ● work collaboratively to role play a creative short skit on an interesting event that takes place in the market. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we describe events and experiences?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Reading to acquire information
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Reading to acquire information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension, b) apply reading strategies SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read a short passage based on the theme,  scan for specific vocabulary from the passage,  work collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank based on the words identified,  use a simple language dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary identified,  identify compound sentences from the text with peers,  use sentence strips to break down the compound KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to comprehend the meaning of vocabulary in context? How do we read to get information?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1 Writing sentences
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Writing sentences. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify parts that make a sentence for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  cooperate with peers to play a digital language game to identify, drag and drop coordinating conjunctions to complete sentences,  work together to discuss new words related KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do we connect ideas in sentences?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1.1 Listening for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Listening for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe positions of objects in relation to others for information, b) respond to oral questions based on the theme, c) advocate for animal welfare practices for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● work in partnership with peers to identify types of animals from audio recordings, ● compose sentences describing the position of an object in relation to another with words such as next to, under, in front of, between, behind, on, in, beside, outside, ● role play placing objects at different positions according to instructions given, ● work closely with peers to identify prepositions from the passages, ● answer comprehension questions , ● listen to a resource person on imaginative stories on animals and their welfare, ● conduct a debate on animal welfare practices. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is the importance of prepositions in description? 2. Why should we take care of animals?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.1 Reading fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1 Reading fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read poems with correct pace, speed and intonation for self -expression b) answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension. c) recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  practice reading poems on animal welfare with correct pace, speed and intonation,  watch poem recitations based on the theme from digital platforms,  work jointly with peers to compose simple poems based on the theme,  recite the poems in class while recording speed and pace of recitation,  peer assess each other’s performance for improvement,  answer questions from the poems,  take part in a spoken word competition applying pace, speed and intonation correctly,  record themselves reciting the spoken word and organise their work in digital portfolios. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we read poems fluently? 2. Why are poems important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3.1 Creative writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.3WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 6.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand ,the learner should be able to: a) highlight the elements of creative writing, b) write a story on the theme from artistic expressions, c) enjoy picture reading for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  collaboratively discuss the elements of creative writing,  study artistic work/pictures used to write creative stories,  write creative stories in groups based on the pictures,  exchange their written stories for peer review,  draw pictures to form a story based on the theme,  organise picture stories in a class KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why are stories important in communities? 2. What is the importance of artistic work in expressing creativity?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1.1 Listen to make personal opinions and judgements
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1 Listen to make personal opinions and judgements. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe leisure activities for information, b) respond to comprehension questions correctly, c) appreciate listening SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● collaboratively listen to an audio recording on leisure activities, ● cooperate with peers to list constructive leisure activities, ● use interjections to describe a leisure activity of choice, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you spend your leisure time? 2. How do we identify our talents?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 7.2.1 Reading comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1 Reading comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify interjections in texts for comprehension, b) use interjections in oral paragraphs for expression, c) enjoy reading a variety of texts with interjections for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read passages on the use of leisure time,  take notes on main ideas from the passage,  jointly identify interjections used,  list the interjections in their community on flashcards,  read the interjections with correct intonations,  discuss meaning of the interjections such as please and excuse me,  collaborate with peers to take part in a reading competition involving paragraphs with interjections. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: When do we use interjections in sentences?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3.1 Creative writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) highlight the steps of writing a simple dialogue, b) write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections, c) appreciate the need of creative writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss the steps of writing a simple dialogue,  list interjections used in their community on flashcards,  work with peers to write a simple dialogue on the theme and share with the class  role play the dialogue while using interjections creatively in groups,  collaboratively compose a simple singing game with interjections. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the steps of writing a simple dialogue? 2. What are interjections?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 8.1.1 Attentive listening
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Attentive listening. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe digital devices for information, b) use polite expressions in an oral conversation, c) enjoy using appropriate and polite expressions during conversations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● Jointly work with peers to describe digital devices based on aspects like colour, height, size, shape, ● work collaboratively to match digital devices to their uses, ● role play a telephone conversation from a call centre with peers articulately, ● list the polite expressions used in the telephone conversation, ● answer questions based on the telephone conversation. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we respond during a telephone conversation? 2. How do we ask questions during conversations?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 8.2.1 Extensive Reading- Adverts and News
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 8.2.1 Extensive Reading- Adverts and News. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe objects from adverts and news for information, b) interpret advertisement and news items for information, c) enjoy viewing advertisements and news items for extensive reading. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  make personal collections from newspaper cuttings e.g. of personal booklet of news,  work collaboratively with peers to view and read the selected advertisements from newspapers and magazines  role play a news report bulletin to describe objects/products based on aspects such as colour, size and shape,  jointly work with peers to use digital devices to recreate content from adverts,  play the ‘Pictionary vocabulary games’ with peers,  read and answer questions on advertisements correctly  prepare posters and adverts for an indigenous product and display in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why are advertisements important? 2. How do we describe objects?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 8.3.1 Functional writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify parts of a simple form for information b) create a form related to the theme c) appreciate value of forms for information SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  in groups, collect a variety of forms and organize them in the portfolio,  discuss the parts of a simple form,  work collaboratively to create a digital form seeking for basic information from peers like name, school, favorite subject, class, favourite cultural food.  share the forms with their friends for filling,  provide information in the forms as per instructions given. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we fill forms?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 9.1.1 Expressing Personal Opinions
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Expressing Personal Opinions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe a real life experience using acquired language, b) use appropriate turn taking and polite interruption skills in a conversation, c) appreciate discussing daily experiences using acquired language strategies. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● describe a real life experience based on the theme using vocabulary acquired , ● listen to an audio recording on appropriate turn taking and polite interruption skills, ● identify verbs from the audio recording, ● practice using verbs in sentences appropriately, ● conduct a panel discussion on the theme while taking into account appropriate turn taking and polite interruption. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to interrupt appropriately in a speech?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 9.2.1 Reading for Comprehension- Poems
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 9.2.1 Reading for Comprehension- Poems. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify components of a poem for comprehension, b) read poems based on the theme for comprehension, c) answer questions from poem based on the theme for comprehension, d) appreciate reading to poems for personal judgement. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  list components of a poem,  read poems based on the theme and make personal judgements,  practice reading short poems and give peer review,  discuss main issues raised in a poem based on leadership,  play a vocabulary game in pairs or small groups,  works jointly with peers to use digital devices to watch poems,  use components of a poem to create own poems,  recite choral poems in class while applying non-verbal cues. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we describe a poem? 2. Why do we read poems?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 9.3.1 Functional writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand the learner should be able to: a) give clear instructions for information, b) create instruction charts for information, c) appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  give clear instructions on a task to be done by peers,  work jointly with peers to identify verbs used in the instructions given,  role play giving instructions based on the theme,  play the ‘simon says’ game to give and respond to clear instructions,  work collaboratively to create instruction charts for information,  share the charts with other members in class for peer assessment. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should we give clear instructions?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Selected Surahs (i) Al-Fatiha (ii) An-Naas (iii) Al-Falaq (iv) Al-Ikhlas (v) Al-Masad (vi) An-Nasr (vii) Al-Kafirun
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 QUR’AN. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Selected Surahs (i) Al-Fatiha (ii) An-Naas (iii) Al-Falaq (iv) Al-Ikhlas (v) Al-Masad (vi) An-Nasr (vii) Al-Kafirun (21 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read and memorise the selected surah for spiritual nourishment b) explain the basic meaning of the selected surah to enhance positive character formation, c) deduce the lessons learnt from the selected surah for spiritual nourishment, d) apply the teachings of the selected surah in his/her daily life, e) appreciate the importance of the selected surahs by adhering to their teachings.

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Read and memorise the selected surahs some Surah with assistance.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) a model of good character
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 HADITH. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) a model of good character (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) read the selected hadith on the character of the Prophet as a role model, b) analyse ways in which Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) is a model of good character, c) emulate the character of the Prophet in his/her daily life. d) value the Prophet as a role model by practicing his character traits in daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read the hadith: “I have been sent for the purpose of perfecting good morals.” (Narrated by Al-Hakim),  discuss ways in which Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) is a model of good character (trustworthy, truthful, kind, and generous) in pairs or small groups and present in class,  role play character traits of the Prophet,  watch/listen to the story of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) from a digital device/teacher. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the character traits of a good child? 2. What were the character traits of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as a youth?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Hadith on Etiquette of Eating
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 HADITH. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Hadith on Etiquette of Eating (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) read the selected hadith on appropriate manners of eating, b) demonstrate the etiquette of eating while taking meals, c) appreciate the etiquette of eating in accordance with the teachings of the Prophet to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read the hadith: “…Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right, and eat what is directly in front of you.” (Narrated by Al- Bukhari),  demonstrate the etiquettes on eating Individually/in small groups,  role play manners of eating,  to watch a video clip on good manners of eating. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you do before eating? 2. What is the benefit of saying Bismillah while eating?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Hadith on brushing teeth
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 HADITH. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Hadith on brushing teeth (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read the selected hadith on brushing teeth for the promotion of oral hygiene, b) assess the importance of brushing teeth as per the tradition of the prophet (S.AW), c) practice brushing teeth as an act of ibadah, d) appreciate the importance of brushing teeth so as to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read the hadith: “Brushing of teeth is a means of purification of mouths and pleasing Allah.” (Narrated by Ibn Majah),  individually demonstrate how to brush his/her teeth,  discuss the importance of brushing their teeth regularly in small groups,  recite/sing song/qasida/poem on brushing teeth. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. When do you brush your teeth? 2. Why do you brush your teeth?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Hadith on Fitness:
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 HADITH. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Hadith on Fitness: (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read the selected Hadith on physical fitness to promote healthy living, b) assess the importance of physical fitness in the life of a Muslim, c) participate in games and sports while observing Islamic values, d) value the importance of physical fitness as means of being dearer to Allah (S.W.T). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read the hadith: “Teach your children swimming, archery and horse riding.” (Narrated by Muslim),  discuss the importance of physical fitness and values derived from participating in games and sports (e.g. teamwork, sharing, humility, fair-play, discipline, and leadership skills) in small groups,  discuss the types of games and sports permissible in Islam in pairs/small groups,  discuss the Islamic etiquettes to be observed during games and sports activities (dressing mode, observing times for swalah) in pairs,  demonstrate the Islamic etiquette to be observed during games. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should one be of physical fitness? 2. What Islamic rules should a Muslim observe while participating in games and sports activities?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Attributes of Allah (S.W.T) Al-Rahman, Al-Rahim, Al-Malik, Al-Salaam, Al- Samiu and Al- Basir
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 PILLARS OF IMAN. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Attributes of Allah (S.W.T) Al-Rahman, Al-Rahim, Al-Malik, Al-Salaam, Al- Samiu and Al- Basir (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) mention the Attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) with their corresponding meaning to strengthen the belief in Allah, b) apply the Attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) while making dua (supplication), c) appreciate the unique Attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) as part of Islamic faith. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to the Attributes of Allah from a digital device,  sing qasida on the Attributes of Allah,  identify Attributes of Allah and their corresponding meaning (Al-Rahman, AL- Rahim, Al-Malik, AL- Salaam, AL-Samiu and Al- Basir),  match and sort the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) and their meaning,  discuss the unique Attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) in pairs or small groups,  demonstrate reciting duas using the mentioned Attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) individually or in pairs. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the favours of Allah (S.W.T.) to mankind? 2. What are the Attributes of Allah (S.W.T.)?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Belief in Angels Jibril, Raqib and Atid, Mikail, Israil and Israfil
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 PILLARS OF IMAN. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Belief in Angels Jibril, Raqib and Atid, Mikail, Israil and Israfil (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) mention names of the angels and their duties as a Pillar of Iman, b) assess the significance of belief in angels in the life of a Muslim, c) appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  name the angels of Allah, (Jibril, Raqib and Atid, Mikail, Israil and Israfil),  match and sort the names of angels and their corresponding duties using flashcards/pocket boards,  find names of angels from a crossword puzzle in pairs or small groups,  search and sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device,  brainstorm on the significance of angels in their lives in pairs or small groups and write the points in their note book. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the duties of angels? 2. Why did Allah (S.W.T.) create angels?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an. Virtues of the Prophets
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 PILLARS OF IMAN. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an. Virtues of the Prophets. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) mention the twenty- five prophets of Allah (S.W.T.) in the Qur’an, b) analyse the virtues of the prophets of Allah for character formation, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify fellow learners named after prophets,  name the prophets of Allah in the Qur’an (Q.4:163- 165, 6:84-86, 21: 85-88) and write in their notebook,  describe the virtues (patience, honesty, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What virtues do we learn from these prophets?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1 Twahara (Ritual Purity) Types of Najasaat
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 DEVOTIONAL ACTS. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Twahara (Ritual Purity) Types of Najasaat (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the types of najasaat (impurities) for physical and spiritual purification, b) demonstrate appropriate ways of cleaning najasaat (impurities) for purpose of purification, c) acknowledge ritual cleanliness as a condition for ibadah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  name the different types of najasaat (mukhaffafah or light, mutawassitah or medium, and mughalladha or heavy),  discuss items used in the purification of najasa in pairs or small groups and present in class,  demonstrate how to purify different najasaat individually/in pairs/in groups. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you purify najasaat? 2. What items do you use in removing najasaat?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.2 Wudhu (Ablution)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 DEVOTIONAL ACTS. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.2 Wudhu (Ablution) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the nullifiers of wudhu (Ablution) so as to maintain a state of ritual purity. b) assess the significance of wudhu in the life of a Muslim, c) value the need to be in a state of purity as a condition for ibadah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search for nullifiers of wudhu (Ablution) using digital devices/from resource books and write in their notebook,  discuss times recommended to be in a state of wudhu and present in class,  discuss the importance of maintaining wudhu in pairs or groups and be guided to write the points in their notebook. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What nullifies wudhu? 2. Why is it important to be in a state of wudhu? 3. When is it recommended to be in a state of wudhu?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Conditions for Swalah
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 DEVOTIONAL ACTS. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Conditions for Swalah (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the conditions for Swalah as a requirement for its validity, b) demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to-day life, c) acknowledge the need for observing the condition for swalah for its validity. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  mention the nine conditions for swalah and be guide to write them in their 1. notebook,  discuss the conditions for Swalah in pairs or groups and present in class,,demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code individually,  demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices/direction of the sun in identifying direction of Qibla individually/in pair/groups,  discuss how to determine times for swalah in pairs /groups and present in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How would you identify time for swalah and direction of Qibla

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3 Pillars of Swalah
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 DEVOTIONAL ACTS. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Pillars of Swalah (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the pillars of swalah as a requirement for its validity, b) apply the pillars of swalah correctly in daily prayers, c) appreciate the need for observing the pillars of swalah by emulating the Sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss the pillars of swalah in pairs/groups and write them in their notebook,  role play the pillars of swalah individually/in pairs/in groups,  watch a video clip of pillars of swalah on digital device,  demonstrate the pillars of swalah individually/in pairs/in groups. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you recite when praying? 2. Which postures are performed in prayers?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to perform Swalah while adhering to all its rules
chunks.sub_strand: Performs Swalah while adhering to all its rules consistently and correctly
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to perform Swalah while adhering to all its rules. SUB-STRAND: Performs Swalah while adhering to all its rules consistently and correctly. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Performs Swalah while adhering to all its rules correctly SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Performs Swalah while adhering to all its rules with few mix-ups KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Performs Swalah while adhering to all its rules with major mix-ups

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1 Virtues: Kindness to Allah’s Creatures
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (MORAL VALUES). SUB-STRAND: 5.1 Virtues: Kindness to Allah’s Creatures (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) assess the significance of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures in the environment, b) demonstrate ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures as an act of ibadah, c) appreciate Allah’s creatures by showing kindness to them. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  mention creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) in their environment,  discuss the significance of being kind to Allah’s creatures in pairs/groups and write the points in their note book,  watch on digital devices/charts/photos appropriate ways of caring for Allah’s creatures (animals/insects/plants/fish),  dramatise ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are some of Allah’s creatures in your environment? 2. Why should you be kind to Allah’s creatures? 3. How can you show kindness to Allah’s creatures?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2 Islamic Manners of Dressing
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (MORAL VALUES). SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Islamic Manners of Dressing (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe appropriate Islamic code of dressing as per the teachings of Islam, b) assess the significance of Islamic code of dressing to enhance character formation, c) observe Islamic manners of dressing as an act of ibadah, d) appreciate Islamic code of dressing as a means of earning rewards from Allah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Learner is guided to:  identify features of the Islamic code of dressing,  watch video clip on a digital device/observe charts/photos of different Islamic attires,  discuss the significance of the Islamic code of dress in pairs or in groups and presents in class,  model an ideal Islamic dress in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How should a Muslim dress? 2. What is the importance of the Islamic code of dress? 3. What are some of the dressing trends that should be avoided by a Muslim?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3 Positive Usage of Media
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 AKHLAQ (MORAL VALUES). SUB-STRAND: 5.3 Positive Usage of Media (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify types of media in the environment so as to reinforce learning, b) explain the positive use of media for Islamic character formation, c) observe Islamic ethics while using media in day- to-day life, d) appreciate media as a gift from Allah (S.W.T.) by using them appropriately. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify different types of media in their environment print media, Internet media (laptops/desktops, videogames, PlayStation), broadcast (TV, Radio and movies) media, mobile phones  watch video clips on positive use of media,  listen to a resource person discussing the Islamic teachings governing the use of media,  discuss the positive and negative uses of media in pairs/ groups and present in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What types of media do you use at home? 2. How can you use media positively? 3. How can you use media while observing Islamic teachings?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4 Prohibitions in Islam Evils of Begging
chunks.text: STRAND: AKHLAQ (MORAL VALUES). SUB-STRAND: 5.4 Prohibitions in Islam Evils of Begging (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify categories of people who deserve, assistance in the society. b) describe the evils of begging as a mean of fostering a work ethic, c) appreciate work as an act of ibadah and a means of eradicating poverty. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Learner is guided to:  identify categories of people deserving support (i.e. debtors, those who loose property through disaster and destitute),  discuss evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam in pair/groups and present in class,  discuss ways of earning income/ generating income in pairs/groups present in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do people beg? 2. Why is begging discouraged?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3 Dua (Supplication) for Leaving and Entering the House
chunks.text: STRAND: AKHLAQ (MORAL VALUES). SUB-STRAND: 5.3 Dua (Supplication) for Leaving and Entering the House (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recite the dua for leaving and entering the house to seek Allah’s protection, b) use the dua in his/her day- to-day life, c) acknowledge the importance of using dua to get protection from Allah (S.W.T.). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Learner is guided to:  recite from a digital device/chart/reference material the dua: dua for leaving the house “in the name of Allah I have placed my trust in Allah; there is no might and no power except by Allah” dua for entering the house “In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do you recite when you leave home for school? 2. What do you recite when entering home from school? 3. Why do you recite the dua when leaving and entering the house?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1 Obligations of Parents to children
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 MUAMALAAT. SUB-STRAND: 6.1 Obligations of Parents to children (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the obligations of parents to their children, b) assess the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children, c) demonstrate ways in which parents can fulfil their obligations to their children, d) cherish love and care given to them by their parents. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  brainstorm parents’ obligations towards their children in pairs/ small groups and write the points in their notebook,  discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children in pairs/ groups and present in class,  role play the obligations of parents to their children,  watch/listen anashid from digital devices on the roles of parents to their children. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are some of the thing’s parents do for their children? 2. why is it important for parents to fulfil their obligation towards their children?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2 Obligations of Children to Parents
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 MUAMALAAT. SUB-STRAND: 6.2 Obligations of Children to Parents (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline obligations of children to their parents, b) assess the importance of obeying and respecting parents as a religious obligation, c) demonstrate ways on how to obey and respect parents, d) appreciate their parents by respecting and obeying them. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss the duties of children to their parents in pair/groups and present in class,  discuss the importance of obeying and respecting their parents (Q 17:23-24) and write the points in their notebook,  dramatise children’s obligations to their parents,  listen to qasidas/anashid (e.g. Ummy) on importance of respecting and obeying parents from a digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you show obedience and respect to your parents? 2. Why should children be dutiful towards their parent?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3 Children’s Obligations to Other Family Members
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 MUAMALAAT. SUB-STRAND: 6.3 Children’s Obligations to Other Family Members (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline obligations of children to other family members as an act of ibadah (worship), b) assess the significance of fulfilling obligations to other family members, c) appreciate maintaining bond with other family members. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  prepare chart with names of extended family members and hang strategically,  discuss children’s obligations to other family members (e.g. Respect, visiting, attending ceremonies, helping and caring for them etc.) in pairs/groups and write the point in their notebook,  brainstorm the significance of fulfilling obligations to other family members in pairs/groups,  dramatise their obligations to other family members. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Who are the other family members? 2. How do you develop good relationship with other family members? 3. What is the significance of strengthening your relationship with other family members?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify the earliest converts to Islam, b) explain the role played by the earliest converts to Islam, c) appreciate the role played by earliest converts to the development of Islam. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  mention the earliest converts in Islam (Khadija (R.a.) Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.) in pair/groups and write them in their note book,  read from reference material/course books on the story of (Khadija (R.a.) Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.) and write the role they played in the Prophet’s mission,  listen to a resource person discussing the role played by earliest converts. (E.g. First person to accept Islam, moral and material support, and lives etc.),  listen to a story on Khadija (R.A), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.) from a resource person/digital device. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What role did earliest converts play in the Prophet’s mission?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the prophet’s incidence at cave Hira with Angel Jibril (A.S.), b) assess the significance of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W) in relation to seeking knowledge, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch audio-visual clip/listen to a story from a digital device/resource person on prophet’s experience at cave Hira,  read from reference material story on call to prophethood and narrates to others in class, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the teachings of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W)?

chunks.text: STRAND: 7. HISTORY OF ISLAM. SUB-STRAND: 7.3 Prophet (S.A.W.)’s journey to Taif (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) narrate the story of the Prophet (s.a.w)’s journey to Taif, b) demonstrate the virtues exhibited by the Prophet (S.A.W) in his journey to Taif, c) appreciate the virtues demonstrated by the Prophet (S.A.W) while in Taif. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen/watch a story on the Prophet (s.a.w)’s journey to Taif from a digital device/ resource person and retell individually in class,  identify the virtues learnt from the Prophet (s.a.w)’s journey to Taif and display them on a chart,  brainstorm on the situations that require exhibition of the following virtues: (patience, tolerance and perseverance) pairs/groups and present in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What lessons can Muslims learn from the Prophet (s.a.w)’s journey toTaif? 2. How did the Prophet (s.a.w) treat the people of Taif?

chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 4)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 4). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua silabi zinazotokana na sauti p/b, t/d, k/g, ch/j katika maneno, b) kutamka silabi zinazotokana na sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi, c) kutamka vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa kwa silabi za sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi, d) kuunda vitanzandimi kutokana na sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa (p/b, t/d, k/g, ch/j) kutokana na maneno kwenye vitabu, ubaoni au kwa kutumia vifaa vya kidijitali,  kusikiliza silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kidijitali k.v. kinasasauti na rununu,  kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa na vitanzandimi akiwa na wenzake,  kusikiliza vitanzandimi vilivyoundwa kutokana na maneno yenye sauti lengwa vikikaririwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au katika vifaa vya kidijitali (k.m. baba alivua papa katika bahari pana, kila Chacha akila hali chakula kikichacha),  kuunda vitanzandimi vyepesi vinavyotokana na vitate husika akiwa na wenzake,  kuunda vitanzandimi kwenye vifaa vya kidijitali na KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Matamshi bora yana umuhimu gani katika mawasiliano?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati wa mada lengwa uliotumika katika kifungu cha hadithi ili kuimarisha ufahamu, b) kutumia msamiati lengwa kwa usahihi katika sentensi, c) kutoa muhtasari wa ujumbe wa kifungu cha hadithi, d) kujenga mazoea ya usomaji bora katika maisha ya kila siku. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua msamiati wa nyumbani (k.v. meza, sebule, balbu/globu, kizingiti, fremu, neti, tendegu, mtoto wa meza, mvungu, figa, kinu, tumbuu, kochi, kupiga deki) uliotumiwa katika kifungu cha hadithi,  kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili maana na matumizi ya msamiati lengwa katika sentensi,  kuimba nyimbo zinazolenga msamiati lengwa,  kusoma kifungu kinachohusiana na suala lengwa kwenye kitabu au kwenye tarakilishi akiwa na wenzake,  kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu alichosoma,  kutoa muhtasari wa ujumbe wa kifungu alichokisoma,  kumweleza mzazi au mlezi wake ujumbe wa kifungu alichokisoma. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unazingatia nini ili kupata ujumbe katika kifungu cha hadithi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Kuandika Insha ya Wasifu (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Kuandika Insha ya Wasifu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia muundo, b) kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, mtindo na muundo ufaao, c) kuchangamkia utunzi mzuri wa insha ya wasifu ili kujenga ubunifu wake. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kujadili na wenzake maana ya insha ya wasifu,  kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha vilivyoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kujadili na wenzake mada ya insha na muundo wa insha ya wasifu akiwa,  kuandaa vidokezo vitakavyomwongoza kuandika insha yake,  kuandika insha inayoeleza sifa za mtu kama vile mzazi au mlezi, rafiki, mwalimu au kiongozi yeyote kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati nadhifu, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa ubunifu,  kuandika insha ya wasifu mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili waisome na kuitathmini. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unazingatia mambo gani unapoandika insha nzuri ya wasifu?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.1 Nomino (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.1 Nomino (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kueleza maana ya nomino ili kuitofautisha na aina nyingine za maneno, b) kutambua nomino katika kundi la maneno na sentensi, c) kutumia nomino kwa njia sahihi katika sentensi, d) kuonea fahari matumizi ya nomino katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya nomino,  kutambua nomino katika matini mbalimbali,  kushirikiana na wenzake kutoa mifano ya nomino,  kuchagua nomino kwenye tarakilishi, kuziburura na kuzitia kapuni akiwa na wenzake,  kutumia nomino kujaza nafasi katika sentensi,  kutumia nomino kutunga sentensi kwenye daftari na mtandaoni ili wenzake wazisome na kuzisahihisha. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni vitu gani unavyoweza kupata katika mazingira yako?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.2 Vitenzi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.2 Vitenzi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kueleza maana ya vitenzi ili kuvitofautisha na aina nyingine za maneno, b) kutambua vitenzi katika kundi la maneno na sentensi, c) kutumia vitenzi ipasavyo katika mawasiliano, d) kuonea fahari matumizi ya vitenzi katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kushirikiana na wenzake kwa amani kueleza maana ya vitenzi,  kushirikiana na wenzake kutoa mifano ya vitenzi (k.v. soma, andika, keti, simama, cheka) katika kadi za maneno, kapu maneno, ubao, vifaa vya kidijitali n.k.,  kutambua vitendo vinavyofanyika katika picha au michoro,  kuigiza vitenzi mbalimbali akishirikiana na wenzake,  kutumia vitenzi kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi na kifungu kifupi,  kutumia vitenzi mbalimbali kutunga sentensi daftarini au mtandaoni kwa kuzingatia suala lengwa na masuala mtambuko mbalimbali,  kuwashirikisha wenzake katika kuzisahihisha sentensi zake na kumpa maoni kwa heshima. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni shughuli gani unazofanya kila siku?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.3 Vivumishi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.3 Vivumishi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kueleza maana ya kivumishi ili kukitofautisha na aina nyingine za maneno, b) kutambua vivumishi katika kundi la maneno na sentensi, c) kutumia vivumishi ipasavyo katika sentensi na kifungu, d) kuonea fahari matumizi ya vivumishi katika sentensi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya kivumishi,  kutambua vivumishi katika kundi la maneno aliyopewa (k.m. -zuri, -baya, - refu, -fupi, -eusi, -eupe, n.k),  kuchagua vivumishi kwenye tarakilishi, kuviburura na kuvitia kapuni akiwa na wenzake,  kutumia vivumishi kujaza nafasi katika sentensi,  kutumia vivumishi kutunga sentensi daftarini na mtandaoni akizingatia masuala mtambuko mbalimbali yakiwemo masuala ya usalama wa mtandaoni, usawa wa kijinsia, usalama wa nyumbani, mahusiano ya kijamii, n.k,  kuandika aya fupi akitumia vivumishi mbalimbali,  kuwasomea au kuwasambazia wenzake kazi yake ili kuitolea maoni kwa heshima na upendo. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni sifa zipi unazoweza kutambua katika nomino mbalimbali?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Maamkuzi na Maagano (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Maamkuzi na Maagano (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua aina mbalimbali za maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano, b) kueleza maamkuzi na maagano yanayotumika katika miktadha mbalimbali, c) kutumia aina mbalimbali za maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano, d) kuchangamkia maamkuzi na maagano katika mahusiano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua maamkuzi (k.v. U mzima? U hali gani? Alamsiki, Lala unono, Siku njema) kutoka kwenye chati, ubao au vifaa vya kidijitali, michoro na picha,  kushiriki mjadala na mwenzake kuhusu maamkuzi na maagano yanayolengwa na matumizi yake,  kushirikiana na wenzake kuigiza maamkuzi na maagano lengwa,  kutazama watu wakiamkuana na kuagana katika vifaa vya kidijitali,  kuambatanisha maamkuzi na maagano na majibu sahihi daftarini au kwenye tarakilishi,  kujadiliana na mzazi au mlezi wake kuhusu maamkuzi na maagano yanayotumiwa katika jamii yao. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, watu husalimiana na kuagana vipi katika jamii yako? 2. Kuamkua na kuaga watu kuna umuhimu gani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Matumizi ya Kamusi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Matumizi ya Kamusi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kueleza maana ya kamusi ili kuitofautisha na vitabu vingine, b) kutumia kamusi ipasavyo kutafuta maana za maneno asiyoyajua ili kukuza msamiati wake, c) kuchangamkia umuhimu wa kamusi katika kukuza msamiati wake. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kujadiliana na wenzake kuhusu maana na matumizi ya kamusi,  kujadiliana na wenzake kuhusu mpangilio wa maneno katika kamusi,  kutumia kamusi kutafuta maana za maneno mbalimbali akiwa na wenzake,  kutumia mtandao kusikiliza na kusoma maelezo kuhusu msamiati anaotafutia maana. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unazingatia nini unapotafuta maneno katika kamusi?

chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Insha ya Masimulizi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua insha ya masimulizi kwa kuzingatia muundo, b) kuandika insha ya masimulizi inayozingatia mada, ujumbe, mtindo na muundo ufaao, c) kuchangamkia utunzi mzuri wa insha ya masimulizi ili kukuza ubunifu wake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Insha ya masimulizi inahusu nini? 2. Je, unazingatia nini unapoandika insha ya masimulizi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4.1 Viwakilishi (Vipindi 2 )
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.1 Viwakilishi (Vipindi 2 ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kueleza maana ya kiwakilishi ili kukibainisha, b) kutambua viwakilishi katika kundi la maneno na sentensi, c) kutumia viwakilishi ipasavyo katika sentensi, d) kuonea fahari matumizi ya viwakilishi katika mawasiliano. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni maneno gani yanayoweza kutumika badala ya nomino?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unafanyaje shughuli zako za kila siku?

chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Kusikiliza na kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 2). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutafiti maana ya kitendawili kwenye kamusi, vitabuni au mtandaoni akiwa na wenzake,  kutambua vitendawili katika chati, ubao au katika vifaa vya kidijitali (k.m. Nifungue nikufunike (Mwavuli); Pitia huku nami nipitie kule, tupatane pale (mshipi); Ukinitembelea nyayo zi salama (viatu),  kusikiliza vitendawili vikitegwa na kuteguliwa kupitia vyombo vya kidijitali.  kushiriki katika kutega na kutegua vitendawili akiwa na wenzake,  kujadiliana na mzazi au mlezi wake kuhusu vitendawili vinavyotegwa katika jamii yao. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unazingatia nini unapotega na kutegua vitendawili?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili

chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kujadili vipengele vya kuzingatia katika kusoma kwa ufasaha, b) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora, c) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti, d) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo, e) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kwa kuambatanisha ishara zifaazo, f) kuchangamkia kusoma kwa ufasaha ili kufanikisha mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe: ● kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili vipengele vya kuzingatia katika kusoma makala kwa ufasaha,  kusikiliza na kutazama mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa, mwanafunzi mwenzake au video za watu wanaosoma makala kwa ufasaha (k.v. hotuba na habari),  kujadili na wenzake vipengele vya kuzingatia katika kusoma kwa ufasaha vilivyozingatiwa katika usomaji alioutazama,  kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akiwa na wenzake,  kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti (k.v. kiwango cha sauti na kiimbo), ● kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno yasiyopungua 70 kwa dakika na kwa kuzingatia KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unazingatia nini ili kuweza kusoma kifungu cha hadithi ipasavyo?

chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Kuandika kwa kutumia tarakilishi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sehemu mbalimbali za tarakilishi zinazotumika kupigia chapa, b) kufungua na kufunga tarakilishi ili kuandika kazi na kuihifadhi, c) kuandika mada lengwa kwa kutumia tarakilishi, d) kuhariri kazi yake kwa kuzingatia uakifishaji ufaao, e) kuhifadhi kazi aliyoiandika kwenye tarakilishi, f) kujenga mazoea ya kuandika kwa kutumia tarakilishi na kuhifadhi kazi yake ya maandishi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua sehemu za kimsingi za tarakilishi za kupigia chapa akiwa na wenzake (k.v. kiibodi, kipanya, kiwambo, kitufe na faili),  kuzingatia hatua za kufungua na kufunga tarakilishi,  kuandika mada lengwa kwa kutumia tarakilishi akizingatia chapa koza, italiki na kupigia mistari panapofaa,  kuandika aya kuhusu mavazi katika tarakilishi na kuihariri,  kutumia mtandao kusambaza kazi aliyoandika ili wenzake na mwalimu waitathmini,  kuhifadhi kazi yake kwenye faili ya tarakilishi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unazingatia nini unapoandika kwa kutumia tarakilishi?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya viunganishi,  kutambua viunganishi katika kundi la maneno aliyopewa (k.v. na, pia, kwa sababu, lakini),  kutafiti vitabuni au mtandaoni ili kutoa mifano mbalimbali ya viunganishi,  kutumia viunganishi kujaza nafasi katika sentensi,  kutumia viunganishi kutunga sentensi daftarini au mtandaoni kwa kuzingatia suala lengwa na masuala mtambuko mbalimbali,  kumsomea mzazi au mlezi wake sentensi alizozitunga. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, kwa nini ni muhimu kutumia viunganishi katika mawasiliano?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya vihusishi na kuvitolea mifano (k.m. karibu na, mbali na, juu ya, chini ya, nje ya na ndani ya),  kutambua vihusishi katika kundi la maneno aliyopewa,  kuchagua vihusishi kwenye kundi la maneno katika tarakilishi, kuviburura na kuvitia kapuni akiwa peke yake au kwenye vikundi,  kutumia vihusishi kutunga sentensi daftarini au mtandaoni kwa kuzingatia suala lengwa na masuala mtambuko mbalimbali,  kuwasomea au kuwasambazia wenzake na mwalimu sentensi alizotunga ili kuzitathmini. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Vihusishi vina umuhimu gani katika mawasiliano?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kutumia vihisishi katika mawasiliano kuna umuhimu gani?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kutumia maneno ya upole kuna umuhimu gani katika mawasiliano?

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Kusoma kwa Mapana (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua na kufungua faili iliyo na kifungu cha kusoma, b) kutambua na kuzingatia hatua za kiusalama katika matumizi ya vifaa vya kidijitali, c) kusakura matini kwenye tovuti salama ili kupata vifungu vya kusoma vyenye mada lengwa, d) kutumia vifaa vya kidijitali kwa urahisi kupata SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua na kuzingatia hatua za kiusalama (k.m. kutowasiliana na watu asiowajua, kuwajibika anaposakura tovuti mbalimbali) kutoka kwenye chati au kwenye tarakilishi na mitandao,  kutambua jina la faili lengwa kwenye tarakilishi na kufanya mazoezi ya kufungua na kufunga,  kutambua mitandao salama yenye matini inayoafiki kiwango na mahitaji yake,  kutambua umuhimu wa kutoa habari kwa mwalimu, mzazi au mlezi wake endapo atapata ujumbe kutoka kwa watu asiowajua mtandaoni na kutowasiliana nao,  kutafuta maana za maneno kuhusu mada lengwa (k.m. kaskazini, kusini, magharibi, mashariki, kaskazini mashariki, kaskazini magharibi, kusini KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Ni hatua zipi za kiusalama unazofaa kuzingatia unapotumia mtandao?

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Kuandika Barua ya Kirafiki (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua barua ya kirafiki kwa kuzingatia muundo wake, b) kujadili umuhimu wa barua ya kirafiki katika mawasiliano, c) kuandika barua ya kirafiki inayozingatia mada kwa kufuata kanuni zifaazo, d) kuchangamkia utunzi wa barua ya kirafiki katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua barua ya kirafiki kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya barua za kirafiki zilizoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kujadiliana na wenzake kuhusu umuhimu wa barua za kirafiki katika mawasiliano,  kujadili na wenzake mada ya barua ya kirafiki na vipengele vyake/ yale yanayofaa kujumuishwa,  kuandaa vidokezo vitakavyomwongoza kuandika insha yake,  kuandika barua ya kirafiki kwa rafiki, ndugu, mzazi, n.k kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati safi, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa lugha ya kiubunifu,  kuwasomea wenzake na mwalimu KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, unazingatia nini ili kuandika barua nzuri ya kirafiki? 2. Barua za kirafiki inashughulikia masuala gani?

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 4.4.1 Ngeli ya A-WA (Vipindi 4). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua methali kuhusu malezi (k.v. mtoto umleavyo ndivyo akuavyo, mtoto wa nyoka ni nyoka na mtoto hutazama kisogo cha nina) kutoka kwa orodha ya methali, chati au mtandaoni,  kueleza maana za methali kuhusu malezi akiwa na wenzake,  kukamilisha methali kuhusu malezi,  kutumia methali kuhusu malezi katika kifungu kifupi na masimulizi akiwa na wenzake  kushirikiana na mzazi au mlezi wake kutambua methali kuhusu malezi katika jamii yao. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Ni methali gani zinazohusu malezi? 2. Methali hutumiwa kufanya nini?

chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kueleza maana ya shairi, ubeti na mshororo ili kuvibainisha, b) kusoma shairi kwa ufasaha kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, c) kutambua beti na mishororo katika shairi, d) kutambua shairi kutokana na umbo lake, e) kufurahia kutumia lugha ya ushairi anapozungumzia ushairi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua shairi, beti na mishororo katika matini mbalimbali kama vile vitabu, chati na vilevile kwa kutumia tarakilishi,  kushiriki katika majadiliano kuhusu maana za shairi, ubeti na mishororo,  kusoma akizingatia msamiati wa mada lengwa,  kusikiliza mashairi yanayokaririwa kwenye vifaa vya kidijitali,  kusoma au kukariri shairi kwa mahadhi mbalimbali akizingatia ujumbe,  kushiriki mjadala kuhusu ujumbe unaojitokeza kwenye shairi,  kusoma mashairi kwenye mitandao. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Unaufahamu msamiati gani wa ushairi? 2. Mashairi yanaweza kuwasilisha ujumbe gani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili

chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Kuandika Insha ya Maelezo (Vipindi 2). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Insha ya maelezo inahusu nini? 2. Unazingatia nini unapoandika insha ya maelezo?
