SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify the characteristics of animals as living things, b) distinguish vertebrates from invertebrates in the environment, c) Appreciate the need to care for animals. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to: ● take a walk in the school compound and adjacent environment to observe, discuss and record evidence that animals: feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond to changes in their environment and die, ● search for information from print and non-print materials on characteristics of animals as living things and discuss with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are animals grouped as living things?

chunks.subject: Science and Technology
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Properties of matter  ● Meaning of matter ● States of matter (solid, liquid and gas) ● Properties of matter (shape, volume and mass) ● Importance of the different states of matter
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Matter. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Properties of matter ● Meaning of matter ● States of matter (solid, liquid and gas) ● Properties of matter (shape, volume and mass) ● Importance of the different states of matter (14 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) categorise substances in the environment into the three states of matter, b) describe the properties of the three states of matter, c) appreciate the importance of the different states of matter in day to day life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● brainstorm on the meaning of matter and identify its different states (solid, liquid and gases), ● collect and group different substances from the environment into the three states of matter collaboratively, ● carry out activities to demonstrate the properties of the three states of matter (shape, volume and mass) with peers, ● discuss the importance of the different states of matter in day to day life, ● where possible use digital devices to observe the characteristics of the three states of matter. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the properties of matter?

chunks.subject: Science and Technology
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Management of solid waste  ● Types of solid wastes (decomposing and non-decomposing (plastic, metals, food wrappers, kitchen waste) ● Dangers of solid waste to the environment ● Managing wastes in places (classrooms, schools, home, public functions) ● Methods of managing solid waste (reuse, reduce and recycle) ● Safety measures
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Matter. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Management of solid waste ● Types of solid wastes (decomposing and non-decomposing (plastic, metals, food wrappers, kitchen waste) ● Dangers of solid waste to the environment ● Managing wastes in places (classrooms, schools, home, public functions) ● Methods of managing solid waste (reuse, reduce and recycle) ● Safety measures (16 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) classify solid waste into decomposable and non- decomposable, b) describe the dangers of solid waste to the environment, c) apply appropriate methods to manage solid waste in the environment, d) appreciate the need for proper management of solid waste in the environment. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Learner is guided to: ● identify solid waste in the environment with peers, ● discuss the meaning of decomposable and non- decomposable solid waste, ● collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing collaboratively, ● discuss the dangers of solid waste to the environment and present in class, ● discuss methods of managing different types of waste in their environment (To include Re-using, Recycling and Reducing), Hint: Include common waste in school and KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How is solid waste dangerous to the environment?

chunks.subject: Science and Technology
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Water conservation  ● Meaning of water conservation ● Methods of conserving water (cover: Simple examples of reducing water wastage, Reusing water and Recycling water ● Importance of water conservation
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Matter. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the meaning of water conservation in the environment, b) describe methods of conserving water at home and school, c) outline the importance of conserving water at home and school, d) develop interest in conserving water at home and school. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Learner is guided to: ● Brainstorm on how water is wasted at home and school, ● brainstorm on the meaning of water conservation, ● explore their locality and observe how water is conserved with peers, ● discuss ways of conserving water (simple examples of reducing water wastage, Reusing water and Recycling water), ● discuss the importance of conserving water, ● practise responsible use of water at home and school. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to conserve water?

chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Force and Energy. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe types of forces in nature, b) demonstrate the effects of force on objects in nature, c) describe the uses of force in daily life, d) appreciate the importance of force in day-to- day life. chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Compass Direction
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Natural and Built Environment s. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Compass Direction (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the four cardinal points of a compass, b) use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map, c) appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm the four cardinal points, ● practice giving directions to places using the four cardinal points, ● draw and label the four cardinal points, ● play computer games on the compass direction for enjoyment, ● use the four compass points to show direction on the interactive map to enrich the mapping skills. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we show direction of places?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2 Location and size of the County
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Natural and Built Environments. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Location and size of the County (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify sub-counties in the counties, b) locate the county in relation to neighboring counties, c) estimate the size of the county in relation to neighbouring counties, d) acknowledge the location and size of the county. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm and identify sub-counties in their County. ● use relevant print of digital resources to identify the location of the County in relation to neighbouring counties ● discuss the size of the county in relation to the neigbouring counties ● sketch, colour, and display the map of the County in class. ● play games on the location of the county in relation to neighbouring counties. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to learn the size and location of a county?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Physical features in the County
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Natural and Built Environments. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Physical features in the County (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the main physical features in the County, b) illustrate the main physical features in the County, c) state the importance of the main physical features in the County, d) embrace responsible behavior to conserve physical features. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm the main physical features in the County (Vegetation, mountains, hills, rivers, lakes, oceans, valleys and plains,) ● sketch the main physical features in the county, ● use digital resources to draw or take photographs of the main physical features in the county, ● use print resources to draw or take photographs of the main physical features in the county, ● discuss the importance of the main physical features in the county and share the discussion points in class, ● model some of the main physical features in the county, ● display pictures or models of the main physical features in the county in class, ● find out from parents or guardians how to KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are physical features important for a County?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 Seasons in the County
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Natural and Built Environments. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 Seasons in the County (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify seasons experienced in the county, b) explain how seasons influence human activities in the county, c) model weather charts of seasons in the county, d) appreciate the different seasons experienced in the county. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● use print or digital resources to identify seasons experienced in the county (Hot, cold, dry and rainy season), ● brainstorm about seasons experienced in the County, ● sing songs about seasons experienced in the County, ● observe and record in charts human activities associated with different seasons. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do seasons influence human activities in the county?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 1.5 Historic built environments in the County
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Natural and Built Environmen ts. SUB-STRAND: 1.5 Historic built environments in the County (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the main historic built environments in the County, b) explain the importance of the main historic built environments in the County, c) state ways of caring for historic built environments in the County, d) participate in SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm and share the main historic built environments in the County (Museums, monuments, Cultural centers), ● use print or digital resources to identify historic built environments in the county, ● visit some of the historic built environments within the locality (take photographs, audio tape conversations on the environments or take notes), ● engage the resource person to discuss the importance of the KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we care for the historic built environments in our County?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Inter- dependence of people
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 People and Population. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Inter- dependence of people (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify ways in which people depend on each other in the County, b) explain the benefits of inter- dependence of people in the County, c) appreciate inter- dependence of people in the County. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm in class the ways in which people depend on each other in the County, ● use print or digital resources to identify ways in which people depend on each other in the County, ● create a chart on benefits of interdependence among the people, ● role-play inter-dependence of people (market, farming ,hospital, church, mosque), ● recite a poem about the importance of inter-dependence of people, ● find out from parents or guardians about the importance of inter- dependence of people and report back. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do people in the County depend on each other? 2. Why should we support each other in the County?

chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Population distribution
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 People and Population. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Population distribution (5 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe patterns of population distribution in the County, b) design the patterns of population distribution in the County, c) appreciate population distribution in the County. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● discuss population distribution in the County, ● use a digital map or print of the County to identify the patterns of population, distribution in the County, ● share the diagrams of the patterns on population distribution in class, ● use the map of the County to plot patterns of population distribution, ● draw a map of the county showing population distribution, ● display the map of the County in the appropriate learning corner. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How is population spread out in the County?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Culture and Social Organizations. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify aspects of traditional culture in the County, b) describe aspects of traditional culture in the County, c) appreciate the importance of traditional culture in the County. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm to identify aspects of traditional culture in the County. (dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, festivals and ceremonies) ● describe aspects of traditional culture in the County. ● discuss the importance of traditional culture in the County. ● collect and record aspects of traditional culture in the community. (pictures ,songs, artefacts, dress, food, paintings, tools) ● display different aspects of traditional culture in class ● conduct peer assessment of the displays. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is culture important?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2. The school
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Culture and Social Organizations. SUB-STRAND: 3.2. The school (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) narrate the history of the school, b) recite the school motto, c) explain the values of the school, d) desire to obey the school rules. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● gather information on “The history of the school” from the school administration and share in class, ● participate in the designing of school motto and rules, ● discuss the history of the school with others in class, ● recite the school motto, ● create a journal on the history of the school, ● use digital or print resources to develop a poster on the school motto, ● use digital or print resources to develop a poster on the school values core values and display it in class, ● display, make a gallery walk and peer assess. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to maintain discipline in school?

chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Resources and Economic Activities. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Resources in the County ( 4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the main resources found in the county, b) identify the main economic activities carried out in the county, c) explain the importance of economic activities carried out in the county, d) participate in economic activities in the county, e) desire to conserve resources in the county. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● use print or digital resources to ● identify the main resources found in the county ● collect and display samples of resources in learning corners. (Observe safety) ● brainstorm the resources and economic activities in the county ● make posters on the resources and activities found in the county ● recite poems and sing songs on the resources and economic activities in their county ● play relevant educational computer games on economic KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we conserve the resources found in the county?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Trade and Industries in the County
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Resources and Economic Activities. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Trade and Industries in the County (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to; a) identify industries in the County, b) locate industries in the County, c) explain the benefits of industries in the County, d) identify methods of trade in the county e) explore the benefits of trade in the County, f) appreciate lawful trading activities in the County. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm the industries in the County, ● discuss the benefits of industries in the County, ● brainstorm on types of trade in the County (Barter & Currency), ● use digital and print resources to locate industries in the county ● visit a trading centre to learn more about trading activities and report back, ● role-play trading activities, ● discuss the benefits of industries in the County, ● visit and take photos or video clips of industries found in the County, ● create a journal of industries visited and share with others in class, ● collect and display sample products from industries in the classroom, ● care and conserve resources in the county. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can a county benefit from its industries?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3 Enterprise Project at school
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Resources and Economic Activities. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Enterprise Project at school (7 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) Identify the projects that can be initiated at school, b) participate in initiating an enterprise project at school, c) uphold ethics in managing the enterprise project money at the school, d) appreciate collective efforts in the success of enterprise project at school. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm and identify enterprise projects that can be undertaken at school, ● use digital or print resources to search for enterprise projects undertaken in schools, ● plan for a viable enterprise project at school. ● participate in the initiation and management of the enterprise project in the school ● share responsibilities on the planned enterprise project. ● discuss ethical practices to be observed in managing the enterprise project (money, final products). ● undertake the enterprise project at school and evaluate its success. ● participate in the school entrepreneurship week. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can enterprise projects have initiated and managed?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1 Good citizenship in school
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Citizenship. SUB-STRAND: 5.1 Good citizenship in school (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify qualities of good citizens in school, b) exhibit qualities of good citizenship in school, c) appreciate qualities of good citizenship in school. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm qualities of a good citizen in school ● discuss how to become a good citizen in school ● use digital or print resources to identify qualities of a good citizen in school ● role play qualities of a good citizen in a school ● design a poster with qualities of a good citizen in school ● engage a resource person to discuss the importance of good citizenship ● write an essay on a good digital citizen (using technology in a positive way) and share the essays in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we demonstrate good citizenship in school?

chunks.subject: Social Studies
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2 Peace
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Citizenship. SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Peace (4 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify factors that promote peace in school, b) explain ways of living in peace with others in school, c) uphold peace in school, d) appreciate living together in peace in society. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● discuss ways of promoting peace in school ● brainstorm ways of living in peace with others ● role- plays a peaceful situation ● use digital or print resources to create messages on peace and display them at strategic points in the school compound ● brainstorm and identify peace activities that can be undertaken at school. ● use digital or print resources to find out examples of peace activities undertaken in schools (Peace gardens/nature trails, Peace corners, Peace competition essays). ● plan a peace-building activity in the school ● share responsibilities on the planned peace-building activity KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can we live in peace with others in school? 2. Why is it important to plan for a peace building activity in school?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify forms of child abuse in the community, b) identify cultural practices that are harmful to children, c) explain effects of child abuse in the community, d) protect self and others from child abuse in the community, e) desire to promote child Rights and responsibilities in the community. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to: ● brainstorm forms of child abuse in the community (Early and forced marriages, Female genital mutilation, Slavery, Child Trafficking, child labour, Sexual abuse, abuse of children with special needs), ● use digital or print resources to identify cultural practices that violate child rights in the community, ● engage a resource person to identify cultural practices that violate child rights in the community, ● discuss effects of child abuse in the community, ● design posters on the effects of child abuse in the community, ● sing songs and recite poems on the protection of self and others from child abuse in the community, ● participate in a campaign to promote child Rights and responsibilities in the community. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can harmful cultural practices violate child rights in the community? 2. How can we protect ourselves from child abuse?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Soil Conservation
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Soil Conservation (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community b) Construct organic waste pit for soil improvement c) Demonstrate use of plant remains for soil improvement. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss and identify sites in the school or community that have poor soil for crop growth. • Construct a pit, a site or a structure for damping plant residue and suitable food remains and organic kitchen wastes in school. • Plant crop in a residue pit to observe and appreciate soil improvement from accumulated organic wastes. • Develop observation skills as they identify appropriate site; value of unity as they work to construct the pit; and environmental awareness while recycling organic wastes in the pit method to improve the soil. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we improve the soil using suitable organic wastes?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2. Water Conservation
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.2. Water Conservation (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify ways of conserving water for household gardening b) Practice water conservation within the school or community c) Appreciate importance of conserving water in the community. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Use devices or other resources to search for information on ways of water conservation such as mulching, cover cropping and shading in kitchen and backyard gardening. • Make presentations to share experiences on importance of conserving water (mulching, cover cropping and shading) in kitchen and backyard gardening activities. • Practice various ways of conserving water in farming (Mulching, shading, cover cropping) within the school. • In groups learners to experiment on mulching (mulch some crops and leave others un-mulched and compare moisture conservation). • Develop learning to learn by engaging in self-driven task of water conservation; responsible use of devices to search for KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we conserve soil water in household gardening practices?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3 Conserving Wild Animals
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Conservation of Resources. SUB-STRAND: 1.3 Conserving Wild Animals (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify ways of repelling wild animals to avoid damage of property b) Repel wild animals to avoid destruction of property c) Appreciate importance of living better with wild animals. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Watch video clips or listen to a resource person on safe ways of repelling wild animals (such as use of smoke, smells) to avoid damage on property (crops and domestic animals) and live better with wild animals. • Innovate safe ways of repelling small wild animals (smoke, use of smell repellant or any other). • Develop critical thinking skills to solve the problem of destruction of property; demonstrate value of patriotism as they care the environment by conserving biodiversity. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we repel wild animals to avoid destruction of property?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Growing Vegetables
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Growing Vegetables (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify gardening practices for vegetables b) Establish a nursery bed for vegetables c) Grow vegetable crop after transplanting d) Appreciate the importance of vegetables in provision healthy meals diet. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Brainstorm and share experiences on gardening practices of vegetables in a nursery bed. • Prepare a nursery bed (container or ground nursery), sow vegetable seed and take care of the seedling. • Make class presentations importance of growing vegetables as a source of food for animals and humans. • Develop self-efficacy in producing their own vegetable foods; demonstrate the value of social justice in sharing of tasks; and financial literacy skills by reducing daily vegetable purchases. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does growing vegetables contribute to food production?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Uses of Domestic Animals
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Uses of Domestic Animals (8 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify uses of various domestic animals in food production b) Relate various domestic animals to their uses c) Appreciate the importance of domestic animals in food production. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Brainstorm and share experiences on the uses of domestic animals in food production (bees, rabbits, camels, fish, pigs, donkeys, dogs and cats). • Match domestic animals to their uses. • Make class presentations on importance of domestic animals in food production while relating contributions of all the scoped animals. • Develop communication skills as they present the uses of domestic animals; demonstrate patriotism as they appreciate diversity of animals in the country; and appreciate importance of animals in food security. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How are domestic animals important in food production?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe methods of preserving cereals and pulses the locality b) Preserve cereals and pulses for food security c) Appreciate the importance of preserving cereals and pulses for food security. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Brainstorm and share experiences on methods of preserving and storing cereals and pulses (such as sun drying, use of ashes, use of airtight containers) at household level. • Preserve and store cereals and pulses using methods such as sun drying, use of ash and airtight containers. • Make class presentations to share experiences on importance of preserving and storing cereals and pulses. • Develop critical thinking skills to solve the problem of food spoilage; value of unity as learners make class presentations; and food security awareness in preserving foods. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does preservation and storage of cereals and pulses enhance food security?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Food Nutrients
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Food Nutrients (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Explain functions of food nutrients in the body b) Categorize foods based on their major nutrients c) Identify nutritional diseases and disorders associated with poor eating habits d) Appreciate the importance of various nutrients in the body. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Search and share information on functions of food nutrients (carbohydrates, vitamins, proteins, fats). • Use real food materials, photographs, to categorize foods based on their major nutrients (protein rich foods, carbohydrates rich foods, vitamins and minerals rich foods). • Make class presentations on the importance of various nutrients in the body. • Use print and digital devices to search for information on various nutritional diseases and disorders such as kwashiorkor, marasmus, goiter and anaemia. • Develop digital literacy as they search for information on nutrients; value of unity as they make presentations; and health promotion awareness skills as they learn about the importance of nutrients in the body. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is the knowledge of food nutrients important in food production?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 2.5 Dry Fat Frying and Deep Frying
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Food Production Processes. SUB-STRAND: 2.5 Dry Fat Frying and Deep Frying (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe dry fat frying and deep frying as methods of cooking b) Cook food using dry fat frying and deep frying methods c) Embrace dry fat frying and deep frying in food production. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Watch video clip or demonstration on dry fat frying and deep frying methods of cooking. • Cook and serve dry fried and deep fried foods. • Develop learning to learn while working cautiously to carry out dry frying and deep frying; responsibility while following the cooking steps; and observe safety measures while working with fire and fats. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we cook foods using dry fat frying and deep frying methods?

chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Hygiene Practices. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Good Grooming Practices (7 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe good grooming as a daily health habit b) Practice good grooming as a daily health habit c) Appreciate good grooming as a healthy habit. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss and share experiences on aspects of good grooming such dressing for different occasions. • Demonstrate different ways of dressing and etiquette for different activities. • Adopt good grooming while carrying out daily chores. • Develop self-efficacy while promoting good grooming; respect by appreciating others; and personal hygiene to promote preventive health. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does good grooming promote personal hygiene?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Home Hygiene
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Hygiene Practices. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Home Hygiene (9 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify surfaces made from different materials in home environment b) Clean different types of surfaces in the home environment c) Appreciate living in a clean home environment to promote healthy living. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Discuss and share experiences on surfaces made from different materials such as glass, wooden, earthen floors, cemented and tiled. • Clean different types of surfaces such as glass, wooden, earthen floors, cemented and tiled. • Develop listening and speaking skills while brainstorming; unity while cleaning surfaces; and observe safety while they take personal care in the cleaning activity. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you clean surfaces made from different materials?

chunks.subject: Agriculture and Nutrition
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Hygiene Practices. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item (10 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe how to launder a cotton item b) Launder a cotton item for personal hygiene c) Appreciate importance of laundry work for hygiene purposes. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to: • Watch a clip or observe a demonstration on how to launder a cotton item (white and fast coloured cotton). • Launder a white and fast coloured cotton item. • Practice laundering of white and fast coloured items at home to appreciate the importance of laundry work for personal hygiene. • Develop learning to learn as they adopt learnt skills to launder personal items; responsibility while taking care of the personal items; and promote hygiene by maintaining cleanliness. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does laundering cotton items promote hygiene?

chunks.sub_strand: The learner reads simple texts with natural and smooth flow and at an appropriate pace all through. Pays attention to all punctuations and applies appropriate pauses and intonation to express intention and emotions
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to read with fluency (smoothness, pace, pauses and intonation). SUB-STRAND: The learner reads simple texts with natural and smooth flow and at an appropriate pace all through. Pays attention to all punctuations and applies appropriate pauses and intonation to express intention and emotions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: The learner reads simple texts with natural and smooth flow and at an appropriate pace all through. Pays attention to all punctuations and applies appropriate pauses and intonation to express intention and SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner reads simple texts with natural and smooth flow and at an appropriate pace through most parts of the texts. Pays attention to most of the punctuations and applies appropriate pauses and intonation to KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: The learner reads simple texts with stilted and choppy flow through most parts of the texts. Pays attention to very few punctuations as pauses and intonation are misplaced.

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Nuclear family; name (What’s _ name)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Nuclear family; name (What’s _ name). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) write Arabic words correctly, b) write short sentences from a given context, c) develop interest in writing Arabic. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  complete word with missing letters(nuun,raa,saad,faa,) with its vowels.  copy sentences about family members from a given display in pairs  play scrabble games forming simple Arabic words related to family members in groups KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you develop a good handwriting?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing In the classroom  Stationery/items  Learning areas Giving simple description of items found in the classroom( colour)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing In the classroom  Stationery/items  Learning areas Giving simple description of items found in the classroom( colour). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) construct simple sentences correctly, b) use basic descriptive words in writing simple sentence, c) appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  list the items found in the classroom in groups  draw, colour and label items found in the classroom of their choice in groups and share their work with their peers.  work in pairs to write simple sentences, describing items in the classroom. E.g my pencil is short the board is black the chair is broken KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you take care of classroom items?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Moments of the day (morning, afternoon, evening, night) ● Sequencing general activities in relation to moments of the day e.g. waking up, meals, sleeping
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Moments of the day (morning, afternoon, evening, night) ● Sequencing general activities in relation to moments of the day e.g. waking up, meals, sleeping. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) construct simple sentences correctly, b) use basic descriptive words in writing simple sentence, c) appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  creating sentences from a given substitution table about moments of the day  compete rearranging jumbled parts of sentences to make meaningful texts on moments of the day in small groups.  fill in sentences using the correct words in pairs KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it good to write legibly?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Hobbies and interests (singing, dancing, drawing and painting) In my free time I like….. In my free time I don’t like……
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Hobbies and interests (singing, dancing, drawing and painting) In my free time I like….. In my free time I don’t like……. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) create short personal and imaginative writings, b) construct sentences using acquire vocabulary correctly, c) appreciate different Arabic writing styles. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  write accurately simple sentences about hobbies and interest  use arrange of vocabulary to write correct sentences about hobbies groups  compete rearranging jumbled parts of sentences to make meaningful texts hobbies in groups KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can you develop a good handwriting?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Meals Mentioning what one eats in relation to different mealtimes
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Meals Mentioning what one eats in relation to different mealtimes. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) construct simple sentences correctly, b) use basic descriptive words in writing simple sentence, c) appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  practise writing simple sentences on mealtimes legibly and correctly in pairs  copy sentences, paying attention to spacing of words in the sentence and display their work  use jumble up the sentences to making up sensible paragraph in pairs KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we take meals??

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Functions of External human body parts
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Functions of External human body parts. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) construct simple sentences to express feeling using acquired vocabulary, b) write correctly sentences from given words, c) develop interest in artistic expression through writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  write words and simple sentences through dictation  draw and label body parts of their choice and post in the class wall for peer review in groups  compete rearranging jumbled parts of sentences to make meaningful texts on my body parts in small groups KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do you take care of your body?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Weather patterns Description of weather patterns ( it is sunny, it is rainy, it is……..)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Weather patterns Description of weather patterns ( it is sunny, it is rainy, it is……..). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) construct simple sentences correctly, b) use basic descriptive words in writing simple sentence, c) appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  writes very simple descriptions about weather patterns using short phrases/sentences.  compete writing simple sentences with speed and neatness on weather patterns.  observe the weather for one week and record the weather patterns in groups KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How does weather patterns affect our daily life?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Guided writing Locating others/common items in class; (where is) book, duster, pen, chair - In, on, under, behind
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Guided writing Locating others/common items in class; (where is) book, duster, pen, chair - In, on, under, behind. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) create sentences using acquired vocabularies and phrases, b) construct simple sentences to express feelings, ideas, or describe items, c) develop positive attitude towards writing Arabic. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  order words correctly to form simple sentences on locating classroom items in small groups  rearranging words to make meaningful sentences  through think-pair-share write simple sentences on classroom items from display of pictures  practice copying a short paragraph legibly and correctly on the board. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we need to keep classroom items safe?

Words are SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner writes readable texts paying attention to neatness in most parts of the text.
