chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: Exhibits a logical and coherent sequence throughout; provides a clear sense of a beginning, middle, and end. Makes smooth transitions between ideas
chunks.text: STRAND: Organization. SUB-STRAND: Exhibits a logical and coherent sequence throughout; provides a clear sense of a beginning, middle, and end. Makes smooth transitions between ideas. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Exhibits a logical sequence; provides a beginning, middle, and end. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Attempts to provide a logical sequence and/or the beginning or ending is abrupt or unclear. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Exhibits little order; provides a series of separate sentence and/or disconnected ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise sounds, words, and phrases correctly, b) use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to an oral narrative in pairs or groups,  identify words and phrases containing the sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː / from a print or audio text,  say words and phrases related to the theme accurately, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Use of Reference Materials
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Use of Reference Materials (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select relevant reference materials on a variety of subjects, b) spell words correctly for effective communication, c) read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure, d) use reference materials to find the required information, e) adopt the use of reference materials for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  select appropriate print and non-print reference materials (dictionaries, junior encyclopaedias, and, subject- specific encyclopaedias),  read selected reference materials independently,  look for information related to the theme from reference materials,  report and discuss what they have read with peers,  visit a library to find reference materials for information related to the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do you read books? 2. Which type of books do you enjoy reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstrative Determiners
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstrative Determiners (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify demonstrative determiners in a variety of texts, b) use demonstrative determiners correctly, c) promote the use of the correct demonstrative determiner to use during communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify demonstrative determiners from a text such as this, these, that, those,  read sentences containing demonstrative determiners in print or electronic materials,  construct sentences using demonstrative determiners with peers,  make sentences containing demonstrative determiners from a substitution table, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you identify objects that are near or far? 2. How do we show that objects being referred to are singular or more?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) record specific details in a variety of forms, b) design a form to obtain the required information, c) acknowledge the importance of filling forms correctly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  search for sample forms from the internet, individually,  select the information to be filled in a form collaboratively,  fill a form related to the theme using the following details: personal information, school information, parents/guardians details, religion/county information, favourite sport, hobby among others,  discuss the importance of filling forms correctly with peers,.  design a form to obtain information with peers and upload it online. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we fill forms? 2. Why is it important to fill forms accurately? 3. What details do we fill in forms?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Listening Comprehension: Dialogue
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Listening Comprehension: Dialogue (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words, phrases, and sentences containing the target sounds, b) construct sentences orally using words related to the theme, c) listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication, d) interpret a speaker’s feelings and emotions (non-verbal cues) correctly during an oral presentation, e) realise the importance of non-verbal cues and appropriate word choice in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify words with these sounds: /p/ /b/ from print materials such as newspapers, magazines,  listen to audio-visual recordings of dialogue containing the sounds /b/ /p/,  8isualiz saying tongue twisters with the sounds /b/ /p/,  discuss with peers the vocabulary used in the text and construct sentences using the vocabulary,  respond correctly to questions based on the dialogue.  role plays the events depicted in the dialogue,  interpret gestures, eye contacts, and facial expressions correctly. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we listen carefully? 2. Why do we take turns when talking?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narrative (about 400 words) Poem of about 5 Stanzas
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Oral Narrative (about 400 words) Poem of about 5 Stanzas (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify characters, places, and events in a story for comprehension, b) predict events in a text for comprehension, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  make predictions of what a story is about; what happens next in a story using the title/pictures in a story,  infer the meaning of words from the context,  use their imagination to 9isualize the events in a story, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is the title of a poem or a story important? 2. How do we predict events in a story or poem?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify collective nouns and reflexive pronouns in texts, b) use collective nouns and reflexive pronouns in sentences correctly, c) adopt the use of collective and reflexive pronouns to use during communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify reflexive pronouns and collective nouns from print and digital texts,  watch a video clip in which collective nouns and reflexive pronouns (myself, ourselves) have been used in sentences,  pick out collective nouns and reflexive pronouns, and list them as you work collaboratively with peers,  construct sentences using collective nouns and reflexive pronouns,  create and complete crossword puzzles using collective nouns and reflexive pronouns. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you emphasise that you did something on your own? 2. Which words do you use to refer to a group of things or animals?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select relevant points when planning a composition, b) write an open ended composition creatively, c) advocate for the use SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  brainstorm and discuss possible points to include in their composition,  write the first paragraph with peers while observing correct punctuation and spelling,  complete the composition individually of about (100-150 words),  proofread their compositions collaboratively, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we express ideas on different topics? 2. Why do we share ideas?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Polite Words Phrases and Expressions
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Polite Words Phrases and Expressions (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify polite words, phrases, and expressions in oral contexts, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to correct pronunciation of sounds, phrases, and expressions from the teacher, audio-visual recordings among others,  practise saying the sound /ɔɪ/ in words.  practise using polite words and phrases with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should you use polite expressions when talking to others? 2. Why should you listen to

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Intensive Reading Narrative of about 400 words)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Intensive Reading Narrative of about 400 words) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) relate events in the story with their life experiences, b) predict events in a text for comprehension, c) create mental images from the events in a story, d) respond to factual and inferential questions correctly, e) relate events in a reading text to real life experiences. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  make predictions on a story when reading,  use their imagination to visualise the events in a story,  scan and skim texts for new words and information with peers,  answer factual and inferential questions from the texts,  use digital devices to read online stories for comprehension. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you get information from a text? 2. Which things do you predict or visualize in a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Language Pattern: Use of too…to/for and Use of Must/Should with an Adverb/Adverbial
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Language Pattern: Use of too…to/for and Use of Must/Should with an Adverb/Adverbial (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify sentences featuring the target language patterns, b) use the language patterns in sentences correctly, c) Promote the use sentence patterns correctly for clarity of communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  make sentences with too…to/for from a substitution table. For example, ‘The stone is too heavy for Nanjala to lift.’  construct sentences using : ‘must/should with an adverb/adverbial’ for example, We must brush our teeth every day,  recite poems with the target language pattern.  discuss instances when the sentence patterns are used, in small groups,  fill in blank spaces in sentences using the patterns, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you identify correct sentences? 2. Why is it important to use sentences correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Word Stress (contrast between, nouns/verbs, verb /adjectives)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Word Stress (contrast between, nouns/verbs, verb /adjectives) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) list words whose meaning differs according to pronunciation, b) construct sentences orally using words related to the theme, c) pronounce words using the correct stress, d) use vocabulary related to the theme correctly, e) advocate for the importance of correct use of stress in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  recite a poem and apply the correct stress on words,  listen/watch to an audio-visual material on pronunciation,  list the words that are stressed,  classify the nouns, verbs, and adjectives from the list,  practise saying words using the correct stress, with peers for example; conflict (verb)/conflict (noun), subject (verb) /subject (noun)  say words containing the sounds /t/ and /d/,  construct sentences orally using the new vocabulary,  take part in a language game involving word stress, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce words correctly? 2. Why do words have different meanings at times?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension ( Visuals)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension ( Visuals) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) list the visuals in the classroom, b) make predictions based on visuals for comprehension, c) create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  view pictures, illustrations, posters, videos, pictures maps mnemonics, and symbols among others collaboratively with peers,  describe and interpret visuals correctly collaboratively with peers,  preview and make predictions based on pictures, illustrations, titles and experiences, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do you like pictures? 2. How can you use pictures to communicate?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify possessive forms in print or digital texts, b) use possessive forms correctly in sentences, c) advocate the correct use of possessive forms among peers. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  engage in online/offline games involving pronouns such as dice, goofy cards and word search collaboratively with peers,  simulate, dramatise or role play a conversation featuring possessive forms,  watch videos/songs involving the use of possessive pronouns/ belong to,  compose songs based on the use of personal and possessive pronouns,  fill gaps in sentences correctly using possessive pronouns and belong to,  create a list of sentences with possessive and personal pronouns for display with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we use possessive forms correctly? 2. Which words show something belongs to a person?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the components of a friendly letter, b) write a friendly letter using the correct format, c) judge the appropriateness of words, phrases and sentences used in friendly letters. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  read a sample friendly letter with peers and pick out the parts such as address, salutation, date, complimentary close among others,  write a reply to a sample friendly letter using the correct format,  proofread/edit the letter collaboratively,  present the edited version to other groups,  search for more examples of friendly letters on the internet while collaborating with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you communicate with people who are far away? 2. Why do we write letters?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Sounds/ Adjectives
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Sounds/ Adjectives (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognise sounds, words and phrases correctly, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a speech and pick out words containing sound /e/,  interpret non-verbal cues such as gestures, facial expressions and eye contact collaboratively with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce sounds correctly? 2. Which words do we use to describe

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select relevant reading materials from a collection of books, b) scan a text to obtain specific information, c) skim through digital or print texts to establish appropriateness and relevance, d) read a variety of materials for fluency, e) judge the appropriateness of a reading text on the basis of language and interest. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  preview a text to determine suitability.  skim through reading materials,  select fiction and non-fiction reading materials of between 1000-1250 words (both print and non-print),  read selected materials independently,  set up an after school reading club where they meet regularly, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What materials do you enjoy reading? 2. Why is it necessary to read many books?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1 Word Class:  Comparatives and Superlatives forms of Regular and Irregular adjectives.  Order of Adjectives
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1 Word Class:  Comparatives and Superlatives forms of Regular and Irregular adjectives.  Order of Adjectives (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text, b) order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately, c) use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately, d) advocate the importance of using adjectives correctly in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  describe items using the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives e.g. that window is bigger than this one,  change positive forms of regular and irregular adjectives to their comparative and superlative forms, with peers,  pick out adjectives of size, shape and age from a narrative or poem in collaboratively with peers,  construct sentences featuring adjectives of size, shape and age,  fill gaps using adjectives in the correct order,  create a crossword puzzle using adjectives. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we compare things, people or events? 2. Which words are used to describe things or people?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the parts of a narrative composition, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  brainstorm ideas for a narrative composition collaboratively with peers,  read samples of narrative compositions with peers,  identify the parts of a narrative composition, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do you enjoy reading stories? 2. How do you make your

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Stress and Intonation
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Stress and Intonation (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) sort statements and questions based on rising and falling intonation, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  reproduce appropriate patterns of stress and intonation in speech,  sort the statements and questions on the basis of rising or falling intonation collaboratively with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. Why do we raise our

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select unfamiliar words and phrases from a reading text, b) use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words, c) respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension, d) relate events in the story to their own experiences. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  make connections between the characters in the text and the people they know,  relate events in the dialogue to their experiences,  read and role play a dialogue of about about 400 words collaboratively with peers,  pick out main ideas from the dialogue,  answer direct and inferential questions based on the dialogue,  infer the meaning of words from the context (for example, from words occurring before or after). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we tell the meaning of words? 2. What makes you a good reader?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3.1 Word Class: Determiners: Quantifiers: Few/ a few, little/ a little, a lot of/ lots of, each, all, enough, most, least
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 6.3.1 Word Class: Determiners: Quantifiers: Few/ a few, little/ a little, a lot of/ lots of, each, all, enough, most, least (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify quantifying determiners in a variety of texts, b) use quantifying determiners appropriately in a variety of contexts, c) judge the appropriateness of quantifying determiners in oral and written texts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  read a passage related to the theme and identify quantifying determiners from the passage collaboratively,  match quantifying determiners with corresponding countable and uncountable nouns,  list quantifying determiners that can be used with both countable and uncountable nouns,  read sentences containing quantifying determiners from the internet with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which words do we use to show amount or quantity? 2. Why is it important to tell the quantity of something?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) choose possible topics for pictorial compositions, b) create a composition based on the visuals or pictures, c) judge visuals appropriately for creativity in writing. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  interpret pictures collaboratively with peers,  match the pictures with the different parts of a composition: beginning, middle and end,  watch a variety of animations, videos and sample write pictorial compositions collaboratively with peers,  arrange different pictures logically to write a story coherently,  write a pictorial composition of about 120 - 160 words,  proof read the pictorial composition,  display their compositions in the classroom. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we enjoy looking at pictures? 2. What messages do pictures communicate?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  select words with the sound: /ə/ and the diphthongs: /ɪə/ and /eɪ/ from a dialogue, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non- Fiction Texts (1000-1250 words) Poems (not more than 5 stanzas)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non- Fiction Texts (1000-1250 words) Poems (not more than 5 stanzas) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select relevant reading materials from a collection of books, b) read a variety of materials for information and pleasure, c) judge the appropriateness of reading materials on the basis of interest, complexity and subject. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  skim through reading materials to obtain the main idea,  preview texts to determine suitability and relevance,  scan materials for specific details collaboratively,  select appropriate reading materials from a library,  read the selected materials individually,  share reflections on the books read collaboratively,  keep a record of materials read. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What kind of information do you find in books? 2. Why is it necessary to read many books? 3. What do you consider when choosing a material to read?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Tense: Future Time using will/shall (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify words that indicate future time in sentences, b) use will and shall to express SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  pick sentences which express future time from a text,  make sentences from a substitution table,  answer questions on future time using will/shall collaboratively,  construct sentences using will/shall collaboratively,  role play activities they plan or wish to do in future with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which words do we use to show future time? 2. How do you tell the time something happened? 3. What will you do tomorrow?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation-  Use of the Commas  Use of Double Quotation Marks
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation-  Use of the Commas  Use of Double Quotation Marks (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts, b) use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences, c) advocate the use of correct punctuation in written communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  read a short text and identify punctuation marks used collaboratively with peers,  use commas to show pauses between words, phrases or clauses,  complete sentences using double quotation marks and commas,  pick out sentences with double quotation marks in newspapers, magazines, articles or internet resources,  play punctuation games with peers,  create posters or charts with sentences with double quotation marks and commas and display them in class, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which punctuation marks do you know? 2. Why do we punctuate sentences?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Oral Narrative Featuring Proverbs and Sayings
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Oral Narrative Featuring Proverbs and Sayings (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) list proverbs and sayings in a narrative, b) construct sentences orally using words related to the theme, c) pronounce words with the target sounds correctly, d) use words, proverbs and sayings appropriately in oral communication, e) anticipate what is likely to happen as a story unfolds, f) display varied emotions and feelings when listening to an oral presentation. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a narrative and select proverbs and sayings,  match the vocabulary with their meanings,  make oral sentences using vocabulary,  practise saying words with the sounds /k/ /g/ with peers,  create tongue twisters with the sounds /k/ /g/ with peers,  search for vocabulary, proverbs and sayings in the internet collaboratively,  listen and view stories of about 130 words and songs featuring proverbs and sayings,  create posters and charts with common proverbs and sayings that the learners can relate to with peers and display them in the classroom. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we pronounce words correctly? 2. Which proverbs and sayings do you know? 3. Why are proverbs and sayings important in speech?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading (Texts of about 400 words)
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading (Texts of about 400 words). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify unfamiliar words in texts for fluency, b) read a text accurately and with expression and at the SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  skim and scan through paragraphs for information collaboratively,  search for an article on a topic they enjoy, select a portion to read,  set a goal on the number of words to be read per minute,  find a word or phrase from a word - chart within a stipulated time, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What makes someone a good reader? 2. How long do you take to read a text? 3. What can you do to improve your reading speed?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.3.1 Sentences:  Use of Double Imperatives:  Question Tags on the Verb to be
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Sentences:  Use of Double Imperatives:  Question Tags on the Verb to be (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify sentences with tag questions and double imperatives from a text, b) use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences, c) advocate the correct use of double imperatives and question tags in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  fill in gaps in sentences using double imperatives,  select question tags from a story, dialogue or poem,  match statements with the correct question tag to make a tag question,  practise giving instructions related to the theme using double imperatives such as: shut down your tablets and listen to the teacher. Type this word in your tablet and look up its meaning,  role play giving and receiving of instructions at home using double imperatives,  use double imperatives to make rules for their classroom and display them in charts or posters,  write correct sentences using double imperatives. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are some of your school rules? 2. How do you give instructions? 3. Why do we ask questions?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 8.4.1 Creative Writing:  Narrative Composition (120 -160 words)  Similes and Proverbs
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 8.4.1 Creative Writing:  Narrative Composition (120 -160 words)  Similes and Proverbs (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify similes and proverbs in a variety of texts, b) use similes and proverbs correctly, c) create a narrative composition featuring similes and proverbs, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  read narratives with formulaic expressions in print and digital format,  list similes and proverbs in texts collaboratively,  create a clear and coherent storyline using proverbs and similes,  engage in a dialogue to advance plot and storyline,  compose a story featuring similes and proverbs with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we make our compositions interesting? 2. Which similes and proverbs do you know?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.1.1 Speaking Fluency: Narrative of about 150 words
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Speaking Fluency: Narrative of about 150 words (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) list words with sound /h/ from an oral text, b) construct sentences orally using words related to the theme, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a poem or narrative and identify words with the /h/ sound,  retell a narrative in own words collaboratively,  listen to graded texts with audio recordings of whole narratives,  listen to music and pick out sounds and vocabulary, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to speak accurately and express the right feelings? 2. How can you listen more attentively? 3. Which words do you use to talk about diseases?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words)
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: Descriptive Fictional or Non-Fictional Texts (about 400 words) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the main idea in each paragraph, b) visualise events, characters and descriptions in texts for comprehension. c) summarise the main points in a text. d) answers factual and inferential questions for comprehension. e) challenge others to focus on detail when reading a text. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners are guided to:  make connections between events in the text and their experiences,  retelling the story collaboratively with peers,  use illustrations, the introduction and the title of a text to make predictions,  describe collaboratively the characters, episodes and places in a text,  scan a text for specific details,  answer questions from a text,  state the main ideas from a text,  watch a video related to the theme and pick specific information. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you describe things? 2. How can you tell what will happen in a story?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.3.1 Word Class:  Adverbs (manner, time, place, frequency)  Use of could, would and how many  How many…could/would
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Word Class:  Adverbs (manner, time, place, frequency)  Use of could, would and how many  How many…could/would (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify adverbs of manner, time, place and frequency in a text, b) use adverbs correctly in oral and written contexts, c) use the modals could and would and the phrase how many in sentences correctly, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learners is guided to:  identify and list adverbs from a digital or print text collaboratively,  make sentences from a substitution table using the pattern how many…could/would,  fill in blank spaces with appropriate adverbs,  construct sentences using adverbs of manner, time place and frequency, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we describe when, how, where and how many times an action takes place? 2. Which word or words do we use to ask questions?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the apostrophe and SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a short oral text and write the text with the correct punctuation marks  underline the apostrophe and exclamation marks in a text with peers, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which punctuation marks do you know?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening  Choral verse  Narrative in Dialogue Format (Conversation Narrative)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Interactive Listening  Choral verse  Narrative in Dialogue Format (Conversation Narrative) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify different moods in a narrative or a choral verse, b) use words and phrases with the selected sound in sentences, c) interrupt politely during a conversation, d) challenge others to listen interactively during conversations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a narrative and retell it while expressing different moods or feelings,  construct sentences orally collaboratively with peers,  say words containing the sounds /s/ and /z/ with peers,  watch a video of a conversational narrative or a choral verse online or offline,  take turns during a conversation,  engage in a dialogue and practise interrupting one another politely. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should you interrupt others politely? 2. How do you show different moods and feelings when listening to someone? 3. Which words do you use to join an on- going conversation?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) relate the ideas in a text to their experiences, b) respond to factual and inferential questions correctly, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  skim through a text and obtain the main idea,  scan through a text to obtain specific information,  discuss and relate ideas to their experiences collaboratively with peers,  read a text independently and retell it in own words, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we read books? 2. Why should we make notes when reading? 3. What makes you a good reader?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions
chunks.text: STRAND: 10. 3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify conjunctions in texts for effective communication, b) use conjunctions correctly in communication, c) judge the correctness and appropriateness of conjunctions in oral and written texts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a short dialogue and identify conjunctions,  make sentences from a substitution table using but, or, yet, because, since and also,  construct sentences using conjunctions with peers,  fill in blank spaces using conjunctions in sentences or paragraphs,  create a display chart of sentences containing conjunctions with peers,  conduct a gallery walk and give feedback to each group. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do you join words and sentences? 2. How do you join words or sentences?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words)
chunks.text: STRAND: 10.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe people or things mentioned in a text, b) create a descriptive composition related to the theme, c) collaborate with peers to critique a SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  read a sample composition from print or electronic sources,  talk about people or things in the text,  make sentences to describe how they spent their leisure time collaboratively,  organise the sentences to make a paragraph collaboratively, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we describe things or events? 2. Why is it important to describe things or events clearly?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:  Listening Fluency  Non-verbal cues
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:  Listening Fluency  Non-verbal cues (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select words containing the target sound in sentences, b) construct sentences orally using words related to the theme, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to oral presentations (dialogues or poems on topical issues) containing words with the sound /aɪ/,  identify words with the sound /aɪ/ from texts,  practise saying selected tongue twisters collaboratively, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to listen carefully? 2. How can we become better listeners?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Reading with Technology
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Reading with Technology (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) relate ideas in the text to personal experiences, b) create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text, c) answer factual and inferential questions correctly, d) judge the appropriateness of digital texts on the basis of word choice, theme and interest. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  infer the meaning of words from context,  make connections between town experiences and events in the reading text.  create pictures, mimes, videos or crossword puzzles in with peers,  search and read texts from the internet with peers,  dramatise or role play events or characters in stories they have read online,  print the visuals obtained from online sources and share or display in a gallery. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to relate what you read to real life experiences? 2. What digital resources can you use in your reading? 3. Why are digital materials more interesting to read than print ones?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify interrogatives in sentences correctly, b) use interrogatives accurately in sentences, c) adopt the use of interrogatives used in oral and written texts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  mention the words used to ask questions - how, what, when, why, who,  use the wh- words and how to ask questions,  construct questions using the pattern: how much more…, when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony? how much more sugar was bought?  use the interrogatives with: else, much … to complete sentences, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we ask questions? 2. How do we ask questions?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 11.4.1 Spelling:  Commonly Misspelt Words  Homophones  Homonyms
chunks.text: STRAND: 11.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 11.4.1 Spelling:  Commonly Misspelt Words  Homophones  Homonyms (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) spell selected words correctly for effective communication, b) use homophones and homonyms in sentences correctly, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner should be guided to:  discuss with peers words they find difficult to spell,  make a presentation on correct spelling homophones and homonyms, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we write words correctly? 2. Which words do you find difficult to write?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.2 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:  Speaking Fluency (Content from other Learning areas)  Making a Speech
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 12.2 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:  Speaking Fluency (Content from other Learning areas)  Making a Speech (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) pronounce words with selected sounds accurately for effective communication, b) construct sentences orally using words related to the theme, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  say words containing the sounds /f/ and /v/ with peers,  pronounce the words related to the theme correctly,  construct oral sentences using vocabulary learnt,  listen to a recorded speech from a digital KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we speak clearly and confidently? 2. Why do we make speeches?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poems, Songs and Tongue Twisters
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poems, Songs and Tongue Twisters (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) creates mental images from events, characters and places in a text, b) infer information and meaning of words from context, c) answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension, d) relate events and characters in the reading text to personal experiences. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  watch a video on environmental pollution and answer questions,  read a poem or song and role play the events, experiences or characters in the text,  answer factual and inferential questions on the poem and song they read,  visualise events, characters or places mentioned in a text,  role play events or characters in the poem collaboratively with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What can you learn from poems and songs? 2. Which poems and songs do you know? 3. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words while reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.3.1 Word Class: Nouns (which only occur in singular or plural)
chunks.text: STRAND: 12. 3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 12.3.1 Word Class: Nouns (which only occur in singular or plural) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify nouns which only occur in singular or plural from given sentences, b) use nouns which only occur in singular or plural to make sentences, c) collaborate with others to determine the correctness and appropriateness of nouns used in various texts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify and underline nouns which only occur in singular or plural sentences,  construct sentences with peers using nouns which only occur in singular or plural such as news, dirt, waste and rubbish,  practise a conversation using plurals of nouns which only occur in singular or plural collaboratively,  watch videos on nouns which only occur in singular or plural and answer questions,  create display charts on nouns which only occur in singular or plural in sentences. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to use words correctly? 2. Which singular nouns end with letter -s?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 12.4.1 Functional Writing:  Appointment Diary  Journal (3 days)
chunks.text: STRAND: 12.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 12.4.1 Functional Writing:  Appointment Diary  Journal (3 days) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the key components of a diary/journal, b) create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format, c) collaborate with peers to create personal journals SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  view a sample diary sample journal/and identify the components,  write journal/diary entries with peers,  create an appointment diary collaboratively,  create a three day journal with peers,  display their work in class and take a gallery walk,  give feedback to each group about their work after the gallery walk, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we plan our activities in advance? 2. What is the most memorable experience in your life?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Intensive Listening (Dialogue containing similes)
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: Intensive Listening (Dialogue containing similes). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select words and phrases with the target sounds, digraphs and consonant clusters from a text, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  listen to a dialogue from an audio-visual recording or read by the teacher and select words with the target sounds, digraphs and clusters,  say words containing the sounds /m/ /n/ /ŋ/ with peers,  identify words featuring the target sounds,  identify similes from an audio visual text, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we listen attentively? 2. How can you tell someone is attentive?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.2.1 Extensive Reading Variety of texts such as Newspapers, magazines, class readers and poems
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.2 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 13.2.1 Extensive Reading Variety of texts such as Newspapers, magazines, class readers and poems (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) select suitable reading materials from a variety of texts, b) read a variety of materials independently for information and pleasure, c) use fluency strategies such as previewing, skimming and scanning strategies to find necessary information, d) judge the appropriateness of a reading text on the basis SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  select appropriate print and non-print reading materials; newspapers, magazines, class readers or poems,  scan through a text for specific details and skim through a material to obtain the main idea,  read selected materials independently,  promote extensive reading among peers and the greater community,  collaborate with peers to determine the appropriateness of reading texts on the basis of interest, themes and complexity of language,  make notes on a topic they read with peers,  make an entry of what they have read in their creative writing diary, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do you read? 2. How do you obtain specific information from a text? 3. What materials do you enjoy reading?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.3 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify prepositions of time, place and direction in sentences, b) use prepositions of time, place and direction appropriately for effective communication, c) collaborate with others to judge the accuracy, appropriateness and correctness of prepositions used in varied texts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  underline prepositions of time, place and direction in sample sentences: o time such as in, on, at) o place such as :in, on, at o direction such as : into, towards, to, through  play preposition games and songs online/offline,  construct sentences using prepositions,  watch videos and online material on prepositions collaboratively,  create display charts containing prepositions of time and direction,  create crossword puzzles using prepositions,  solve code words and crossword puzzles involving prepositions,  search for prepositions online, from newspapers magazines among others. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Which words show direction and time? 2. Why is it important to show time and direction?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 13.4.1 Spelling:  Homophones  Words with double consonants  Words with double vowels
chunks.text: STRAND: 13.4 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 13.4.1 Spelling:  Homophones  Words with double consonants  Words with double vowels (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly, b) spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner is guided to:  identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels from a text,  listen to words read by the teacher or from audio recording for example: - waist/waste - collect or dropped  write down from a dictation correctly, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should we write words correctly? 2. Which words have the same pronunciation but different spelling?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) Oral reading or dictation recitations b) Role play c) Debates d) Oral interviews e) Dialogues f) Oral discussions g) Oral presentations h) Public speaking SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES:  Participation in poetry recitations during music and drama festivals.  Readers’ theatres organised after classes where poems are read for fun.  Engaging in public speaking contests where knowledge on pronunciation is applied.  Preparing speeches and delivering them during prize giving days, school assembly, extravaganzas among others to enhance fluency.  Debating club contests  Taking part in the 4K club and young farmers association to reinforce learnt vocabulary. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Non Digital Resources  course books  story books  poetry books  pictures and photographs  newspapers  magazines  junior encyclopaedia  journals  dictionaries  diorama

chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Intensive Reading 2.2 Extensive 2.3 Reading Fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Intensive Reading 2.2 Extensive 2.3 Reading Fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) Reading aloud b) Dictation c) Oral interviews d) Question and answer e) Teacher-made tests f) Learner summaries of what they read g) Learner journals h) Learner portfolios SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES:  Reading news during the morning assembly.  Conducting virtual tours using Google maps and establishing the direction of various national parks using Google Maps.  Collecting narratives from their community for a school magazine.  Performing short plays, conversational poems or choral verses within the school or during drama festivals.  Acting as reporters, sports commentators or journalists during sports and games activities in school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Word Classes 3.2 Sentences 3.3 Patterns 3.4 Tense
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Grammar in Use. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Word Classes 3.2 Sentences 3.3 Patterns 3.4 Tense. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) Tasks such as multiple choice b) Discrimination c) Gap-filling d) Short-answer e) Dialogue- completion, information gap f) Role play g) Simulation h) Matching tasks i) Substitution tables SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES:  Essay writing competitions on different topics.  Debating club sessions to enhance their language competency.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1 Creative Writing 4.2 Functional Writing 4.3 Mechanics of Writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Writing. SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Creative Writing 4.2 Functional Writing 4.3 Mechanics of Writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: a) Teacher-made tests b) Learner journals c) Peer assessment d) Self- assessment learner e) Portfolio dictation f) Standardised writing tests SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES:  Establishment of writers’ clubs, journalism clubs, and compiling articles for the school magazine to nurture writing talent.  Spelling contests among schools.  Set up an after school club where they meet on a regular basis to read books and do extensive reading activities

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Phonological awareness Greetings and introductions  Le son[z]
chunks.text: STRAND: 1. Listening and speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Phonological awareness Greetings and introductions Le son[z] (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognize letter sounds in words from audio stimuli, b) articulate words correctly in oral interactions, c) appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to and sing songs on simple greetings in French.  play rhyming games to enhance vocabulary mastery.  do simulations on greetings and self- introductions, in pairs.  (Comment tu t’appelles ? Je m’appelle …, Je suis une fille, Comment ça va ? Voici mon ami,)  engage role plays to introduce self and another KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you find out the well-being of one another?

chunks.text: STRAND: 1 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.2 Imitative speaking Family Mon père, ma mère, ma sœur, mon frère, Mon petit frère /ma petite sœur /mon grand frère/ma grande sœur Avoir + ans/les chiffres Les professions : Professeur, mécanicien, cuisinier (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) repeat sounds, words and expressions on family as articulated from an audio text, b) use spoken language patterns appropriately for effective real-life interactions, c) display a positive attitude towards speaking activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  practice active listening skills to reproduce spoken words, phrases and expressions on family.  listen to authentic audio- visual dialogues introducing family members and take turns to repeat or act out the dialogues.  use the expressions learned to ask each other questions relating to members of their nuclear family. (Name, age, profession…etc) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do the members of your family do?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: a) recall names of objects and items (les affaires scolaires) in the classroom; b) use digital resources to listen to audio-visual materials to identify objects and items in the classroom; c) describe objects and items which they use in the classroom (name the stationery, say colour and size). d) Mimic and participate in question- answer exercises on classroom items or objects. e) Participate in language games Qu’est-ce que c’est ? C’est un…… ? Oui / Non c’est…. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What items do you need in class?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4 Imitative speaking Time – Days of the week  Lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche, Le matin, le midi, le soir, la nuit
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Listening and speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.4 Imitative speaking Time – Days of the week Lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche, Le matin, le midi, le soir, la nuit (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) repeat correct pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source, b) demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions, c) build confidence in replicating spoken language patterns. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to songs about moments of the day  listen and repeat short simple phrases on moments of the day (Le matin je me lève, à midi je prends le déjeuner, le soir je joue, la nuit je dors)  recite poems for vocabulary acquisition and r.  talk about his activities in relation to moments of the day KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What activities do you do every day?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 1.5 Imitative speaking Fun and Enjoyment  Activités de loisirs – danser, écouter de la musique, regarder la télévision, un film, jouer au + sport, jouer + instrument de musique
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Listening and Speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.5 Imitative speaking Fun and Enjoyment Activités de loisirs – danser, écouter de la musique, regarder la télévision, un film, jouer au + sport, jouer + instrument de musique (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make correct pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source, b) use fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions, c) display a positive attitude towards speaking activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: a) actively listen and repeat phrases or sentences related to hobbies as modelled by the teacher or audio-visual materials; (Pour/Dans mon temps libre, j’aime… je n’aime pas… chanter, la télé, danser, dessiner…) b) orally describe actions related to hobbies with the aid of visual aids and infographics and by respond to questions: (Qu’est-ce qu’il /elle fait ? Elle danse…). c) to exchange information on what they do during their free time at home using selected KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do you do when you are free?

chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Listening and speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.6 Imitative speaking Foods and Drinks (Le café, le thé, le riz, le lait, la viande, le poulet, les frites, les haricots, les patates douce, l’igname, les légumes, les fruits, les céréales, l’ougali (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) repeat correct pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from source, b) apply fluent speech patterns for effective real- life interactions, c) display a positive attitude towards speaking activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to audio-visual material relating to meals to pick out vocabulary.  listen to and repeat sentences relating to mealtimes. (Je prends le petit déjeuner le matin, je prends le diner à midi, je prends le diner le soir)  talk about meals in relation to meal times.  play games to practice vocabulary related to mealtimes and food. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do you eat at different mealtimes?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make correct pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from an audio text, b) use fluent speech patterns for effective real-life interactions, c) display a positive attitude toward speaking activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to audio materials to pick out vocabulary on the different parts of the body.  recite poems on parts of the body.  observe images of different parts of the body as they match to the correct flash cards. (Ma bouche est pour manger, mes oreilles sont pour écouter, i.e. Parties du corps + est/sont + verbe infinitif)  watch a video clip on functions of the parts of the body.  sing songs about functions of the parts of the body.

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 1.8 Phonological awareness Weather and Environment  La pluie, le climat, le soleil, les nuages, l’air, le vent, les arbres, le ciel, la lune, le soleil, les averses, orageux, nuageux
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Listening and speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.8 Phonological awareness Weather and Environment La pluie, le climat, le soleil, les nuages, l’air, le vent, les arbres, le ciel, la lune, le soleil, les averses, orageux, nuageux (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) recognize letter sounds in words from audio stimuli, b) articulate words correctly in oral interactions, c) appreciate the importance of correct pronunciation in interactive communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● watch and listen to audio- visual materials on weather and identify weather patterns; (il fait beau/chaud/froid, il pleut, il fait mauvais, il y a du vent, il fait nuageux...) ● listen to songs on weather patterns and weather conditions, in groups. ● play rhyming games in small groups to enhance vocabulary mastery ● group weather conditions in their immediate surroundings. ● recite poems on weather conditions with specific sounds. (Nuageux, orageux) ● source vocabulary on weather patterns from digital devices. ● play games on vocabulary search in groups using digital devices. ● recite tongue-twisters. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What weather conditions do you experience?

chunks.sub_strand: 1.9 Imitative speaking Getting Around  Tableau, étagère, échelle, armoire, pupitre, chaise, bureau, craies, poubelle, tapis, fenêtre, porte Devant, derrière, en face de, devant, entre, sous, dans
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 Listening and speaking. SUB-STRAND: 1.9 Imitative speaking Getting Around Tableau, étagère, échelle, armoire, pupitre, chaise, bureau, craies, poubelle, tapis, fenêtre, porte Devant, derrière, en face de, devant, entre, sous, dans (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) make correct pronunciation of sounds and words as articulated from an audio text, b) use spoken language patterns appropriately for effective real-life interactions, c) display a positive attitude toward speaking activities. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: ● participate in “Repeat-after- me” exercise to acquire vocabulary on class items. (tableau, chaises, poubelle, pupitre, porte, chiffon, règle, cahier, stylo…) ● listen to and sing songs on objects found in class. ● source and watch video clips with authentic dialogues on locating items. ● play games in groups to state the location or position of items in class. (Dans, derrière, à côte de, sur, sous) ● listen and follow instructions on putting items in their right places. (Mets les cahiers dans le pupitre. Range les livres dans les étagères) ● participate in simple simulations on asking for and giving location. ● ask for the location of some household items in paired activities. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Where do you keep items at home?

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.strand: Ability to use spoken language patterns for effective communication [pronunciation, intonation, rhythm, pacing]
chunks.sub_strand: The learner speaks fluently exhibiting a good articulation of words and expressions bringing out a spectacular pronunciation. The pace is excellent giving an excellent rhythm in a conversation allowing passage of the intended information. Speaks with enthusiasm and makes a perfect intonation like native in a conversation
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to use spoken language patterns for effective communication [pronunciation, intonation, rhythm, pacing]. SUB-STRAND: The learner speaks fluently exhibiting a good articulation of words and expressions bringing out a spectacular pronunciation. The pace is excellent giving an excellent rhythm in a conversation allowing passage of the intended information. Speaks with enthusiasm and makes a perfect intonation like native in a conversation. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: The learner speaks fluently exhibiting a good intonation with proper pauses. The pace is excellent giving an impressive smoothness due to a proper articulation of words and expressions. Speaks mostly in familiar contexts. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner speaks exhibiting some fair intonation due to an effort made to articulate words and expressions correctly. The pace is moderate giving a fair smoothness. Tries to hold a conversation for shorter period of time. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: The learner pronounces words and phrases with difficulties. Speaks with some pauses that affects the smoothness of the conversation. The pace is slow as the learner tries to articulate words correctly.

chunks.strand: Ability to demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions
chunks.sub_strand: The learner uses wide range of vocabulary. Exhibits an excellent sentence structure during oral interactions

Exhibits correct sentence structures during oral interactions. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner uses a limited range of vocabulary. Exhibits inaccuracies in sentence structures during oral interactions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: The learner uses few words correctly. Experiences difficulties in word order in a sentence during oral interactions.

chunks.subject: Foreign Languages
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Reading aloud Greetings and introductions  Le son[z]
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Reading. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Reading aloud Greetings and introductions Le son[z] (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) distinguish greetings in a text while reading, b) read aloud simple words with targeted sound accurately, c) develop confidence in their reading abilities through guided support. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  practice choral reading of simple texts on greetings and introductions to follow rhythm and pace.  practice echo reading  practice targeted sounds in vocabulary and expressions on greetings. Comment tu t’appelles ? Je m’appelle … Je suis une fille Comment ça va ? Voici mon ami...)  source for poems on greetings and introductions from digital devices and recite in groups. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do you read that promotes interaction?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  practice reading games for proper pronunciation of nuclear family lexical.  engage in letter art reading in order to help learners that learn through visual aids.  create paper stripes for reading containing simple phrases about nuclear family.  play bingo games bearing a nuclear family lexical.  use flash cards for learning in order to retain vocabulary.  arrange jumbled up sentences to come up with the corrects sentence structure about the nuclear family.  create word games, using digital devices to help on vocabulary building. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is it important to read accurately?

KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What important objects or items should be found in your classroom?

SUB-STRAND: 4.1 Importance Of Features In Jain Derasar And Sikh Gurdwara Carved domes, Shoerack Moorti of the deity, Mirror, Panch aarti Deepak, Pooja thaal, Bell Sikh Gurdwara Nishaan Sahib, Shoe rack Place to clean feet and hands.SGGSJ, Palki sahib, Symbol, Degh (Karrah Prasaad), Chaur Sahib, Langar (7 lessons). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to visit a place of worship? 2. What are the important features you see while visiting a Jain Derasar?

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  using digital devices, like YouTube and demonstrative manuals and correctly perform  visit and participate in the celebration of International Yoga day.  practice asanas in pairs and groups to encourage and help each other  create a Yoga guidance video using digital devices.  sing song on Pranaayam that they familiar with  discuss types of Pranaayam with the guidance of teacher KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How does communal aspects of Yoga beneficial to the society? 2. How is meditation helpful in spiritual growth?

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify features of a poem for comprehension, b) translate an oral poem into prose with accuracy for communication, c) appreciate the benefits of attentive listening for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  identify names of clothes and attire (nouns) from the community,  work collaboratively to construct sentences using the nouns identified,  brainstorm on various features of a poem with peers,  recite poems based on the theme with expressions ( non-verbal cues),  work with peers to paraphrase the poem in their own words without altering the ideas,  listen attentively to recorded clips of simple poems on cultural attire and answer comprehension questions,  compose spoken word items on the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What should you do in order to listen attentively?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Reading for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Reading for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a text with accuracy and fluency for information, b) interpret written instructions from a text for comprehension, c) develop an interest in reading texts on topical issues for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  match names and pictures of cultural attire and clothing,  practice reading texts based on the theme fluently and with accuracy,  read instructions and interpret their meaning with peers,  organize a reading theatre to read texts based on the theme,  identify various cultural attire from stories and make short notes,  listen to a resource person explaining various cultural attires. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is the importance of fluency in reading? 2. Why should we use cultural attire in our community?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Handwriting
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Handwriting. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) outline letters of the alphabet neatly for effective communication, b) compose a paragraph neatly and legibly for effective communication, c) appreciate the importance of writing legibly and neatly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  trace letters of the alphabet in upper case and lower case neatly,  identify various cultural attire from pictures,  create target words on flashcards using the letters of the alphabet,  work jointly with peers to write a short paragraph neatly and legibly on the theme,  share the short paragraphs developed in class for peer review,  organise their neatly written paragraphs in the class portfolio. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we write instructions? 2. Why should we write neatly and legibly?

chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Listening for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Listening for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify components of a conversation for comprehension, b) respond to an oral conversation related to the theme effectively, c) appreciate expressing self logically and coherently for communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a conversation from an audio clip to identify conjunctions,  collaborate with peers to talk about their experiences on environmental awareness in their community,  answer oral questions based on a listening comprehension,  role play giving or taking instructions during a conversation with peers,  construct sentences using conjunctions,  narrate and retell stories based on the theme collaboratively,  listen to songs sung by peers on environmental issues and discuss main ideas,  compose simple stories and songs using conjunctions. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is the importance of listening in a conversation? 2. How do we express self logically and coherently?
