SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read a passage on the theme aloud for fluency and expression, b) answer questions from texts based on the theme for comprehension, c) appreciate reading texts on importance of conserving the environment for information. . SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  conduct a reader’s theatre to read a simple passage based on the theme,  identify instances of change in intonation from the texts read,  read a passage independently and answer comprehension questions,  work jointly with peers to discuss and infer meaning of vocabulary in context,  use vocabulary to make sentences based on the theme collaboratively,  collaboratively compose an oral narrative on weather,  perform an oral narrative with fluency and expression in class. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we read fluently? 2. Why should we be alert on weather changes?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Punctuation
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Punctuation. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) identify punctuation marks (exclamation, double quotation and question marks) in a variety of texts, b) combine sentences to form a coherent and logical paragraph, c) appreciate sequencing of ideas for in writing for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work with peers to identify punctuation marks (exclamation, double quotation and question marks) in texts,  use exclamation, double quotation and question mark in sentence construction,  share the punctuated sentences in class for peer review,  fill blanks in sentences using punctuation marks,  brainstorm with peers the uses of exclamation, double quotation and question marks in sentences.  Collaborate to play online games involving the use of punctuations marks. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we punctuate sentences?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Listening for comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Listening for comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify vocabulary items in oral texts for effective communication, b) use vocabulary in sentences to express self accurately and effectively, c) advocate for the use of acquired language in communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen and identify pronouns in oral sentences,  listen to a story from a digital device and identify sentences with pronouns,  create oral sentences using pronouns in collaboratively,  fill gaps in sentences using pronouns,  play pronouns games using cards or through online platforms  talk about a topic in class using pronouns,  compose and sing songs containing pronouns,  create a collection list of commonly used pronouns,  match pronouns in singular and plural forms KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you use pronouns in communication?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Reading for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Reading for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read a passage based on the theme fluently for comprehension, b) respond to instructions to perform a relevant task for communication, c) appreciate the importance of following instructions. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work jointly with peers to read a passage on the theme,  identify vocabulary used from the passage,  identify pronouns from the passage,  use pronouns to construct sentences with peers,  work collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank with words identified,  use a digital device to read content and follow steps of performing simple tasks,  respond to questions based on the content read,  collect reading materials for reference during a library lesson. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to read instructions with comprehension? 2. What is the importance of following instructions on performing a task?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Sequencing of ideas
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Sequencing of ideas. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) identify connectors in varied texts for effective communication, b) use connectors to sequence ideas in paragraphs for fluency, c) enjoy writing texts using connectors for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work collaboratively to use digital devices to search for various connectors,  list connectors on charts for display,  work jointly with peers to identify connectors (therefore, yet, also, because) in texts,  use connectors to write two paragraphs on the theme,  read the paragraphs on the theme in class for peer review,  prepare sentence strips on the theme collaboratively,  connect sentence strips to form a paragraph using the connectors given. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we use connectors in writing?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Self - expression
chunks.text: STRAND: 4 .1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Self - expression. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) articulate vocabulary related to the theme correctly for communication, b) use nouns to construct sentences accurately for self-expression, c) Appreciate speaking clearly, fluently and efficiently in a conversation for communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  match nouns with their synonyms,  listen to recorded clips on articulation and pronunciation of words and repeat saying them,  record each other as they pronounce words and peer review for correctness,  take turns to select nouns from a word basket and use them to create own sentences,  participate in a debate on a topic related to the theme using sentences containing nouns fluently,  engage in digital language games to identify synonyms of words. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to speak clearly? 2. How do we learn correct pronunciation of words?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.1 Extensive reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.1 Extensive reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read a dialogue on peace building and summarise the main points, b) create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension, c) appreciate reading text on conflict resolution SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  use a dictionary to search for synonyms of word,  use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary and create a word bank,  conduct a reader’s theatre to practice reading dialogues,  work jointly with peers to practice library rules on selection of materials,  identify materials in the library appropriately and read silently to make notes on conflict resolution,  use a digital device to find simple poems based on the theme. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What do you consider when selecting materials from the library?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3.1 creative writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 4.3.1 creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) highlight features of an interesting story, b) write an interesting story based on the theme, c) enjoy writing imaginative stories. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work with peers to highlight features of an interesting story ,  collect interesting stories from their community,  collaboratively hold storytelling sessions,  create a collection of vocabulary items from the stories they have read,  work together to write an interesting story based on the theme,  search for interesting pictures relevant to the theme from print and non-print sources,  write an interesting story based on the pictures retrieved,  present the written stories in class for peer review,  organize their stories in a class portfolio. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How can we make stories interesting in writing?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1.1 Expressing self creatively
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 5.1.1 Expressing self creatively. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify creative language elements in narratives for comprehension, b) use creative language in narration for self- expression, c) appreciate the use of creative language conversation for effective communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  use adjectives to describe events and experiences with peers,  watch recorded clips of narratives and riddles and identify creative expressions,  listen to each other telling stories and pick out creative language elements such as proverbs, sayings and idioms,  participate in a riddle game,  discuss and role play events at market places,  make own narrative using creative language to describe events and experiences,  say meaning of commonly used proverbs, sayings and idioms,  make display charts containing proverbs and sayings. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we use language creatively? 2. What is the importance of creative language?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2.1 Reading for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 5.2.1 Reading for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read a text based on the theme fluently for comprehension, b) Interpret information from news and adverts for understanding, c) Enjoy reading texts on a variety of subjects at appropriate speed. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  describe products based on their colour, size, shape and origin (adjectives),  with peers, read texts on advertisement in the market,  connecting ideas in passages to improve reading speed,  read texts fluently observing punctuation marks for correct interpretation,  read articles from digital devices and answer comprehension questions,  practice identifying the sequence of ideas in paragraphs as they KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are adverts important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3.1: Functional writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 5.3.1: Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) highlight the format of a shopping list, b) write a shopping list for life-long SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work collaboratively to search for varied samples of shopping lists from print and non-print sources,  write down the components of a shopping list,  describe things to be bought using aspects such as colour, amount, material, shape, size (adjectives) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why is a shopping list important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1.1 Listening for information
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 6.1.1 Listening for information. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify special and vulnerable groups from a listening comprehension for information, b) use vocabulary based on the theme in conversations for communication, c) appreciate vocabulary acquisition in language development. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to a listening comprehension from the teacher and identify vocabulary related to the theme,  read words aloud and identify verbs,  view pictures in books and identify vocabulary,  mimic and say vocabulary in cards accurately with peers,  collaborate with peers to discuss the meaning of vocabulary,  create sentences using vocabulary and read them aloud,  search for vocabulary related to the theme online and create vocabulary charts,  narrate stories containing vocabulary related to the theme with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we get meaning of words? 2. What is the importance of vocabulary in communication?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2.1Reading fluency
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 6.2.1Reading fluency. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub- strand, the learner should be able to: a) predict events in a text bases on the theme for comprehension, b) skim and scan texts based on the theme for general information, c) appreciate skimming and SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  observe pictures and identify action words(verbs),  Predict texts based on the title or picture clues,  practice skimming and scanning texts for specific details collaboratively,  practice reading texts clearly and fluently and give peer reviews,  read texts and answer comprehension questions,  brain storm skimming and scanning strategies with peers,  use digital devices to find information on KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why do we skim and scan text?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 6.3.1 Creative writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 6.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify idioms commonly used in the locality for SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  mention idioms commonly used in the locality with peers  listen to an audio recording on a creative story, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why are idioms important?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1.1Making opinions and judgements
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 7.1.1Making opinions and judgements. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify interjections accurately in a conversation for comprehension, b) apply turn taking and interrupting politely in a conversation, c) advocate for good interrupting and turn taking skills in conversations. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  view and watch recorded clips and identify components of a conversation,  role play using introductory and closing phrases in a conversation with peers,  pick out interjections in an oral conversation in class,  participate in a dialogue about the theme while using interjection and turn taking skills,  compose and sing a song about talents,  discuss about the theme while applying appropriate skills for a conversation collaboratively, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do you respond or ask questions during conversations? 2. Why is it important to take turns and interject appropriately in conversations?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 7.2.1Reading comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 7.2.1Reading comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read stories fluently and with expression for comprehension, b) answer comprehension question based on the theme, c) enjoy reading texts for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  read short stories on animals and answer comprehension questions,  read poems and identify the message  discuss characters and themes in stories collaboratively,  read and discuss the moral lessons in the short stories  pick out interjections from simple texts,  role play different characters in stories with peers,  use dictionary to search for meaning of vocabulary. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How do we identify characters in a story? 2. What moral lesson can we learn from a story?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3.1 Creative writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 7.3.1 Creative writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the Sub strand the learner should be able to: a) highlight features of a poem, b) write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication, c) appreciate written poetry for self- expression. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to audio recording on simple poems,  identify features of a poem from the audio recording,  compose and write simple poems based on the theme using a neat and legible handwriting,  recite the poems fluently and do a peer review collaboratively,  record their poem recitations using digital devices,  write a paragraph of a story and punctuate appropriately. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why write legibly and neatly?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 8.1.1 Expressing personal opinions
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 8.1.1 Expressing personal opinions. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) speak clearly and audibly on a topic to express personal opinions effectively, b) apply audience awareness skills in public speaking, c) appreciate public speaking skills for self-expression. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  organise ideas on a topic and present audibly and in good sound projection,  discuss with peers audience awareness skills for presentations,  use words and their opposites in sentences correctly,  record themselves performing speeches and share in class,  take part in a public speaking competition on a topic,  imitate public speeches and presentations clearly and accurately,  watch popular public speeches on care for digital devices and discuss with peers. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What do we consider when speaking in public? 2. Why is it important to speak clearly and audibly? 3. How do we express personal opinions clearly

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 8.2.1 Extensive Reading
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 8.2.1 Extensive Reading. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the characters in the narrative for comprehension, b) retell the flow of the events in the story for expression, c) appreciate the moral lesson from stories for lifelong learning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  collect a variety of narratives in the community,  read level readers individually and make notes or summaries,  read texts based on the theme and identify vocabulary,  find meaning of vocabulary from context,  use dictionary to confirm meaning of vocabulary from texts,  respond to comprehension questions from level readers,  discuss lessons learnt from level readers,  visit a library to select a material for individual reading. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What should you consider when reading silently? 2. How do you keep a record of learnt vocabulary?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 8.3.1 Functional writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 8.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 8.3.1 Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the components of a friendly letter for comprehension, b) write a friendly letter based on the theme for expression, c) Enjoy writing friendly letters for communication. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  work collaboratively to collect samples of friendly letters from print and non- print sources,  identify components of a friendly letter,  discuss with peers the various components of sample friendly letters,  compose a friendly letter and type in a digital device,  proofread their friendly letters and make corrections,  read and share friendly letters through social medial and emails. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why write friendly letters?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 9.1.1 Language strategies on daily experiences
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.1 LISTENING AND SPEAKING. SUB-STRAND: 9.1.1 Language strategies on daily experiences. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe national events fluently and with expression, b) compose songs based on patriotism for expression, c) value the place of national days in promoting ethnic cohesion. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to recorded events on national days,  work collaboratively to build a vocabulary bank on words based on national days,  describe the events fluently, with accuracy and with expression (adverbs),  listen to each other describing events and identify adverbs used,  work collaboratively to compose patriotic songs for a national day,  perform the patriotism songs during an interclass festival. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why do we celebrate national days? 2. How can we describe an event interestingly?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.2 READING. SUB-STRAND: 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) read a story based on the theme for comprehension, b) make predictions on the events of the story, c) answer comprehension questions correctly, d) enjoy reading texts for comprehension. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  select a reading material based on the theme,  predict and preview text based on the theme,  read simple passages on national days and answer questions collaboratively,  elicit topical words from passages on national days and infer the meaning from context,  discuss events in the stories read with peers,  use digital devices to find texts for reading and make notes. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why make predictions in stories?

chunks.subject: Indigenous Language
chunks.sub_strand: 9.3.1 Functional writing
chunks.text: STRAND: 9.3 WRITING. SUB-STRAND: 9.3.1 Functional writing. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub stand, the learner should be able to: a) identify components of a recipe for information, b) write a recipe of their favourite food for instruction, c) enjoy writing recipes of various foods for information. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  make a list of adverbs based on the theme,  role play various adverbs based on the theme with peers,  identify adverbs and write them on flashcards,  discus different components of recipes with peers,  collaborate to write a recipe on a common cultural food from their community,  share their recipes with other groups in class,  pin the recipes on the classroom gallery for a gallery walk, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: How do you write clear instructions?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1 Selected Surah: - Al-Kauthar - Al-Maun - Al-Quraysh - Al-Fil
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.0 QUR’AN. SUB-STRAND: 1.1 Selected Surah: - Al-Kauthar - Al-Maun - Al-Quraysh - Al-Fil (16 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read and memorise the selected surahs for spiritual nourishment, b) outline the basic meaning of the selected surahs, c) deduce lessons from the selected surah , d) appreciate the Qur’an as the first source of guidance. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen to the teacher/resource person/digital device on the recitation of the selected surah,  recite the selected surahs after the teacher/peer/or the digital devices,  read the selected surahs from a digital device/mus- haf/charts,  practice pronunciation through listening to digital devices,  recite the selected surahs severally to enhance memorization,  listen to the basic meaning of the selected surahs from digital devices and make anecdotal notes,  discuss the different ways of applying the teachings and lessons learnt from the selected surahs. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to recite the Qur’an? 2. What lessons do we learn from the selected surah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to read, memorise and give basic meaning of the verses of the selected Surah
chunks.sub_strand: Learner correctly recites, memorises and explains the meaning of all the verses of the selected Surah and put in practice

SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner correctly recites, memorises and explains the meaning of some verses of the selected Surah. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner correctly recites, memorises and explains the meaning of a few verses of the selected Surah.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to deduce lessons from the selected Surah
chunks.sub_strand: Learner explains lessons from the verses of all the selected Surah and applies them in life
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to deduce lessons from the selected Surah. SUB-STRAND: Learner explains lessons from the verses of all the selected Surah and applies them in life. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner explains lessons from the verses of all the selected Surah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner explains lessons from some verses of the selected Surah KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner can explain lessons from a few verses of some selected Surah.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1 Hadith on good Behaviour ( 3 Lessons )
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.1 Hadith on good Behaviour ( 3 Lessons ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify examples of good behaviour from the selected Hadith for character building, b) discuss the significance of the selected Hadith in shaping the character of a Muslim, c) appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by applying them in day to day life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: Read the following Hadith on good behaviour:  read from chart/digital devices the Hadith on good behaviour:  “Fear Allah wherever you are and follow up a bad deed with a good deed, it will wipe it out. And behave well towards other people.” (Al-Tirmidhi).  identify good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith and present in plenary ,  discuss the teachings and relevance of the Hadith in their daily life,  role play acts showing good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should one behave well? 2. What actions show that you fear Allah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2 Hadith on Greetings
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.2 Hadith on Greetings (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the importance of Islamic greetings in the life of a Muslim, b) practise Islamic greetings to promote love and unity in the society, c) appreciate the use of Islamic greetings in bringing harmony in the society. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to: read the following Hadith on greetings: “…. Shall I inform you of something which, if you do, you will love one another? Promote greetings (salaam) amongst yourselves.” (Muslim)  Watch/listen to Islamic greetings from digital devices,  demonstrate Islamic greetings in pairs,  discuss the importance of Islamic greetings in the life of a Muslim and make summary notes,  search online and sing Qasida on Islamic greetings,  practise Islamic greetings to promote love and unity as learners come to class/school. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should a Muslim use Islamic greetings?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3 Hadith on Knowledge
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.3 Hadith on Knowledge (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) read the Hadith as a source of reference in seeking knowledge, b) explain the importance of seeking knowledge for the benefit of this world and the Hereafter, c) appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by working hard in school. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  Read from a chart/digital devices the Hadith on knowledge:  “Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim.” (Al- Tirmidhi).  Search online the importance of seeking knowledge and present it in class,  discuss ways of improving academic performance in school,  role play acts on the importance of seeking knowledge in the Muslim society. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is it important to seek knowledge in Islam? 2. What challenges may hinder one from acquiring education?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4 Hadith on Responsible living
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.0 Hadith. SUB-STRAND: 2.4 Hadith on Responsible living (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline five issues that mankind should account for according to the Hadith, b) describe the lessons learnt from the Hadith , c) appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by living responsibly. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners are guided to:  Read from a chart/digital device the Hadith on responsible living: “The son of Adam will not be dismissed from Allah on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five issues: his life and how he lived it, his youth and how he used it, his wealth and how he earned and spent it, and how he acted on his knowledge.” (Al-Tirmithi)  outline the five issues that mankind must account for on the Day of Resurrection,  describe the lessons learnt from the Hadith and do class resentations,  dramatize ways of living responsibly,  role play ways of earning lawful income and spending. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can the youth live responsibly? 2. How can knowledge be used to benefit others?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to read and explain the teachings of the Hadith
chunks.sub_strand: Learner correctly reads and explains the teachings of the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and assists other learners in reading the Hadith
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to read and explain the teachings of the Hadith. SUB-STRAND: Learner correctly reads and explains the teachings of the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and assists other learners in reading the Hadith. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner correctly reads and explains the teachings of all the selected Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner correctly reads and explains the teachings of some selected Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner correctly reads and explains the teachings of a few selected Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W).

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to deduce lessons from the Hadith and apply the Hadith in daily life
chunks.sub_strand: Learner deduces lessons from all the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and applies their teachings in daily life as well as encouraging others to do the same
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to deduce lessons from the Hadith and apply the Hadith in daily life. SUB-STRAND: Learner deduces lessons from all the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and applies their teachings in daily life as well as encouraging others to do the same. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner deduces lessons from all the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and applies their teachings in daily life SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner deduces lessons from some of the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and applies their teachings in daily life. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner deduces lessons from a few of the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W) and applies their teachings in daily life.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1 Belief in Allah 3.1.1 Attributes of Allah: - Al- Ghaffaar (The Forgiver) - Al-Alim (The All Knowing) - Al-Hafeedh (The Protector) - Al-Hakam (The Judge) - Al-Hayu (The Ever Living) - Al-Waahid (The One) (6 Lessons )
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.1 Belief in Allah 3.1.1 Attributes of Allah: - Al- Ghaffaar (The Forgiver) - Al-Alim (The All Knowing) - Al-Hafeedh (The Protector) - Al-Hakam (The Judge) - Al-Hayu (The Ever Living) - Al-Waahid (The One) (6 Lessons ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the attributes of Allah and their corresponding meaning, b) explain the importance of the attributes of Allah, c) use the attributes of Allah while making dua (supplication), d) appreciate the unique attributes of Allah as part of Islamic faith. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner guided to:  listen to the recitation of the attributes of Allah from a digital device,  match the attributes of Allah with corresponding meaning using flash cards,  discuss the importance of the attributes of Allah and make notes,  use the attributes of Allah while making dua,  sing qasida on the attributes of Allah,  match the Atributes with meaning using flash cards. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What lessons are learnt from the attributes of Allah? 2. Why should one use the attributes of Allah while making dua (supplications)?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2 Belief in angels 3.2.1 Characteristics of angels (3 Lessons )
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.2 Belief in angels 3.2.1 Characteristics of angels (3 Lessons ). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the characteristics of angels to strengthen their iman, b) explain the significance of the belief in angels in the life of a Muslim, c) obey Allah’s commands by emulating angels, d) differentiate between angels and human beings to appreciate Allah’s creation, e) appreciate the belief in angels as a pillar of iman. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search for information on the characteristics of angels from digital devices/books/resource persons and present in class,  brainstorm on the significance of belief in angels and make notes,  role play different situations that depict obedience to Allah’s commands (obeying parents, teachers, elders, school rules),  read a verse from the Qur’an on the obedience of angels on Allah’s commands (Q66: 6). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is the significance of believing in angels? 2. How can Muslims show obedience to Allah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3 Belief in Prophets 3.3.1 Qualities of Prophets
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.3 Belief in Prophets 3.3.1 Qualities of Prophets (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the qualities of Prophets for character formation, b) apply values learnt from the qualities of Prophets in their daily lives, c) appreciate belief in Allah’s Prophets by emulating the qualities of Prophets. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search for information on the qualities of Prophets from digital, devices/books/resource persons and display in class,  narrate a story of any Prophet that shows these qualities,  role play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the Prophets e.g.(honesty, obedience ,patience),  discuss how the qualities of the Prophets learnt can be applied in school situation. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can qualities of the Prophets be applied in daily life? 2. Why are Prophets regarded as role models?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.2 Miracles of Prophets - Nuh (A.S) - Musa (A.S) - Issa (A.S.)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.0 Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.2 Miracles of Prophets - Nuh (A.S) - Musa (A.S) - Issa (A.S.) (6 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the miracles perfomed by the selected Prophets to strengthen their iman (faith), b) discuss lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected Prophets, c) appreciate the miracles of the selected Prophets to build their reliance on Allah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch/listen to stories of the miracles of the selected Prophets from digital devices and make notes.  deduce lessons from the miracles of the selected Prophets and present in class,  Match the name of the Prophets with miracles performed using flash cards,  draw, colour and display items related to the miracles of the selected Prophet. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What is a miracle? 2. Why did Prophets perform miracles?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to outline attributes of Allah with their corresponding meaning
chunks.sub_strand: Learner outlines all the six attributes of Allah with their corresponding meaning with ease
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to outline attributes of Allah with their corresponding meaning. SUB-STRAND: Learner outlines all the six attributes of Allah with their corresponding meaning with ease. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner outlines all the six attributes of Allah with their corresponding meaning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner outlines five attributes of Allah with their corresponding meaning. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner outlines less than less than three attributes of Allah and struggles to give their corresponding meaning.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to mention the pillars of Iman, explain significance of the belief in the specific pillars
chunks.sub_strand: Learner mentions all the six pillars of Iman and explains the significance of belief in the pillars ease
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to mention the pillars of Iman, explain significance of the belief in the specific pillars. SUB-STRAND: Learner mentions all the six pillars of Iman and explains the significance of belief in the pillars ease. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner mentions all the six pillars of Iman and explains the significance of belief in the pillars. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner mentions all the pillars of Iman and explains the significance of belief in five of the pillars. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner mentions some pillars of Iman and does not explain the significance of belief in the pillars.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2 Sunnah (Optional) Prayers: 4.2.1 Qabliyah and Ba'diyah ( 3 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.2 Sunnah (Optional) Prayers: 4.2.1 Qabliyah and Ba'diyah ( 3 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the significance of performing sunnah prayers in the life of a Muslim, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss sunnah prayers performed before and after fardh prayers and display in class using charts, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Why should a Muslim perform Qabliya and ba’diyah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.2.2 Taraweh and Witr
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.2.2 Taraweh and Witr (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the significance of performing Taraweh and witr prayers in the life of a Muslim, b) Perform swalatul Taraweh and Witr for spiritual nourishment, c) Appreciate the performance of Taraweh and witr prayers to earn thawab, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video on the performance of swalatul Taraweh and witr through digital devices and discuss the procedure of performing the prayer,  Demonstrate/role play swalatul Taraweh and witr in class,  discuss the importance of performing swalatul Taraweh and witr and present in class, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the significance of praying swalatul Taraweh and witr?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.3 Swadaqah (Charity)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.3 Swadaqah (Charity) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify forms of swadaqah for character development, b) demontrate different acts of swadaqah to earn rewards, c) explain the benefits of practising acts of swadaqah in the society, d) appreciate the different forms of swadaqah in their daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class  discuss the different forms of swadaqah in pairs/group as per the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w) (e.g. feeding an animal, removing an obstacle from the path, sharing with others etc.),  participate in charitable activities (clean up exercise, visit to children’s home, tree planting…),  discuss the benefits of giving charity in pairs/group and do class presentation. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What acts of swadaqah do Muslims perform? 2. What are the benefits of practising swadaqah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 4.4.3 Nullifiers of Saum (fasting)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.0 Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: 4.4.3 Nullifiers of Saum (fasting) (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum, b) practce suam as pillar of Islam , c) appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss in pairs/group the nullifiers of saum and make oral presentation in class,  sort nullifiers of saum from of conditions on flash cards, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should Muslims observe rules and regulation when fasting? 2. What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to perform of acts of Ibadah
chunks.sub_strand: Learner routinely, appropriately and promptly performs acts of Ibada
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to perform of acts of Ibadah. SUB-STRAND: Learner routinely, appropriately and promptly performs acts of Ibada. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner regularly, appropriately and promptly performs the acts of Ibada. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner regularly, and promptly performs acts of Ibada with some inconsistencies in the performance. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner performs acts of Ibada without observing promptness and appropriateness.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.1 Virtues 5.1.1 Sabr (Patience) ( 2 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.1 Virtues 5.1.1 Sabr (Patience) ( 2 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the importance of exhibiting patience in their daily life, b) practise patience as a virtue for character formation, c) appreciate the virtue of patience as a means of earning rewards from Allah. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learners is guided to:  narrate short stories portraying patience,  watch/listen to a story on patience and deduce the teachings,  discuss in pairs/group the importance of observing patience,  participate in activities that involve practising patience e.g.turn taking during games, when queueing  role play activities that encourage/show patience. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why should a Muslim observe patience? 2. When should a Muslim practise patience?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.2 Effects of Social Media ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.2 Effects of Social Media ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the positive and negative effects of social media on the youth SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  debate on the positive and negative effects of social media KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How can one use social media positively? 2. How can social media enhance learning?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.3 Prohibitions in Islam (Vices) 5.3.1 Evils of Gambling ( 2 lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.3 Prohibitions in Islam (Vices) 5.3.1 Evils of Gambling ( 2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the evils of gambling to promote responsible citizenship, b) state ways of discouraging gambling in the society, c) appreciate the prohibition of gambling by working hard for halaal (legal) earning. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  discuss in pairs/group the effects of gambling and present in class (loss of property, family break down),  role play the effects of gambling,  brainstorm on ways of discouraging gambling in the society and display on a chart . KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. What are the effects of participating in gambling? 2. Why is gambling forbidden in Islam?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 5.4 Dua (Supplications) 5.4.1 Dua On Increase In Knowledge ( 3 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Values). SUB-STRAND: 5.4 Dua (Supplications) 5.4.1 Dua On Increase In Knowledge ( 3 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) memorise the selecteddua as a form of ibadah, b) apply the dua (supplication ) in day to day life, c) explain the importance of the dua to a person seeking knowledge, d) appreciate the act of supplication as a form of Ibadah (act of worship). SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen and recite the following dua from a digital device/teacher,  “Oh Allah make what you teach me beneficial, teach me what is beneficial, and increase me in knowledge.”  recite the dua every morning before start of class,  brainstorm on the importance of making dua and write notes. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What is the importance of making dua always?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to apply moral values in day today life
chunks.sub_strand: Learner demonstrates acquisition of Islamic values and shows In-depth understanding of how moral values are applied in daily life
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to apply moral values in day today life. SUB-STRAND: Learner demonstrates acquisition of Islamic values and shows In-depth understanding of how moral values are applied in daily life. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner demonstrates acquisition of Islamic values and applies moral values in daily life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner demonstrates acquisition of Islamic values and requires guidance in applying moral values in daily life. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner demonstrates acquisition of Islamic values and does not apply moral values in daily life.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.1 Etiquette of Islamic Wedding Celebrations
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 Muamalat (Social Relations). SUB-STRAND: 6.1 Etiquette of Islamic Wedding Celebrations (2 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the etiquette to be observed during Islamic wedding celebrations, b) outline unislamic activities that take place during wedding celebrations, c) appreciate Islamic wedding celebrations as part of Islamic heritage. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  brainstorm on a wedding celebration they have attended and note down what they observed/experienced,  watch an Islamic wedding celebration from a digital device and the etiquette observed,  sort the Islamic and unislamic activities performed during wedding celebrations using flash cards,  role play the etiquette to be observed during the celebration e.g. (appropriate dressing, gender separation, avoiding Israaf and music) KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: What are the Islamic etiquette that guides wedding celebrations?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 6.2 Rights of Neighbours ( 2 Lessons)
chunks.text: STRAND: 6.0 Muamalat (Social Relations). SUB-STRAND: 6.2 Rights of Neighbours ( 2 Lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the rights of neighbours for harmonious living, b) demonstrate the awareness of the rights of neighbours as an act of ibadah, c) appreciate the rights of neighbours as an obligatory act upon a Muslim. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  search the rights of neighbours in Islam using digital devices/print media and make notes,  Discuss in pairs/group the significance of treating neighbours well and display on a chart,  dramatize the right way of treating neighbours,  search for Hadith on the rights of neighbours and deduce lessons from it using digital devices/ books/resource persons. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. How should Muslims relate with neighbours? 2. What are the significance of upholding good neighbourhood?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to demonstrate awareness of different relationships and application of Islamic teachings in interactions with others
chunks.sub_strand: Effectively and correctly demonstrates an awareness of different relationships and interactions and accurately applies the teachings of Islam in his/her interactions with others to promote harmonious relationships
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to demonstrate awareness of different relationships and application of Islamic teachings in interactions with others. SUB-STRAND: Effectively and correctly demonstrates an awareness of different relationships and interactions and accurately applies the teachings of Islam in his/her interactions with others to promote harmonious relationships. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Correctly demonstrate an awareness of different relationships and interactions and applies the teachings of Islam in his/her interactions with others to promote harmonious relationships. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Has some understanding on the different relationships and interactions and attempts to apply the teachings of Islam in his/her interactions with others to promote harmonious relationships. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Has some understanding on the different relationships and interactions and fails to apply the teachings of Islam in his/her interactions with others to promote harmonious relationships.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.1 Pledges of Aqabah (Events that Led,Terms of Aqabah)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: 7.1 Pledges of Aqabah (Events that Led,Terms of Aqabah) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) state the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah b) identify the terms of the pledges of Aqabah c) appreciate the pledges of Aqabah as a base for the migration of muslims in madina SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  watch a video on the pledges of Aqaba from a digital device and write the terms  discuss in group the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah  role play and present in class (e.g the Prophet (S.A.W) meeting delegates from Yathrib, preaching by Mus’ab bin Umayr in Madina, signing the pledges…) . KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why is the pledges of Aqabah important in the History of Islam? 2. How did Muslims benefit from the pledges of Aqabah?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.3 Hijra to Madina
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: 7.3 Hijra to Madina (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) narrate the events on the Prophet’s migration to Madina, b) assess the significance of the Prophet (S.S.W)’s journey to Madina, c) appreciate the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s journey to Madina as milestone in islamic History. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  listen/watch a story on the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s migration to Madina from a digital device/teacher,  in group braistorm reasons for Prophets migration to Madina,  discuss the major events that took place during the Prophet (S.A.W.)’s migration to Madina e.g.(the Prophet (S.A.W) leaving Ali in his house ,departure with Abubakar, at cave Thaur, the incident of Suraqah,reception in Madina),  sing a Qasida of welcoming the Prophet (S.A.W) i.e Talaal Badru ‘alaynaa),  discuss the significance of Hijra and make short note e.g. end of persecution, unity of the Ummah, beginning of the Islamic calendar). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Why did the Prophet (S.A.W.) migrate to Madina? 2. Why is Hijra important to Muslims?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: 7.4 Constitution of Madina ( Terms of Madina Constitution)
chunks.text: STRAND: 7.0 History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: 7.4 Constitution of Madina ( Terms of Madina Constitution) (3 lessons). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline the terms of Madina constitution, b) explain the importance of Madina constitution to the people of Madina, c) explain the role played by the Ansar in the settlement of Muhajirun in Madina, d) develop a desire to maintain Islamic brotherhood as per the teachings of Islam. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The learner is guided to:  brainstorm on the terms of Madina constitution ,  discuss in pairs/group the importance of Madina constituition to the people of Madina,  listen/watch a story on how united the Muhajirun and the Ansar were from a digital device/teacher,  discuss the role played by the Ansar in settling the Muhajirun (e.g. shared their wealth assisted them in integration and settlement),  discuss the lessons learnt from the spirit of brotherhood established by the Prophet (S.A.W) (Muslims must be united, assist one another). KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. why the was Madina constituition importance to the people of Madina? 2. What role did the Ansar play in the settlement of the Muhajirun?

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.strand: Ability to narrate events in Islamic History and applying lessons from Islamic Historical events in life
chunks.sub_strand: Learner narrates all the events in Islamic History and Applies lessons from Islamic historical events in life with a clear sequence
chunks.text: STRAND: Ability to narrate events in Islamic History and applying lessons from Islamic Historical events in life. SUB-STRAND: Learner narrates all the events in Islamic History and Applies lessons from Islamic historical events in life with a clear sequence. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Learner narrates all the events in Islamic History and Applies lessons from Islamic historical events in life. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Learner narrates some events in Islamic History and Applies some lessons from Islamic historical events in life. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learner requires assistance in narrating events in Islamic History and has difficulties applying lessons from Islamic historical events in life.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: Selected Surah: - Al-Kauthar - Al-Maun - Al-Quraysh - Al-Fil
chunks.text: STRAND: Qur’an. SUB-STRAND: Selected Surah: - Al-Kauthar - Al-Maun - Al-Quraysh - Al-Fil. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Portfolio, written assessment, oral assessment and observation schedule SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Digital devices, Mus-haf, charts, course books and resource person KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learners recite the selected surah during assembly, Pastoral Programme Instructions (PPI), during prayers and in clubs.

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: Selected Hadith
chunks.text: STRAND: Hadith. SUB-STRAND: Selected Hadith. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: written assessment, oral assessment, observation schedule and portfolio Written assessment oral tests, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Charts & course books, digital devices, resource persons KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Learners learn more Hadith on good behaviour from madrasa/masjid, give a talk on knowledge during assembly

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: Attributes of Allah
chunks.text: STRAND: Pillars of Iman. SUB-STRAND: Attributes of Allah. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Written assessment, oral assessments, portfolio and observation SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: The Qur’an, books on Hadith, course books, digital devices, reference materials/online sources KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Write the attributes of Allah (S.W.T.) on a plaque and sell on Open Days

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: Nullifiers Swalah
chunks.text: STRAND: Devotional Acts. SUB-STRAND: Nullifiers Swalah. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Oral assessment and observation schedule, written assessments SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Charts, course books, resource person, flash cards, digital devices, resource persons, personal logs. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: -Learners perform valid swalah with their peers/schoolmates/school community during prayer time. -Participate in cleaning the compound, sharing things with their schoolmates

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: Etiquette of Islamic wedding
chunks.text: STRAND: Muamalat ( Social relations). SUB-STRAND: Etiquette of Islamic wedding. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Oral questions, observation schedule, written assessment, project work, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Digital devices, realia, shop items. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: -Learners dramatize an Islamic wedding during clubs/games -

chunks.subject: Religious Education (IRE)
chunks.sub_strand: Al- Isra wal miraj
chunks.text: STRAND: History of Islam. SUB-STRAND: Al- Isra wal miraj. SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Oral questions, observation schedule, project SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Story books on the sirah, course books and digital devices, Islamic calendar/charts,map KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: -Learners narrate the story of the Prophet (S.A.W)’s journey to their schoolmates during their free time

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 4)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 1.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 4). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua silabi zinazotokana na sauti zinazokaribiana katika maneno: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh, b) kutamka silabi zinazotokana na sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi: f/v, s/z, l/r na th/dh ili kutofautisha matamshi yake, c) kutamka vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa kutokana na maneno kwenye vitabu, ubaoni au kwa kutumia vifaa vya kiteknolojia,  kusikiliza silabi za sauti f/v, s/z, l/r/ na th/dh zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kiteknolojia (k.v. kinasasauti),  kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa akiwa na wenzake,  kusikiliza vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa kutokana na maneno yenye sauti lengwa vikikaririwa (k.m. shirika la reli la Rwanda larejelea shughuli zake rasmi),  kuunda vitanzandimi vinavyotokana na sauti KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, unajua maneno gani yenye silabi zinazokangany a kimatamshi? 2. Je, unajua vitanzandimi gani vyenye silabi zinazokangany a kimatamshi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 1.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa uliotumika katika kifungu ili kuimarisha ufahamu, b) kutumia msamiati lengwa kwa usahihi katika sentensi, c) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, matukio na wahusika, d) kuonyesha uelewa SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa (k.v. vyakula, viungo vya kupikia, njia za kupika na vifaa vya kupikia) kwa kutumia kadi za maneno, chati, mti maneno au kifaa cha kidijitali,  kushiriki katika vikundi kujadili na kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa katika sentensi,  kusoma kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa kwenye kitabu au kwenye tarakilishi akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi,  kutoa muhtasari kuhusu kifungu alichosoma,  kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu alichosoma, kusoma vifungu mtandaoni kuhusu KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Kusoma kuhusu mapishi kuna umuhimu gani? 2. Ni hadithi gani umewahi kuisoma kuhusu mapishi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.3.1 Insha ya wasifu (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 1.3.1 Insha ya wasifu (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia mtindo na muundo wake, b) kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa ubunifu ili kujenga maelezo yenye kutoa picha dhahiri, c) kufurahia kutunga insha bora ili kuimarisha mazoea ya kuandika. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha zilizoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kusoma vielelezo vya insha ya wasifu vilivyoandikwa katika matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya wasifu,  kukishirikiana na wenzake katika vikundi ili kubainisha na kujadili vidokezo vifaavyo vya mada lengwa,  kuaandika insha ya wasifu isiyopungua maneno 150 inayohusu mada lengwa (k.v. Mpishi nimpendaye) kwa kuzingatia, anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati safi, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Insha ya wasifu inahusu nini? 2. Unazingatia nini unapoandika insha ya wasifu?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.1 Nomino za Pekee (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.1 Nomino za Pekee (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino za pekee kwenye sentensi au vifungu vya maneno, b) kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za pekee ili kukuza matumizi ya lugha sahihi, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya nomino za pekee katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino za pekee (k.v. Kisumu, Mei, Rabuka, Alhamisi na Yohana) kwenye tarakilishi, kapu maneno, mti maneno, kadi maneno au chati,  kutaja nomino za pekee akiwa na wenzake kama vile za majina ya mji, majina ya mito, majina ya watu na majina ya miezi,  kutambua nomino za pekee katika sentensi kwenye vitabu, tarakilishi, chati kwa kuzipigia mstari au kukolezea rangi,  kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi au kifungu kwa kutumia nomino za pekee,  kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za pekee akiwa na wenzake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Nomino za pekee zinahusu nini? 2. Ni nomino zipi za pekee unazozijua?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 1.4.2 Nomino za kawaida (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 1.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 1.4.2 Nomino za kawaida (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino za kawaida kwenye sentensi au vifungu vya maneno, b) kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za kawaida ili kukuza matumizi sahihi ya lugha, c) kufurahia kutumia nomino za kawaida katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino za kawaida kwenye kadi au kapu la maneno (k.v.mtu, mtoto, darasa, ukuta, mwalimu, meza na kiti),  kutaja akiwa na wenzake nomino za kawaida,  kutambua nomino za kawaida katika sentensi kwa kuzipigia mistari au kuzikolezea rangi kwenye tarakilishi,  kutumia nomino za kawaida kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi,  kutunga sentensi kwa kutumia nomino za kawaida akiwa peke yake wawiliwawili au kwenye vikundi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, ni vitu gani vipatikanavyo katika mazingira yako? 2. Ni vitu gani vinavyotumi wa katika mapishi mbalimbali?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.1.1 Maamkuzi na Maagano (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 2.1.1 Maamkuzi na Maagano (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua aina mbalimbali za maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano, b) kueleza maamkuzi na maagano yanayotumik katika miktadha mbalimbali ili kuyabainisha, c) kutumia aina mbalimbali za maamkuzi na maagano katika mawasiliano, d) kuchangamkia maamkuzi na SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua maamkuzi (k.v. shikamoo, Habari za utokako? Habari za adhuhuri? Habari za jioni?) kutoka kwenye chati, ubao au vifaa vya kidijitali, michoro na picha,  kushiriki kujadiliana na mwenzake a au katika vikundi maamkuzi yanayolengwa na matumizi yake,  kutambua maagano (k.v lala salama, safari njema, alamsiki) kutoka kwenye chati, ubao au vifaa vya kidijitali, michoro na picha,  kushirikiana na wenzake kuigiza maamkuzi na maagano lengwa,  ktazama watu wakiamkuana na kuagana katika vifaa vya kidijitali, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, watu husalimiana vipi katika jamii? 2. Je, watu huagana vipi katika jamii?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.2.1 Kusoma kwa Kina (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 2.2.1 Kusoma kwa Kina (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua mpangilio wa maneno katika kamusi ili kupata maneno lengwa kwa urahisi, b) kutumia kamusi ipasavyo kutafuta maana za maneno asiyoyajua yaliyo katika matini teule ili kukuza msamiati wake, c) kuchangamkia kutumia kamusi katika kukuza msamiati wake. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kupanga maneno aliyopewa kwenye chati, kapu maneno au mti maneno kialfabeti,  kuchague neno kutoka kapu maneno au mti maneno ili kulitafuta kwenye kamusi,  kutumia kamusi kutafuta maana za maneno mbalimbali akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi,  kutumia mtandao kutafuta maana za maneno. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Maana ya maneno ya Kiswahili hupatikana wapi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.3.1 Insha ya masimulizi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 2.3.1 Insha ya masimulizi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua insha ya masimulizi kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, mtindo na muundo, b) kuandika insha ya masimulizi kwa kufuata kanuni zifaazo, c) kuchangamkia utunzi mzuri wa insha ya masimulizi ili kukuza ubunifu wake. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua insha ya masimulizi kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha zilizoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,  kushiriki na wenzake kujadili mada ya insha na muundo wa insha ya masimulizi,  kuandika insha isiyopungua maneno 150 inayosimulia kisa cha tukio linalohusiana na huduma ya kwanza kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati safi, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa lugha ya kiubunifu,  kuandika insha ya masimulizi mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili kuisoma na kuitathmini, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unazingatia nini ili kuandika insha nzuri ya masimulizi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4.1 Nomino za Wingi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.1 Nomino za Wingi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze; a) kutambua nomino za wingi katika matini ili kuzibainisha, b) kutumia nomino za wingi katika sentensi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano, c) kufurahia kutumia nomino za wingi katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi  kutambua nomino za wingi (k.m chumvi, sukari, maji, uji, mafuta na manukato) kutoka kwenye kapu la maneno, chati, vitabu na vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika kikundi,  kutambua nomino za wingi kwa kuzipigia mistari au kuzikolezea rangi kwenye matini,  kutumia nomino za wingi kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi,  kutumia nomino za wingi katika sentensi kwa kufanya mazoezi daftarini. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Unajua majina gani yanayohusu vitu vinavyopatikana katika wingi tu?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 2.4.2 Vitenzi-jina (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 2.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 2.4.2 Vitenzi-jina (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze; a) kutambua nomino za vitenzi-jina kwenye kifungu cha maneno au kwenye sentensi, b) kutunga sentensi au vifungu vya maneno akitumia nomino za vitenzi- jina ili kukuza matumizi bora ya lugha, c) kufurahia kutumia nomino za vitenzi- jina katika utungaji wa sentensi na kujaza nafasi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua vitenzi-jina kutoka kwenye kapu la maneno, vyombo vya kijiditali (k.v. kusoma, kucheka, kula, kulia na kuandika.),  kutambua vitenzi-jina akiwa na wenzake kwa kuvipigia mistari au kuzikolezea rangi kwenye matini n.k,  kutumia nomino za vitenzi- jina kwa kujaza nafasi kwenye sentensi,  kutunga sentensi au vifungu vya maneno kwa kutumia nomino za vitenzi-jina akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika vikundi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Ni mambo gani wewe hufanya ukiwa nyumbani? 2. Unapenda kufanya mambo gani darasani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 3.1.1 Matamshi Bora (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua vitendawili vya suala lengwa, b) kutega na kutegua vitendawili ili kujenga matamshi bora, c) kuchangamkia matumizi ya vitendawili kama njia ya kujenga utamkaji bora wa maneno. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua vitendawili vya mapambo katika chati, ubao au vifaa vya kidijitali (k.m Wafaa lakini wavaliwa bila matumizi maalum (Mtandio), Ananitazama, hasemi hasikii (Picha), Lapendeza rangi lakini halidumu (Ua). Dhahabu yangu ya thamani haisimami (Mkufu],  kushiriki katika kutega na kutegua vitendawili ,  kusikiliza vitendawili vikitegwa na kuteguliwa kupitia vyombo vya kidijitali. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, ni vitendawili gani unavyovijua?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.2 Kusoma. SUB-STRAND: 3.2.1 Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua msamiati wa mapambo uliotumiwa katika kifungu, b) kuelezea maana za msamiati mbalimbali wa mapambo, c) kusoma kifungu cha hadithi ili kupata ujumbe, d) kuonyesha uelewa wa hadithi kwa kutoa muhtasari na kujibu maswali, SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua msamiati wa mapambo (k.v vipuli, pete, bangili na ushanga) kwa kutazama picha na vifaa halisi,  kutumia tarakilishi kutafuta msamiati wa mapambo na maana yake mtandaoni,  kueleza mapambo na sehemu yanapovaliwa,  kutunga sentensi akitumia msamiati husika, akiwa peke yake kisha kwenye wawiliwawili au kikundi,  kusoma maneno yasiyopungua( 80) katika hadithi kwa dakika moja kwa usahihi,  kutoa muhtasari wa hadithi aliyoisoma  kujibu maswali kutokana na hadithi. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kwa nini ni muhimu kusoma kuhusu mapambo?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.3.1 Kuandika kwa Tarakilishi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.3 Kuandika. SUB-STRAND: 3.3.1 Kuandika kwa Tarakilishi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua sehemu mbalimbali za tarakilishi zinazotumika kupigia chapa, b) kutumia tarakilishi ili kujenga maarifa ya kidijitali, c) kujenga mazoea ya kutumia tarakilishi kuandika na kuhifadhi maandishi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua sehemu mbalimbali za tarakilishi za kupigia chapa. (k.v. bodidota, kipanya na kiwambo/ mulishi),  kutumia tarakilishi kuandika maneno au sentensi zinazolenga msamiati wa mapambo (k.v. herini, vipuli, pete, kipini, bangili, shanga, taji, kugesi na hina),  kutumia tarakilishi kuandika kifungu kinachohusisha mapambo mbalimbali,  kuhifadhi kazi yake kwenye faili ya tarakilishi mara kwa mara,  kuhariri kazi yake kwenye tarakilishi akishirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi, KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, ni sehemu zipi za tarakilishi unazojua 2. Tarakilishi hutuwezesha kufanya kazi gani?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.4.1 Nomino za Makundi (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 3.4.1 Nomino za Makundi (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino za makundi katika sentensi ili kuzibainisha, b) kueleza nomino za makundi ili kuzitofautish a na nomino zingine, c) kutumia nomino za makundi kwa usahihi katika sentensi, d) kuonea fahari SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino za makundi (k. v mlolongo wa magari, tita la kuni, mkungu wa ndizi, safu ya siafu, koja la maua, bunda la noti) katika chati, kadi maneno, ubao, vifaa vya kidijitali n.k.,  kujadili katika kikundi au wawiliwawili maana ya nomino za makundi huko akitoa mifano,  kutumia nomino za makundi katika sentensi na kuziandika daftarini mwake,  kutumia nomino za makundi kutunga sentensi mtandaoni akiwa na wenzake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: 1. Je, unajua maneno gani yanayotaja makundi ya watu na vitu? 2. Je, nomino za makundi hutumiwa vipi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.4.2 Nomino Ambata (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 3.4.2 Nomino Ambata (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino ambata katika matini ili kuzitofautisha na aina nyingine za nomino, b) kutumia nomino ambata kwa usahihi katika sentensi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano, c) kuonea fahari matumizi ya nomino ambata katika mawasiliano. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino ambata (k.v askarikanzu, mbwamwitu, mwanasiasa na mwananchi) kwa kutumia kadi maneno, kapu maneno, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali akiwa peke yake, wawiliwawili au katika kikundi,  kujadili katika kikundi au wawiliwawili maana ya nomino ambata huko akitoa mifano,  kutumia nomino ambata katika sentensi na kuziandika katika daftari lake,  kutumia nomino ambata kutunga sentensi mtandaoni akishirikiana na wenzake,  kusakura mtandaoni ili kupata mifano zaidi ya nomino ambata na kuziandika katika daftari lake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unajua maneno yapi yanayounganishwa kuunda neno moja?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.4.3 Nomino za dhahania (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 3.4.3 Nomino za dhahania (Vipindi 2). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua nomino za dhahania katika matini mbalimbali, b) kuelezea nomino za dhahania kwa kutoa mifano mwafaka, c) kutumia nomino za dhahania kwa usahihi katika sentensi, d) kuonea fahari matumizi ya SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua nomino za dhahania (k.v upendo, uhodari, ukweli) kwa kutumia kadi maneno, mti maneno, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali,  kujadili katika kikundi au wawiliwawili maana ya nomino za dhahania huko akitoa mifano,  kutumia nomino za dhahania katika sentensi na kuziandika sentensi hizo daftarini mwake,  kutumia nomino za dhahania kutunga sentensi mtandaoni akishirikiana na wenzake. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Je, unajua maneno yapi yanayotaja vitu ambavyo haviwezi kushikwa au kuonekana kwa macho?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 3.4.4 Uakifishi Vipindi 4)
chunks.text: STRAND: 3.4 Sarufi. SUB-STRAND: 3.4.4 Uakifishi Vipindi 4). SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: Kufikia mwisho wa mada ndogo, mwanafunzi aweze: a) kutambua herufi kubwa, alama ya koma, kikomo na kiulizi katika maandishi, b) kutumia herufi kubwa, koma, kikomo na kiulizi ifaavyo katika maaandishi, c) kufurahia matumizi ya herufi kubwa, koma, kikomo na kiulizi katika maandishi. SUGGESTED LEARNING EXPERIENCES: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:  kutambua herufi kubwa, koma, kikomo na kiulizi katika maandishi,  kushiriki katika vikundi kuakifisha sentensi akitumia herufi kubwa, koma, kikomo na kiulizi (baadhi ya sentensi ziangazie suala lengwa),  kuandika sentensi akitumia herufi kubwa, koma, kikomo na kiulizi ifaavyo,  kuandika sentensi zenye herufi kubwa, koma, kikomo na kiulizi akitumia kifaa cha kidijitali. KEY INQUIRY QUESTION: Kwa nini alama za kuakifisha hutumiwa katika maandishi?

chunks.subject: Kiswahili
chunks.sub_strand: 4.1.1 Heshima, adabu na vyeo (Vipindi 2)
chunks.text: STRAND: 4.1 Kusikiliza na Kuzungumza. SUB-STRAND: 4.1.1 Heshima, adabu na vyeo (Vipindi 2).
